payload.passage: The zoo had a special place just for baby animals. There was a tiny deer, a small bear cub, and a fluffy duckling. A helper fed them milk from a bottle. Everyone said the baby animals were the cutest part of the whole zoo.
payload.title: The Baby Animal Corner
decoys: There was a small bear cub.

payload.passage: The puppy near the school had a thorn stuck in its paw. It limped and whined in pain. A gentle girl pulled out the thorn with care. The puppy licked her hand and walked happily.
payload.title: A girl removes the puppy's thorn

payload.passage: Meera wrote her very own short story at home. She filled the pages with a brave little mouse. She drew bright pictures for each part of the tale. Proudly, she shared her handmade book in the library.
payload.title: Meera shares her handmade story book
decoys: Her story had a brave mouse.

payload.passage: Renu joined the collage competition at the art fair. She tore coloured paper to make a big sunny garden. She layered the petals so the flowers looked real. The judges loved her bright garden and gave her first prize.
payload.title: Renu's Garden Collage Wins

payload.passage: Sunita stayed with her grandmother who loved to paint pots. They covered clay pots with bright flowers and dots. Granny taught Sunita how to hold the thin brush. Sunita was proud of the cheerful pot she painted.
payload.title: Sunita Paints Pots With Granny

payload.passage: Tarun went to his grandparents' home near the hills. Each evening they watched the sun sink behind the peaks. The sky turned pink, orange, and finally deep grey. Tarun loved the lovely sunsets from granny's terrace.
payload.title: Sunsets From Granny's Terrace

payload.passage: Sneha noticed the library books were getting dusty. She asked her friends to help clean the shelves. They wiped each book and put it back in order. The fresh, clean library felt welcoming again.
payload.title: Sneha and friends clean the library shelves
decoys: They put books back in order.

payload.passage: Jiya wanted to make a healthy snack after school. She mixed nuts, raisins, and crunchy cereal in a bowl. She filled a small box to share with her friends. The tasty snack mix gave them energy to play outside.
payload.title: Jiya makes a healthy snack mix
decoys: She mixed nuts and raisins together.
She shared it with her friends.

payload.passage: Tara visited the reptile pond and saw a huge crocodile. It floated very still with only its eyes above the water. Then suddenly it snapped its long jaws shut. Tara jumped back, surprised at how fast the big crocodile moved.
payload.title: The Big Crocodile at the Zoo

payload.passage: Nisha could not decide which book to borrow. The librarian asked her what she liked best. When Nisha said she loved horses, the librarian found a perfect book. Nisha left the library smiling with the horse story.
payload.title: The librarian helps Nisha pick a book

payload.passage: Meera loves making music with simple things at home. She taps spoons, shakes a rice tin, and claps a beat. She mixes the sounds into her own little tune. Meera finds that music can be made from almost anything.
payload.title: Meera Makes Music at Home

payload.passage: Anjali saw a giant model of a ship at the museum. It had tall masts and many tiny sails. A guide said real ships like this once sailed across the sea. Anjali imagined sailors steering it through big waves.
payload.title: The Big Ship Model at the Museum

payload.passage: Our group made a model of the water cycle for the project. We showed the sun, the clouds, and the falling rain. We drew arrows to show how water moves around. Our teacher said the model explained the cycle well.
payload.title: A Model of the Water Cycle
decoys: We showed the sun and clouds.

payload.passage: Anil stayed with his grandfather, who painted pictures. The walls were covered with scenes of fields and rivers. Grandfather let Anil hold the brush and try a few strokes. Anil loved watching his grandfather paint the world.
payload.title: Grandfather Paints the World

payload.passage: The children gathered in the lane to play hide and seek. Govind was chosen to be the seeker first. He counted to twenty with his eyes shut tight. Then he ran and found everyone one by one.
payload.title: Govind plays hide and seek
decoys: Outdoor games are full of fun

payload.passage: Our class made a model of a busy beehive for the fair. We built yellow cells and added tiny paper bees. We showed how the bees store sweet golden honey. Visitors learned how busy a real beehive can be.
payload.title: A Class Model of a Beehive

payload.passage: Anaya saw a hall full of beautiful old pots at the museum. The clay pots were painted with fine patterns. Some were tiny and some were taller than her. A board said people used them to store grain and water.
payload.title: Old Painted Pots at the Museum

payload.passage: Ishaan counted the tunnels as the train wound through the hills. Inside each dark tunnel the children squealed with delight. When light burst back in, they cheered every time. The hilly ride was full of little surprises.
payload.title: Ishaan counts the tunnels on the hill train
decoys: The children squealed in the dark.

payload.passage: Priya could not choose between two wonderful books. The librarian smiled and said she could borrow both. Priya hugged the books happily as she left. That weekend she read both stories twice from cover to cover.
payload.title: Priya borrows two books at once
decoys: The librarian let her take both.

payload.passage: The boys baked banana muffins to use up some old bananas. They mashed the soft fruit and mixed it into the batter. The muffins rose tall and smelled sweet in the oven. Nothing tasty was wasted, and everyone was happy.
payload.title: Boys bake muffins to use old bananas

payload.passage: Seema joined the paper-quilling competition this term. She rolled thin paper strips into tight little coils. She arranged the coils into a colourful flower. The judges admired her neat work and gave her first prize.
payload.title: Seema's Paper Quilling Flower

payload.passage: Tara cheered loudly for the runners at the sports day. She held a banner she had painted the night before. When a small boy felt like quitting, her shouts gave him courage. He finished the race, and Tara felt proud to have helped.
payload.title: Tara's cheering helps a tired runner

payload.passage: Our team made a clean-city model for the project fair. We showed dustbins, parks, and people sweeping the road. We even added little trees made from green sponge. Our model taught everyone to keep their city neat.
payload.title: A Clean-City Model for the Fair

payload.passage: Komal noticed an old man sitting alone on a park bench. He looked lonely and had no one to talk to. So Komal sat beside him and listened to his stories. The old man smiled and said she had made his day.
payload.title: Komal keeps a lonely old man company
decoys: Listening is a kind thing to do

payload.passage: Vikram likes to build tall towers with playing cards. He leans two cards together to make each level. The tower wobbles if he moves too fast. Vikram once built a tower five whole levels high.
payload.title: Vikram Builds Card Towers
decoys: It wobbles if he is fast.

payload.passage: Sneha likes to dance to music in her room. She makes up her own steps and twirls around. Her little sister sometimes joins in too. Dancing is the way Sneha loves to have fun at home.
payload.title: Sneha's Hobby of Dancing
decoys: She makes up her own steps.

payload.passage: Diya cheered for her brother in the school marathon. She stood near the road and held a big sign. When he passed by tired, her shouts gave him new energy. He finished strong, thanks to his sister's cheering.
payload.title: Diya's cheering helps her brother finish
decoys: She held up a big sign.

payload.passage: The library held a treasure hunt to make Book Day exciting. Clues were hidden inside different books on the shelves. Children read each clue to find the next book. The hunt ended at a basket full of small reading prizes.
payload.title: A book treasure hunt on Book Day
decoys: It ended at a prize basket.

payload.passage: Our class made a chart about how to cross the road safely. We drew a zebra crossing and a traffic light. We wrote rules like looking both ways first. The chart taught younger children to stay safe.
payload.title: A Class Chart on Road Safety

payload.passage: Vikram loves to build sand models at home. He keeps a tray of damp sand on the table. He shapes hills, roads, and little tunnels. Vikram drives his tiny cars through the sandy roads he made.
payload.title: Vikram Builds Sand Models
decoys: He drives tiny cars on it.

payload.passage: Dhruv kept his bag close on the busy train. His father had taught him to mind his things. When a man asked to share the seat, Dhruv moved over kindly. He stayed careful and polite the whole ride.
payload.title: Dhruv stays careful on the busy train
decoys: His father taught him to be careful.

payload.passage: Our class made a weather chart for the science project. Each morning we marked if the day was sunny or rainy. We drew little clouds, suns, and raindrops on the chart. By month's end, our chart showed how the weather changed.
payload.title: A Class Weather Chart Project

payload.passage: Tina practised her free throws in basketball every day. The ring seemed very high and far away. She kept her eyes on the ring and shot again and again. In the match she scored five clean baskets.
payload.title: Tina's daily practice scores baskets

payload.passage: Bhavna went to her cousin's house during the holidays. They spent the days painting a big mural on a board. They filled it with trees, birds, and a bright sun. Bhavna loved making the cheerful painting with her cousin.
payload.title: Bhavna Paints a Mural With Her Cousin

payload.passage: Pankaj wanted to join the school relay team. He was not fast enough at the trials. So he ran sprints every morning before class. At the next trial, he made it into the team.
payload.title: Pankaj trains to join the relay team
decoys: He was not fast at trials
He made it into the team

payload.passage: Kabir saw a stall full of bright clay toys. There were tiny animals, carts, and little dolls. The toy maker painted each one with great care. Kabir chose a small clay elephant to take home.
payload.title: Clay Toys at the Fair Stall
decoys: The toy maker painted each toy.

payload.passage: A boy on crutches could not carry his lunch tray. He stood waiting and looked unsure. His friend picked up the tray and carried it for him. They sat together and ate their lunch.
payload.title: A friend carries the lunch tray
decoys: Helping friends is a kind habit

payload.passage: Dev borrowed a book all about growing vegetables. He read how to plant seeds and water them daily. He started a tiny garden in old pots at home. The library book helped him grow his very first tomatoes.
payload.title: A library book helps Dev grow vegetables

payload.passage: Komal visited her grandmother during the school break. Granny taught her how to fold neat little parcels. They wrapped sweets to send to all the relatives. Komal loved helping granny with the kind, careful work.
payload.title: Komal Wraps Sweets With Granny

payload.passage: Aditi and her father waited on the busy railway platform. They watched trains rush in and out with loud horns. A vendor sold hot tea and snacks to travellers. Soon their train arrived, and they climbed aboard.
payload.title: Aditi waits on the busy railway platform

payload.passage: Jatin felt very homesick on his first day at a new school. He missed his old friends and would not smile. His new teacher gave him a small task to feel useful. Slowly Jatin cheered up and made some new friends.
payload.title: A teacher helps Jatin feel at home
decoys: The teacher gave him a small task
New places can be scary at first

payload.passage: Asmita visited her uncle who grew bright dahlias. The garden burst with red, pink, and yellow blooms. Her uncle showed her how to snip the dead flowers. Asmita loved walking through the colourful dahlia garden.
payload.title: The Colourful Dahlia Garden
decoys: The blooms were red and pink.

payload.passage: Sneha likes to make her own greeting stamps. She carves simple shapes into a cut potato. She dips them in paint and presses them on paper. Sneha decorates her letters with her bright potato stamps.
payload.title: Sneha Makes Potato Stamps

payload.passage: Shalini stayed with her grandmother who kept silkworms. Tiny worms munched leaves in flat wooden trays. Granny showed how they spin soft silk threads. Shalini was amazed at the busy little silkworms.
payload.title: Granny Keeps Busy Silkworms

payload.passage: The football match was almost over with the score tied. Then Sahil's team got a free kick near the goal. He aimed carefully and curved the ball past the keeper. His team scored and won at the very end.
payload.title: Sahil scores from a free kick
decoys: He curved the ball past the keeper
Free kicks can decide a match

payload.passage: Priya planted mint in a small clay pot on her sill. She watered it lightly and snipped off dead leaves. The mint smelled fresh whenever she touched it. Bit by bit, the little plant grew bushy and green.
payload.title: Priya Grows a Mint Plant

payload.passage: Anjali loves to make her own bookmarks from pressed flowers. She sticks a dried flower onto a card strip. She covers it with clear tape to keep it safe. Anjali uses her flower bookmark in her storybook.
payload.title: Anjali Makes Flower Bookmarks

payload.passage: Two friends played a quick game of rock paper scissors. They wanted to decide who would bat first. Aarush won three rounds out of five. So he got to bat first in their cricket game.
payload.title: Aarush wins rock paper scissors to bat first

payload.passage: The village fair came to town once a year. There were rides, games, and stalls full of food. Riya rode the spinning wheel and won a small toy at a game. The whole evening at the fair felt like a happy dream.
payload.title: A Fun Evening at the Fair

payload.passage: The relay swimmers cheered each other from the pool edge. As one finished, the next dived in quickly. Their fast handovers saved precious seconds. Smooth teamwork won them the swimming relay.
payload.title: Smooth teamwork wins the swimming relay
decoys: They cheered from the pool edge.

payload.passage: Mohit looked after a pet pigeon with a hurt wing. He kept it in a soft box and fed it grain. Each day he checked the wing and gave it water. Slowly the pigeon healed and learned to trust Mohit.
payload.title: Mohit Cares for a Hurt Pigeon

payload.passage: On a windy day, the clothes on the line flew off into the yard. Mother was busy inside and did not notice. Sonu ran out and gathered every piece of clothing. He folded them neatly and brought them in.
payload.title: Sonu gathers the clothes on a windy day
decoys: The clothes flew off the line
Helping at home makes mothers happy

payload.passage: A spinning top game was played by the village boys. Each tried to spin his top the longest. Hari wound his string tight and threw it down hard. His top spun the longest and he won the round.
payload.title: Hari's top spins the longest
decoys: Top spinning is an old game

payload.passage: Our group built a model garden for the project day. We planted real grass seeds in a wide tray. We added little fences, a swing, and a paper pond. By the day of the fair, our grass had turned green.
payload.title: Our Model Garden Turns Green

payload.passage: Vikram saw his friend Manish fall down in the playground. Manish had scraped his knee and looked ready to cry. Vikram helped him stand and walked him to the teacher. The teacher cleaned the knee and gave a small bandage.
payload.title: Vikram helps his hurt friend Manish
decoys: The teacher gave a small bandage
Friends should look after each other

payload.passage: Anaya loves to make wind spinners from paper plates. She cuts the plate into a spiral shape. She hangs it up so it twirls in the breeze. Anaya watches her spinner turn outside her window.
payload.title: Anaya Makes a Wind Spinner

payload.passage: The children played a game of cricket in the narrow lane. The ball flew into a neighbour's yard by mistake. They went politely and asked for their ball back. The neighbour smiled and threw it over to them.
payload.title: Children politely get their ball back
decoys: The ball flew into a yard

payload.passage: Deepika joined the dance competition for the annual day. She practised her steps every evening for a week. On stage she spun and twirled in perfect time. The crowd cheered loudly as Deepika took the first prize.
payload.title: Deepika Wins the Dance Competition

payload.passage: Roshni planted a hibiscus shrub in the garden. She watered it and fed the soil now and then. She waited as the green buds slowly formed. At last the shrub burst into big red flowers.
payload.title: Roshni Grows a Hibiscus Shrub

payload.passage: The express train was the fastest the children had ever seen. It did not stop at the small stations at all. The world rushed past the windows in a blur. They reached the far city in just a few hours.
payload.title: The children ride a fast express train

payload.passage: On the train, Diya gave her seat to a tired old man. He had been standing with a heavy bag. The old man smiled and blessed her kindly. Diya felt warm inside for the rest of the journey.
payload.title: Diya gives her train seat away
decoys: The old man had a heavy bag.

payload.passage: Meera helped an old lady board the crowded bus. The lady was finding the high step hard to climb. Meera held her bag and offered a steady hand. The grateful lady thanked her with a gentle smile.
payload.title: Meera helps an old lady onto the bus
decoys: The step was hard to climb.

payload.passage: Aarav and his mother made a big bowl of vegetable soup for the cold night. They added soft carrots, beans, and a little pepper. Aarav stirred the pot while it bubbled slowly on the stove. The warm soup made the whole family feel cosy at dinner.
payload.title: Aarav stirs the dinner soup

payload.passage: A boy in the playground fell and his nose started to bleed. He was scared at the sight of the blood. His friend stayed calm and pressed a clean tissue gently. He walked the boy to the school nurse.
payload.title: A boy helps his bleeding friend
decoys: He walked him to the nurse

payload.passage: During the festival, the watchman of the building had to work all night. He looked tired and had not eaten. Neha's family packed him a warm dinner and a sweet. The watchman was touched by their kind thought.
payload.title: Neha's family feeds the tired watchman

payload.passage: Yash and his mother prepared a tiffin for his school trip. They packed rice, a vegetable, and a small sweet. They wrapped a cloth around the box to keep it warm. Yash was glad to share his homemade lunch with friends.
payload.title: Yash prepares a tiffin for the school trip
decoys: They packed rice and a vegetable.
They wrapped a cloth around the box.

payload.passage: Sunita joined the rope-skipping competition on sports day. She turned the rope fast and counted each jump. She skipped longer than anyone else in her class. Sunita won the prize for the most jumps.
payload.title: Sunita Wins the Skipping Count

payload.passage: Seema could not touch her toes when she started yoga. Her body felt stiff and her muscles hurt. She practised the stretches gently every morning. After a month she could bend down and touch her toes easily.
payload.title: Seema becomes flexible through yoga

payload.passage: Sneha enjoys building little houses from ice-cream sticks. She glues the sticks together wall by wall. She paints a tiny door and two small windows. Sneha lined up a whole street of stick houses on her shelf.
payload.title: Sneha Builds Ice-Cream Stick Houses

payload.passage: Aman and his sister surprised their parents with breakfast in bed. They toasted bread and boiled two eggs carefully. They placed everything neatly on a small tray. Their parents were touched by the loving morning surprise.
payload.title: Aman and sister make breakfast surprise
decoys: They toasted bread for the tray.

payload.passage: A little girl could not button her sweater on a cold day. Her tiny fingers fumbled with the round buttons. Her elder sister Roshni buttoned it up for her. The girl felt warm and ready for school.
payload.title: Roshni buttons her little sister's sweater
decoys: Sisters take care of each other

payload.passage: Shalini planted a small okra plant in the yard. She watered it and kept the soil soft. Yellow flowers came, then slim green pods. Shalini was happy to pick fresh okra for cooking.
payload.title: Shalini Grows Okra in the Yard

payload.passage: The boys played a friendly wrestling match on the soft grass. Vimal was smaller but very quick. He used his speed to slip out of every hold. In the end, he won and they shook hands.
payload.title: Quick Vimal wins the wrestling match
decoys: Speed can beat size in wrestling

payload.passage: The class visited the big public library on a field trip. They saw rows and rows of books on tall shelves. A guide showed them how books are sorted by number. The children were amazed by how many stories were there.
payload.title: The class visits the public library

payload.passage: Aarav loves to build cities out of building blocks. He stacks tall towers and wide bridges. He makes roads with little block cars on them. Aarav spends whole afternoons building his block city.
payload.title: Aarav Builds a Block City

payload.passage: Maya helped her mother make a big pot of rice for guests. She measured the rice and washed it three times. Her mother showed her exactly how much water to add. The soft, fluffy rice made the dinner a success.
payload.title: Maya helps cook rice for guests
decoys: She washed the rice three times.
Her mother showed the water amount.

payload.passage: Naveen was given a small fish bowl with one fish. He fed it carefully so the water stayed clean. He set the bowl where it got gentle light. Over the months, his single fish grew happy and bright.
payload.title: Naveen Cares for His One Fish

payload.passage: Karthik visited his grandfather who had a small boat. They rowed out onto the calm village pond. Grandfather showed Karthik how to dip the oars. Karthik loved gliding across the still water with granddad.
payload.title: Rowing the Boat With Grandfather

payload.passage: Akash was a small boy but very quick on his feet. The bigger boys could not catch him on the field. He dribbled the ball past three players with ease. Then he passed it to his friend who scored.
payload.title: Akash dribbles past the bigger boys
decoys: He passed the ball to his friend
Speed helps a lot in football

payload.passage: The marathon for older students was long and tiring. Runners passed water tables along the route. Many slowed down, but one boy kept a steady pace. His even running helped him finish in first place.
payload.title: A steady pace wins the student marathon

payload.passage: Mehak felt sick on the bumpy bus ride at first. Her mother told her to look far out the window. Watching the far hills helped her feel better. By the end she was happily enjoying the trip.
payload.title: Mehak feels better on the bus ride
decoys: She looked at the far hills.

payload.passage: Two friends played a fun dice ladder game on a rainy day. They rolled the dice and moved their tokens. Sahana rolled well and climbed the ladders fast. She reached home first and won.
payload.title: Sahana wins the dice ladder game
decoys: Board games are rainy day fun

payload.passage: Lakshmi visited her uncle who kept a small orchard of limes. The little green trees were full of tangy fruit. Her uncle squeezed fresh lime into cool water for her. Lakshmi loved the sweet-sour drink from the lime trees.
payload.title: Fresh Lime Drinks at Uncle's Orchard

payload.passage: Kabir enjoys folding paper hats for his friends. He folds a newspaper sheet into a neat cap. He makes one for each friend in his group. They all wear their paper hats and march around playing soldiers.
payload.title: Kabir Folds Paper Hats

payload.passage: On a quiet Sunday, Aarav and his sister baked banana bread together. They mashed three ripe bananas and folded them into the batter. The sweet smell filled the house as it baked slowly. They sliced the warm bread and shared it with their happy parents.
payload.title: Aarav and sister bake banana bread
decoys: The sweet smell filled the house.

payload.passage: Sneha saw a hall full of old farming tools at the museum. There were heavy ploughs and big wooden carts. A board said farmers used these in the fields long ago. Sneha was glad that machines now make farming easier.
payload.title: Old Farming Tools at the Museum

payload.passage: The class collected old books to give to a poor school. Each child brought stories they had outgrown. They cleaned and packed the books in big boxes. They were happy to share the joy of reading.
payload.title: Children donate books to a poor school

payload.passage: Two boys played a balancing game on a low wall. They had to walk across without falling off. Sohan held his arms out and stepped slowly. He crossed the whole wall and won the game.
payload.title: Sohan wins the wall balancing game
decoys: They walked on a low wall

payload.passage: At the zoo, the elephant was the biggest animal of all. It splashed water with its long trunk and flapped its wide ears. A baby elephant stayed close to its mother the whole time. Everyone clapped when the big elephant gave a loud trumpet.
payload.title: The Big Elephant at the Zoo
decoys: The elephant splashed water with its trunk.
A baby elephant stayed near its mother.

payload.passage: Amit always missed the basket in basketball games. His friends teased him a little about it. So he stayed back after school and shot the ball again and again. In the next match he scored the most baskets.
payload.title: Amit practises to score in basketball

payload.passage: Grandmother showed Meena how to make soft bread at home. They mixed the dough and let it rest under a cloth. Meena was amazed to see the dough grow bigger by itself. The fresh bread tasted better than any from the shop.
payload.title: Grandmother teaches Meena to make bread
decoys: They let the dough rest under a cloth.
The dough grew bigger on its own.

payload.passage: A little girl could not climb onto the high swing. She tried and tried but kept slipping down. Her brother lifted her up gently onto the seat. He pushed the swing slowly while she laughed.
payload.title: A brother helps his sister onto the swing

payload.passage: Ananya rode the small roller coaster at the fair. The little train zoomed up and down the bumpy track. Her tummy felt funny on the steep drops. Ananya screamed and laughed at the very same time.
payload.title: The Small Roller Coaster Ride
decoys: The train zoomed up and down.

payload.passage: The whole school gathered for the annual sports meet on a bright morning. There were races, jumps, and a long, exciting relay. Houses cheered for their runners from the crowded stands. By the end of the day, the green house had won the most points.
payload.title: The green house wins the sports meet

payload.passage: The library hosted a poetry afternoon for the children. Each child chose a short poem to share. Some poems were funny and some were soft and sweet. Everyone clapped after every brave reader finished.
payload.title: A poetry afternoon at the library

payload.passage: The basketball game came down to the final minute. The score was tied and both teams were tired. A small boy made a careful pass to his friend. His friend scored the last basket and won the game.
payload.title: A last basket wins the close game
decoys: The score was tied near the end.
A small boy made a careful pass.

payload.passage: Priya's father was washing the family car on Sunday. Priya wanted to help, so she held the bucket and passed the cloth. She also wiped the shiny wheels with great care. By lunchtime the car looked brand new and clean.
payload.title: Priya helps wash the family car

payload.passage: Kiara and her father made fresh lemonade to sell at their gate. They squeezed many lemons and stirred in sugar and cold water. They poured the drink into tall glasses with ice cubes. Thirsty passers-by lined up, and the lemonade stall did a happy business.
payload.title: Kiara runs a lemonade stall
decoys: Cold drinks sell well in heat.

payload.passage: Veer tried his luck at the dart game at the fair. He had to pop balloons stuck on a board with darts. He popped two but missed the last one. The man still gave him a small whistle as a prize.
payload.title: Veer's Turn at the Dart Game

payload.passage: Meera enjoys making puppets from old socks. She sews on button eyes and woollen hair. Then she puts on little shows for her younger brother. Meera's sock puppets always make her brother laugh out loud.
payload.title: Meera Makes Sock Puppets
decoys: She does shows for her brother.

payload.passage: Aditya enjoys making maps of his own neighbourhood. He draws the roads, his school, and the park. He marks his house with a big red dot. Aditya pins his map proudly on his bedroom wall.
payload.title: Aditya Maps His Neighbourhood
decoys: He draws the roads and park.
He marks his house in red.

payload.passage: Sneha enjoys drawing cartoons in her sketchbook. She draws funny faces with big eyes and wide smiles. Sometimes she makes up little stories about them too. Drawing cartoons is the best way Sneha likes to spend her free time.
payload.title: Sneha's Hobby of Drawing Cartoons

payload.passage: Riya loves to write little stories in her notebook. She thinks of brave heroes and faraway lands. She draws a small picture at the top of each story. Riya dreams of making a whole book one day.
payload.title: Riya Writes Her Own Stories
decoys: She draws a picture for each.

payload.passage: Our group built a model of a zoo for the project day. We made small cages with paper animals inside. We added a pond for the ducks and a path for visitors. Our teacher said our little zoo was full of life.
payload.title: Our Model Zoo Project

payload.passage: Ravi watched a snake charmer's act at the fair. The man played a flute as a basket sat in front of him. The crowd watched closely to see what would happen. Ravi clapped when the show ended with a clever twist.
payload.title: The Snake Charmer Act at the Fair

payload.passage: Anaya joined a workshop at the museum. A teacher showed the children how people made pots long ago. Each child got to shape a little pot with clay. Anaya was proud to make something the old way.
payload.title: A Pottery Workshop at the Museum

payload.passage: The street light near the temple had stopped working. The lane was dark and people stumbled at night. A boy told his father, who informed the office. Soon a worker came and fixed the light.
payload.title: A boy helps get the street light fixed
decoys: The lane was dark at night

payload.passage: Deepika looked after a small dog that hated the rain. She kept it warm and dry on stormy days. She walked it only when the sky was clear. Over time, the dog grew calm even when it rained.
payload.title: Deepika's Dog That Hates Rain

payload.passage: Ahaan learned to make a simple tomato soup all on his own. He boiled the tomatoes and pressed them through a strainer. He warmed the smooth soup and added a pinch of pepper. He carried two bowls to the table, very proud of his first soup.
payload.title: Ahaan makes tomato soup on his own
decoys: He boiled and strained the tomatoes.
He added a pinch of pepper.

payload.passage: Meera enjoys making masks out of paper plates. She cuts holes for the eyes and paints funny faces. She ties a string so the mask stays on. Meera and her friends wear the masks for their pretend plays.
payload.title: Meera Makes Paper Plate Masks

payload.passage: Diya went to the stationery stall to buy school things. She picked out pencils, erasers, and a bright new notebook. The seller put everything into a small paper bag. Diya could not wait to use her new things at school.
payload.title: Buying School Things at the Market
decoys: The seller used a paper bag.

payload.passage: Asmita joined the best-from-waste competition this term. She made a flower vase from an old plastic cup. She painted it and stuck on bits of coloured paper. The judges praised her work and gave her first place.
payload.title: Asmita's Waste-Cup Flower Vase

payload.passage: Karan visited the museum with his school on Monday. He saw old coins, statues, and tools from long ago. A guide told stories about how people lived in the past. Karan left the museum knowing much more about history.
payload.title: A School Trip to the Museum
decoys: He saw old coins and statues.

payload.passage: Karan has a hobby of building with blocks. He stacks them into houses, bridges, and tall towers. Sometimes his towers fall, but he just builds again. Karan loves making new things with his colourful blocks.
payload.title: Karan Builds with Blocks

payload.passage: On a rainy day, the children could not go out to play. So they took out the carrom board instead. Vinod aimed carefully and pocketed all his coins first. He won the game and everyone wanted to play again.
payload.title: Vinod wins the carrom game indoors

payload.passage: Anil stayed with his grandmother who made paper toys. She folded boats, hats, and little jumping frogs. She taught Anil the secret of each clever fold. Anil filled a box with the paper toys granny taught him.
payload.title: Granny Makes Paper Toys

payload.passage: Manoj looked after a duckling that had lost its mother. He kept it warm and fed it soft grain. He let it splash in a shallow dish of water. As the weeks passed, the duckling grew into a fine duck.
payload.title: Manoj Raises a Lonely Duckling

payload.passage: Kabir has started learning to play the drums. He taps out a steady beat with two sticks. At first his rhythm was slow and wobbly. Now Kabir can keep a beat along with his favourite songs.
payload.title: Kabir Learns to Play Drums
decoys: His beat was wobbly at first.

payload.passage: Our group grew two plants for the science project. We gave one plant water and kept the other dry. After a week, the watered plant was green and the dry one drooped. Our project showed clearly that plants need water.
payload.title: A Plant Project on Water

payload.passage: Kabaddi needs both strength and quick breathing. Vimal took a deep breath and ran into the other team. He touched two players and rushed back to his side. His team got two points and cheered for him.
payload.title: Vimal scores two points in kabaddi

payload.passage: Sara saw beautiful old clothes at the museum. There were robes with gold thread and dresses of fine silk. A board said kings and queens wore them on special days. Sara wished she could try on such grand clothes.
payload.title: Royal Clothes at the Museum
decoys: Sara wished to try them on.

payload.passage: Diya forgot her library book on the bus one day. She felt worried and told the librarian honestly. The librarian thanked her for being truthful and waited. The next day the kind driver returned the lost book.
payload.title: Diya is honest about her lost library book
decoys: She left it on the bus.

payload.passage: Two cricket teams played in the bright afternoon sun. The match was close and every run mattered. Manav ran quickly between the wickets without tiring. His fast running helped his team win by two runs.
payload.title: Manav's quick running wins the match

payload.passage: Pankaj took part in the quiz competition between the houses. His team answered questions about animals, plants, and rivers. He kept calm and remembered each fact just in time. In the end, Pankaj's team lifted the shiny quiz trophy.
payload.title: Pankaj's Team Lifts the Quiz Trophy

payload.passage: Sara joined the sack race at the fair. The children climbed into big cloth sacks and hopped to the finish. Many of them tumbled over halfway through. Sara hopped fast and came in third, all out of breath.
payload.title: The Sack Race at the Fair

payload.passage: During the exam, a boy's pen ran out of ink suddenly. He had no other pen in his bag. His neighbour quietly passed him a spare blue pen. The boy finished his paper on time.
payload.title: A boy lends a spare pen
decoys: His pen ran out of ink
He finished his paper on time

payload.passage: An old man could not read the medicine label clearly. The letters were too small for his eyes. A boy read out the timings loudly for him. The man thanked him and took his medicine right.
payload.title: A boy reads the medicine label

payload.passage: The skipping competition was held in the school yard. Children jumped the rope as many times as they could. Some tripped after only a few jumps. A girl who kept a steady rhythm skipped the most.
payload.title: A steady girl wins the skipping contest
decoys: Some tripped after a few jumps.

payload.passage: The night train rocked gently as the family settled into their bunks. The children peeked out at the passing village lights. The steady sound of the wheels soon made them sleepy. They drifted off and woke up in a brand-new city.
payload.title: A family sleeps on the night train
decoys: The wheels made a steady sound.

payload.passage: Sneha rode the merry-go-round at the fair. She picked a wooden horse painted bright pink. The ride went round and round while gentle music played. Sneha waved at her father each time she passed by.
payload.title: Sneha on the Merry-Go-Round

payload.passage: Diya loves to make tiny clothes for her dolls. She cuts soft cloth and sews it with care. She made a little dress and a tiny hat. Diya's dolls now have a whole wardrobe of clothes.
payload.title: Diya Sews Tiny Doll Clothes

payload.passage: The zookeeper came to feed the animals in the morning. He gave fresh grass to the deer and big chunks of meat to the lions. He cleaned the cages and made sure each animal had clean water. The zookeeper works hard to keep the animals happy and healthy.
payload.title: The Zookeeper Cares for Animals

payload.passage: Ananya loves to learn folk songs from her grandmother. They sing together every evening on the terrace. Ananya remembers the words after singing many times. Now she can sing three whole songs all by herself.
payload.title: Ananya Learns Folk Songs

payload.passage: Reyansh missed two easy catches early in the cricket match. He felt low, but his friends patted his back kindly. He kept his eyes sharp for the rest of the game. Later he took a brilliant catch that helped his team win.
payload.title: Reyansh makes up for his dropped catches

payload.passage: Pooja joined the painting competition at the school fete. She painted a bright peacock dancing in the rain. She blended blue and green for its lovely feathers. The judges admired her colours and gave her first place.
payload.title: Pooja's Peacock Painting Wins

payload.passage: The museum had a hall of old weapons and armour. Kabir saw shining swords, shields, and metal suits. A guide said soldiers wore the armour into battle long ago. Kabir thought the heavy suits must have been hard to walk in.
payload.title: Old Armour at the Museum
decoys: Kabir thought the suits looked heavy.

payload.passage: Vikram rode the waves on a small body board. He waited for a big wave and then floated forward fast. He fell off many times but always climbed back on. Riding the waves was the most thrilling part of his beach day.
payload.title: Riding Waves on a Board

payload.passage: Manya kept a pet kitten that loved a warm lap. Each evening it curled up while she read. She fed it well and brushed its soft fur. Over the weeks, the kitten and Manya grew very close.
payload.title: Manya's Kitten Loves Her Lap
decoys: It curled up on her lap.

payload.passage: The school class went on a train ride for their picnic. They counted the bridges and tunnels along the way. Inside a long tunnel, the children gasped at the dark. When they came out, everyone cheered at the bright light.
payload.title: The class enjoys a picnic train ride
decoys: They gasped in the dark tunnel.

payload.passage: Tina planted a small ginger root in a pot. She watered it lightly and kept it warm. She waited many weeks for a green shoot. Slowly the ginger plant pushed up tall leaves.
payload.title: Tina Grows Ginger in a Pot

payload.passage: The colony held an obstacle race for all the children. They crawled under ropes and hopped through old tyres. Some got tangled and laughed too hard to move on. A focused girl cleared every part and won the race.
payload.title: A focused girl wins the colony obstacle race

payload.passage: Harsh went to his cousin's farm during the summer. They rode on a cart pulled by two strong bulls. The cart bumped along the dusty village track. Harsh thought the bumpy bullock-cart ride was great fun.
payload.title: Harsh Rides the Bullock Cart

payload.passage: A girl's hair ribbon flew off into a muddy ditch. She felt sad as it was her favourite one. Her friend found a stick and lifted it out gently. They washed it clean at the tap together.
payload.title: A friend rescues the lost ribbon
decoys: The ribbon flew into a ditch
They washed it at the tap

payload.passage: Our group made a model of a science lab for the project. We placed tiny bottles, tubes, and a small balance. We showed how careful scientists work with their tools. Everyone said our lab model looked very real.
payload.title: Our Model Science Lab Project

payload.passage: A small boy could not carry his big art chart and bag together. The chart kept slipping from his hands. His friend Tarun took the bag for him. They reached the class without dropping anything.
payload.title: Tarun carries his friend's bag
decoys: They dropped nothing on the way
Sharing a load helps a friend

payload.passage: Komal planted a curry leaf sapling in the yard. She watered it well and kept the soil soft. She watched the small plant put out fresh leaves. After many months, it grew into a tall, leafy bush.
payload.title: Komal Grows a Curry Leaf Bush

payload.passage: Beena stayed with her grandmother during the mango season. Granny made sweet mango juice every afternoon. They sat in the cool room and drank it slowly. Beena thought granny's mango juice was the best treat.
payload.title: Granny's Sweet Mango Juice
decoys: They sat in a cool room.

payload.passage: Aditya likes to grow a small water plant in a jar. He placed a green sprig in clean water on the sill. New roots and leaves slowly grew over the weeks. Aditya was happy to watch his jar plant thrive.
payload.title: Aditya Grows a Plant in a Jar
decoys: He placed a green sprig in water.

payload.passage: Tara and her brother bargained at the bag stall. The seller asked for a high price for a school bag. Their mother spoke politely and asked for less. After some talk, they agreed on a fair price and bought the bag.
payload.title: Bargaining for a School Bag
decoys: The seller asked a high price.

payload.passage: Two teams played a close game of throwball. The ball went over the net many times. Reema made a strong throw at the last point. Her team caught up and won the match.
payload.title: Reema's strong throw wins the match
decoys: The ball went over the net

payload.passage: Our class made a model showing how a plant grows. We glued seeds, sprouts, and a full plant in a row. We drew the sun and rain above each stage. Visitors learned the steps a tiny seed takes to grow.
payload.title: A Model of How Plants Grow

payload.passage: Pinky could swim well but her little brother could not. He slipped and started to splash in the shallow end. Pinky reached him quickly and pulled him to safety. Their mother thanked Pinky for being so quick.
payload.title: Pinky saves her little brother in the pool
decoys: Knowing to swim keeps us safe

payload.passage: The fair had a small train that went around the ground. Little children sat inside the colourful carriages. The train tooted its horn at every turn. Vikram and his baby sister rode it together twice.
payload.title: The Little Train at the Fair

payload.passage: A girl in the bus could not find a seat and felt tired. She had a heavy bag on her shoulders. A boy stood up and offered her his seat. She sat down and thanked him with a smile.
payload.title: A boy gives up his seat
decoys: She thanked him with a smile
Offering a seat shows good manners

payload.passage: Geeta stayed with her aunt who ran a small dairy. Cool jugs of milk and curd lined the shelves. Aunt let Geeta help pour the milk into bottles. Geeta enjoyed the busy mornings at her aunt's dairy.
payload.title: Busy Mornings at Aunt's Dairy
decoys: Jugs of milk lined the shelves.

payload.passage: During lunch, Salim saw a boy with no spoon for his rice. The boy did not know what to do. Salim quickly gave the boy his own spare spoon. The boy smiled and ate his lunch happily.
payload.title: Salim shares his spare spoon

payload.passage: Two friends raced their paper boats in the rainwater. The water flowed fast along the gutter. Kabir's boat was light and moved the quickest. His boat reached the drain first and won the race.
payload.title: Kabir's paper boat wins the race

payload.passage: Anita joined the table tennis class with her friends. At first she could not return the fast serves. She practised her returns hour after hour. Soon she could play long rallies with ease.
payload.title: Anita gets better at table tennis
decoys: She could not return serves first

payload.passage: An old lady could not lift the heavy shutter of her shop. It was stuck and very stiff in the morning. Two boys came and pulled it up together. She opened her shop on time and thanked them.
payload.title: Boys lift the stuck shop shutter
decoys: She opened her shop on time

payload.passage: Ishaan likes to draw maps of made-up places. He adds rivers, hills, and little towns. He gives each place a funny name of his own. Ishaan dreams of one day visiting the lands he draws.
payload.title: Ishaan Draws Made-Up Maps

payload.passage: The library held a guess-the-book game for Book Week. The librarian read one clue from a famous story. Children raced to name the book and its hero. The fun game made everyone want to read more.
payload.title: A guess-the-book game during Book Week

payload.passage: It was raining hard, and a man waited at the bus stop without cover. He was getting wet and shivering. Esha and her mother shared their big umbrella with him. He stayed dry until his bus arrived.
payload.title: Esha shares an umbrella with a wet man
decoys: He stayed dry till his bus came
Sharing in the rain is kind

payload.passage: The classroom dustbin was full and overflowing. Bits of paper spilled onto the floor. Without being told, Rakesh emptied the bin outside. Then he swept up the paper to keep the room clean.
payload.title: Rakesh keeps the classroom clean
decoys: A clean room is everyone's job

payload.passage: In the game of tag, one child must chase and touch others. Farhan was very quick and hard to catch. He dodged left and right and ran in circles. No one could tag him for the whole game.
payload.title: Farhan is too quick to be tagged

payload.passage: Grandfather's slippers were left out in the rain by mistake. They were soaked and could not be worn. Little Manya dried them with a soft cloth. She placed them neatly by his bed.
payload.title: Manya dries grandfather's wet slippers

payload.passage: Anjali enjoys making her own bird feeder. She fills an old cup with seeds and hangs it up. She waits quietly by the window to watch. Anjali smiles when little birds come to eat her seeds.
payload.title: Anjali Makes a Bird Feeder
decoys: She fills a cup with seeds.

payload.passage: The museum had a special part you could touch. Rohan ran his fingers over rough rocks and smooth shells. He felt the soft fur of an old rug. This hands-on room was Rohan's favourite of the whole museum.
payload.title: The Touch Room at the Museum

payload.passage: A baby sparrow sat trapped behind the window grill. It chirped and could not get out. Sahana opened the window slowly and gently. The little bird flew out into the open sky.
payload.title: Sahana frees the trapped sparrow
decoys: Freeing birds is a kind act

payload.passage: The whole class made beautiful greeting cards in art period. Most children kept their cards to take home. But Bhavna sent hers to the children in the hospital. She hoped the cards would make the sick children smile.
payload.title: Bhavna sends cards to sick children
decoys: Small gifts can cheer people up

payload.passage: The library opened a new section just for science books. There were books about volcanoes, oceans, and tiny insects. Children crowded around the shelves with curious eyes. Many learned facts they shared with their families.
payload.title: A new science section opens at the library

payload.passage: Our class made a recycling model for the science fair. We sorted paper, plastic, and glass into coloured bins. We showed how old things can become new again. Our model taught visitors not to throw everything away.
payload.title: A Recycling Model at the Fair

payload.passage: Arnav volunteered to help at the library after school. He stamped the date inside each borrowed book. He also reminded friends to keep the books clean. The librarian thanked him for being a great helper.
payload.title: Arnav volunteers to help in the library
decoys: He stamped the date in books.
He reminded friends to be careful.

payload.passage: On the school trip, the children played antakshari in the bus. They had to sing songs one after another. Riya's team sang the most songs without stopping. Their team won the fun singing game.
payload.title: Riya's team wins the singing game
decoys: They played it in the bus

payload.passage: Vidya put a spider plant in a pot on the shelf. She watered it weekly and kept it in soft light. She watched it send out long, striped leaves. Over time, the plant grew tiny baby shoots too.
payload.title: Vidya Grows a Spider Plant

payload.passage: Pranav took part in the frog-jump game on field day. He squatted low and leapt forward like a frog. He hopped quickly across the line of cones. Pranav reached the end first and won a bright sticker.
payload.title: Pranav Wins the Frog-Jump Game

payload.passage: Naina and her father grew tomatoes and then cooked with them. They picked the ripe red tomatoes from the garden pots. Together they made a tasty sauce on the stove. It felt special to eat food they had grown themselves.
payload.title: Naina and father cook their own tomatoes
decoys: They picked ripe tomatoes from pots.
They made a sauce on the stove.

payload.passage: Our group made a model of a snowy land for the fair. We used cotton for snow and built small igloos. We added a sledge and people in warm coats. Our teacher said the snowy land looked cold and lovely.
payload.title: Our Model Snowy Land Project

payload.passage: Two boys had a friendly game of pithoo in the lane. They threw the ball at a pile of flat stones. Faisal hit the pile and scattered the stones. His team built them back and won the game.
payload.title: Faisal's team wins the pithoo game

payload.passage: Bhavna kept a pet hen that laid eggs. She fed it grain and gave it clean water daily. She kept its little coop dry and warm. Over time, the hen trusted Bhavna and laid eggs each morning.
payload.title: Bhavna Cares for Her Laying Hen

payload.passage: Ekta joined the rhyme-recital competition on stage. She had learned a happy poem about a little kite. She moved her hands as if flying the kite herself. The judges smiled and gave Ekta the winner's badge.
payload.title: Ekta's Kite Rhyme Wins
decoys: The poem was about a kite.

payload.passage: Aarav spent a week with his grandfather, who loved to fish. They walked to the pond before the sun was high. Grandfather showed Aarav how to hold the line and wait. Aarav was thrilled when he caught his very first fish.
payload.title: Aarav Goes Fishing With Grandfather

payload.passage: The market had a stall full of clay pots and lamps. Kabir watched the potter shape wet clay on his wheel. The finished pots were left in the sun to dry. Kabir's mother bought two small pots for their plants.
payload.title: The Clay Pot Stall at the Market

payload.passage: The children played a game of statue in the park. When the leader shouted, everyone had to freeze still. Toya stood like a stone without even blinking. She held it the longest and won the game.
payload.title: Toya wins the statue game

payload.passage: Pooja noticed that a girl in class had forgotten her lunch. The girl sat sadly with an empty box. Pooja opened her own tiffin and shared her sandwiches. The two girls ate happily and became good friends.
payload.title: Pooja shares her lunch with a friend
decoys: The girl had an empty lunch box
Pooja had sandwiches in her tiffin
Sharing food is a kind act

payload.passage: Our class made a model of a busy bakery for the fair. We built an oven, a counter, and shelves of bread. We showed a baker rolling soft dough by hand. Visitors said the warm little bakery looked tasty.
payload.title: A Class Model of a Bakery

payload.passage: Anil planted a creeping bean by the kitchen window. He watered it and let it climb a string. He watched the leaves and buds appear each day. Soon the bean vine framed the whole window.
payload.title: Anil's Bean Vine Frames the Window

payload.passage: Devi helped her uncle prepare a big fruit basket for a wedding. They washed apples, grapes, and oranges with care. They arranged the fruit so it looked colourful and full. The lovely basket was the first thing guests admired.
payload.title: Devi prepares a fruit basket for a wedding

payload.passage: Vidya was given a kitten that would not eat at first. She tried warm milk and a quiet, calm corner. Day by day she coaxed it to take small bites. In time, the kitten ate well and grew healthy.
payload.title: Vidya Coaxes a Shy Kitten to Eat

payload.passage: The zoo had a small farm corner for young children. There were goats, rabbits, and a few clucking hens. Karan brushed a friendly goat and fed it fresh leaves. He liked that he could touch and help the gentle farm animals.
payload.title: The Petting Farm at the Zoo

payload.passage: Charu planted a row of radishes in the soft soil. She watered them and kept the bed weed-free. She watched the leafy tops grow up fast. At last she pulled up crisp red radishes.
payload.title: Charu Grows Crisp Radishes

payload.passage: Mohit was very good at solving puzzles. His sister gave him a hard jigsaw with many pieces. He worked on it quietly for the whole afternoon. By evening he had joined every piece and finished it.
payload.title: Mohit finishes the hard jigsaw puzzle

payload.passage: Our class made a big chart about healthy food for the project. We cut out pictures of fruits, milk, and green vegetables. We wrote why each food keeps our body strong. The chart hung on the wall for the whole school to read.
payload.title: A Class Chart About Healthy Food
decoys: The chart hung on the wall.

payload.passage: Mehul took part in the skipping-rope race on the field. He turned the rope fast and jumped without a trip. His feet moved like a blur as the others fell behind. Mehul reached the finish first and won the race.
payload.title: Mehul Wins the Skipping-Rope Race

payload.passage: Sara saw the gorillas sitting calmly behind the glass. The big gorilla rested while a baby played near its feet. A board said gorillas are gentle and live in family groups. Sara watched the quiet family for a long, happy while.
payload.title: The Gorilla Family at the Zoo
decoys: A baby played near its feet.

payload.passage: Yusuf was too shy to read aloud in front of others. The librarian let him read quietly to a soft toy first. After many gentle tries, his voice grew calm and clear. On Book Day, Yusuf bravely read a story to the whole class.
payload.title: Shy Yusuf learns to read aloud
decoys: He read to a soft toy first.

payload.passage: On the train, Tara helped a mother carry her bags. The mother had a baby and too much to hold. Tara lifted one bag onto the rack above. The grateful mother thanked the helpful girl warmly.
payload.title: Tara helps a mother with her bags
decoys: Tara lifted a bag onto the rack.

payload.passage: Riya enjoys making colourful floor patterns at her doorstep. She draws curves and dots first, using a little chalk. Then she fills in each shape with bright coloured powder. Riya loves how the floor pattern brightens up the whole house.
payload.title: Riya Makes Doorstep Floor Patterns

payload.passage: Naina shared her favourite books with the new student. She walked him around the quiet library shelves. She showed him where the adventure stories were kept. The new boy felt welcome and made a friend.
payload.title: Naina helps a new student at the library
decoys: She showed him the adventure shelf.
The new boy made a friend.

payload.passage: A cow stood in the middle of the busy road, looking lost. Cars honked loudly and the cow grew scared. Ramesh and his uncle gently led it to the side. The cow walked away calmly to the field.
payload.title: Ramesh leads the lost cow to safety
decoys: The cow walked to the field
Animals need help on busy roads

payload.passage: Rehan's bus got a flat tyre near a field of sunflowers. Everyone climbed down while the driver fixed it. The children played among the tall yellow flowers. Soon the bus was ready, and they rode on with smiles.
payload.title: A flat tyre stops Rehan's bus by sunflowers

payload.passage: The class had a memory game during the rainy break. Cards were placed face down on the desk. Ritu remembered where each card was hidden. She matched the most pairs and won the game.
payload.title: Ritu wins the memory card game
decoys: A good memory helps in games

payload.passage: Ishita helped the librarian arrange the books neatly. They put all the picture books on the lower shelves. They placed bigger story books higher up. Now smaller children could reach their favourite books easily.
payload.title: Ishita helps arrange the library books
decoys: Picture books went on lower shelves.

payload.passage: Ravi likes to whittle little shapes from soft wood. With help from his father, he carves slowly and safely. He has made a small spoon and a tiny boat. Ravi keeps his wooden things on a special little shelf.
payload.title: Ravi Carves Shapes from Wood

payload.passage: Kabir's bus broke down on the way to the zoo. The driver checked the engine while everyone waited. Soon another bus came to take them along. They reached the zoo a little late but very happy.
payload.title: Kabir's bus breaks down on the way

payload.passage: Geeta had saved her pocket money for many weeks. She wanted to buy a pretty doll she had seen. Then she heard that a flood had hurt many families. So Geeta gave all her savings to help them instead.
payload.title: Geeta donates her savings to flood victims
decoys: Geeta wanted to buy a doll
She had saved for many weeks

payload.passage: The girls' team was new at hockey and lost many matches. They felt sad and wanted to stop playing. Their captain told them to practise harder together. After weeks of effort, they finally won a match.
payload.title: The hockey team practises and wins

payload.passage: Two villages played a friendly football match in the field. Players from both sides ran hard under the warm sun. Even when goals were missed, everyone clapped kindly. The match ended in a tie, and both teams were happy.
payload.title: Two villages play a friendly football match
decoys: Players ran under the warm sun.
The match ended in a tie.

payload.passage: Deepika planted a small papaya plant in the yard. She watered it and gave it plenty of sun. She watched the broad leaves spread out wide. After many months, the plant gave its first papaya.
payload.title: Deepika Grows a Papaya Plant
decoys: She gave it plenty of sun.

payload.passage: The school marked Book Day with a costume parade. Children dressed as their favourite story characters. There were pirates, princesses, and even a friendly dragon. The parade made everyone excited about reading.
payload.title: Children dress up for Book Day

payload.passage: Ved fell behind early in the cross-country run. The path was long and went up a small hill. He breathed slowly and kept his steps even. By the last stretch he had moved up to second place.
payload.title: Ved climbs to second in the cross-country run
decoys: The path went up a hill.

payload.passage: The school held a craft competition with waste materials. Bhavna made a pen stand from an old bottle. She covered it with bright paper and tiny shells. The judges loved her clever idea and gave her first prize.
payload.title: Bhavna's Waste-Material Pen Stand

payload.passage: Sara enjoys making wind chimes from old keys and shells. She ties them to a stick with bits of string. When the breeze blows, they make a soft jingle. Sara hung her wind chime by the kitchen window.
payload.title: Sara Makes a Wind Chime
decoys: She used old keys and shells.
She hung it by the window.

payload.passage: A girls' kabaddi match was played at the school meet. The two teams were equal till the last raid. Nita took a deep breath and made a clever raid. She tagged two girls and won the match for her team.
payload.title: Nita's clever raid wins the match
decoys: A smart raid can win kabaddi

payload.passage: Seema planted a jasmine creeper by her window. She watered it and let it climb a thin net. She waited as the small white buds appeared. Soon the creeper filled her window with sweet flowers.
payload.title: Seema Grows a Jasmine Creeper

payload.passage: A girls' basketball team was new and lost their first match. They felt low but did not stop trying. They practised passing and shooting after school. In the next match they finally won.
payload.title: The basketball team practises and wins
decoys: Practice turns a loss into a win

payload.passage: The night train rocked the children gently to sleep. They lay in the bunks and watched the lights slip by. The wheels made a soft, steady sound. In the morning they woke up in a new city.
payload.title: Children sleep on the night train
decoys: The wheels made a steady sound.

payload.passage: The train stopped at a busy station full of noise and crowds. Vendors walked along the platform selling tea and snacks. A loud voice announced the names of the next stations. The children watched it all with wide, curious eyes.
payload.title: A busy stop on the train journey

payload.passage: The children helped the cook at the school camp make dinner. Some peeled potatoes while others washed the leafy greens. The cook let them stir the big pot under his watchful eye. The campers cheered as they ate the meal they had helped to prepare.
payload.title: Campers help the cook make dinner

payload.passage: Ishaan visited the deer park inside the zoo. Soft brown deer with spotted backs walked freely among the trees. Some deer came close to nibble grass from his open hand. Ishaan felt very happy to be so near the gentle animals.
payload.title: Feeding Deer at the Zoo

payload.passage: An old grandmother could not switch on the high fan. She was too short to reach the button. A tall boy reached up and switched it on. The grandmother felt cool and blessed him.
payload.title: A boy switches on the high fan
decoys: She was too short to reach

payload.passage: Sahil found a book about caring for pet fish. He read how to keep the water clean and fresh. Soon he set up a small bowl at home. The library book helped him become a good fish keeper.
payload.title: A library book teaches Sahil about fish
decoys: He read about keeping water clean.
He set up a fish bowl.

payload.passage: Aryan visited his grandfather, who kept honeybees. From a safe spot, they watched the bees buzzing about. Grandfather showed Aryan the sweet honey in the comb. Aryan tasted the fresh honey and licked his lips.
payload.title: Grandfather Keeps Buzzing Honeybees
decoys: They watched from a safe spot.

payload.passage: A girls' football team trained hard for the big final. They passed and ran together every day. On the final day they played as one strong team. They scored two goals and lifted the cup.
payload.title: Teamwork helps the girls win the final
decoys: A team wins by playing together

payload.passage: The children helped cook a big meal at the village kitchen. Some washed the rice while others cut the vegetables. The cook showed them how to stir the huge pot safely. Everyone felt proud to help feed the whole gathering.
payload.title: Children help cook a village meal
decoys: The cook used a huge pot.

payload.passage: A girl named Komal was scared to climb the rope in gym. Her hands felt weak and she would slip down. She practised gripping the rope every day. Soon she climbed right to the top and rang the bell.
payload.title: Komal climbs the gym rope to the top
decoys: She rang the bell at top

payload.passage: Anjali looked out of the train window the whole way. She saw rivers shining like silver ribbons. She watched birds fly over the wide green fields. The changing view made the journey feel like a story.
payload.title: Anjali enjoys the view from the train

payload.passage: Diya enjoys making greeting cards by hand. She folds the paper, draws a picture, and writes kind words inside. She made a bright card for her mother's birthday. Diya thinks handmade cards are more special than bought ones.
payload.title: Diya Makes Handmade Cards
decoys: She made one for her mother.

payload.passage: At the market, the fish seller called out his prices loudly. Fresh fish lay on a bed of ice to keep cool. People crowded around to pick the best ones. Anjali held her nose because of the strong fishy smell.
payload.title: The Busy Fish Seller's Stall

payload.passage: When Asha lost the running race, she felt sad and alone. The other children ran to cheer the winner. But her friend Mira came and held her hand. Mira told her that trying her best was what mattered most.
payload.title: Mira cheers up a sad friend

payload.passage: Riya loves to make her own puppets from wooden spoons. She paints a face on the back of each spoon. She glues on woollen hair and a cloth dress. Riya's spoon puppets star in her little plays.
payload.title: Riya Makes Wooden Spoon Puppets
decoys: She paints a face on the spoon.

payload.passage: Kabir watched a bangle seller fit bangles onto a lady's wrist. The seller knew exactly which size would slip on. The glass bangles made a soft clinking sound. Kabir thought it was clever how the seller never broke even one.
payload.title: The Skilled Bangle Seller

payload.passage: Diya and her grandmother went to buy cloth at the market. The shop had silk, cotton, and soft woollen pieces. The shopkeeper unrolled bolt after bolt of bright cloth. Together they chose a blue piece for a new dress.
payload.title: Buying Cloth for a New Dress

payload.passage: Priya brought a bag of oranges for the bus journey. She shared them with the children sitting near her. Soon the whole back of the bus was eating fruit. The sweet snack made the long trip feel shorter.
payload.title: Priya shares oranges on the bus
decoys: She shared them with nearby children.

payload.passage: The class made a book corner inside their own room. They brought storybooks and a soft rug from home. They added a small lamp for cosy reading. Now they could enjoy books even between lessons.
payload.title: The class builds a reading corner

payload.passage: Nikhil decided to cook lunch alone for the very first time. He boiled the rice and made a simple curry he had watched. He was careful near the hot stove the whole time. His proud parents enjoyed the meal he cooked by himself.
payload.title: Nikhil cooks lunch by himself
decoys: He was careful near the stove.

payload.passage: Two friends raced marbles down a long sand track. They dug a smooth channel for the marbles to roll. Dinesh's marble rolled fast without leaving the track. It reached the end first and won the race.
payload.title: Dinesh's marble wins the track race
decoys: A smooth track helps the race

payload.passage: Naveen entered the running race on sports day. He warmed up his legs before the whistle blew. When the race began, he ran with all his might. Naveen crossed the line first and won the gold medal.
payload.title: Naveen Wins the Sports Day Race

payload.passage: Karan likes to grow vegetables in the garden. He has planted tomatoes, beans, and a few chillies. Each day he pulls out the weeds and waters them. Karan is proud when he picks vegetables for the kitchen.
payload.title: Karan Grows His Own Vegetables

payload.passage: Veer likes to make musical shakers from old tins. He fills each tin with rice, beans, or seeds. Each one makes a different rattling sound. Veer shakes them in time with the music he loves.
payload.title: Veer Makes Musical Shakers

payload.passage: A girls' relay team kept dropping the baton in practice. They felt upset after every drop. Their coach taught them to pass it smoothly. On race day they passed it well and won.
payload.title: Smooth passing wins the girls' relay

payload.passage: A volleyball match was played in the bright sunshine. The ball flew high over the net many times. Salim gave a strong jump and hit a winning shot. His team scored and won the close match.
payload.title: Salim's jump shot wins volleyball
decoys: The ball flew over the net
His team won the close match

payload.passage: Every morning before school, Dinesh runs around the park. He started with just one round and felt very tired. After many weeks of practice, he could run five rounds easily. Now he is the fastest runner in his class.
payload.title: Dinesh trains to become a fast runner
decoys: He runs in the park every morning

payload.passage: A long jump event was held on the school field. Each child ran fast and leapt as far as they could. Tarun took a big run and jumped the farthest. He set a new mark for the long jump.
payload.title: Tarun jumps the farthest in long jump
decoys: A good run helps the jump

payload.passage: Shalini joined the clay-modelling competition at school. She shaped a little bird sitting on a nest. She made tiny eggs and a worm beside it. The judges loved her detailed work and gave her first prize.
payload.title: Shalini's Clay Bird Wins
decoys: The bird sat on a nest.

payload.passage: Tina kept a pet fish that liked to hide. She added a small cave for it to rest in. She fed it daily and kept the water clear. Over time, the shy fish swam out more bravely.
payload.title: Tina's Shy Fish Grows Brave

payload.passage: An old man dropped his bunch of keys down a deep step. He could not bend low to reach them. A boy named Yogesh climbed down and picked them up. He placed the keys back in the man's hand.
payload.title: Yogesh returns the old man's keys
decoys: The keys fell down a step

payload.passage: Two teams played a quick word-building game in class. They made words from a set of letters. Manya's team made the most long words. They scored the highest and won the game.
payload.title: Manya's team wins the word game

payload.passage: Naveen badly wanted to win the chess game against Rishi. He saw a chance to move a piece while Rishi looked away. But he stopped himself and played the fair way. Even though he lost, he felt good inside.
payload.title: Naveen plays chess fairly and honestly

payload.passage: A boy named Chetan loved kite flying more than any game. His kite kept diving down because of weak knots. His uncle taught him to tie strong, neat knots. Soon his kite flew high and steady.
payload.title: Chetan learns to fly his kite steadily
decoys: Good knots help the kite fly

payload.passage: Ishaan likes to grow seeds in little cups. He pushed bean seeds into the wet soil and waited. After a few days, tiny green shoots poked out. Ishaan was thrilled to watch his little plants grow taller each day.
payload.title: Ishaan Grows Seeds in Cups

payload.passage: Veer enjoys building bridges across a stream of water. He lays flat stones one after another. He tests if they hold his weight before he steps. Veer is proud when he crosses on his own stone bridge.
payload.title: Veer Builds a Stone Bridge

payload.passage: A boy saw a frog struggling in a deep, slippery drain. It could not jump out of the smooth walls. He lowered a long stick into the drain gently. The frog climbed the stick and hopped to safety.
payload.title: A boy rescues a frog from the drain
decoys: The frog could not jump out

payload.passage: Vivek helped his mother roll out soft flatbread for the evening meal. He sprinkled flour so the dough would not stick. His mother showed him how to make each one round and thin. Vivek felt proud when his first flatbread puffed up like a balloon.
payload.title: Vivek learns to roll flatbread
decoys: He sprinkled flour on the dough.

payload.passage: Manya went to her grandmother's house in the rice fields. Bright green plants stretched as far as she could see. Granny showed her how the rice slowly grows in water. Manya loved the wide, peaceful view of the fields.
payload.title: Manya Sees the Green Rice Fields

payload.passage: Our group built a model of an old fort for the project. We made high stone walls and a tall gate. We added little soldiers keeping watch on top. Our teacher said the fort looked strong and grand.
payload.title: Our Model Fort Project

payload.passage: When the old temple wall needed a fresh coat of paint, the colony joined in. Fathers held the ladders steady and mothers mixed the paint. The children passed the brushes and cleaned the spills. By Sunday the wall looked bright and new.
payload.title: The colony paints the temple wall together
decoys: People can do great things together

payload.passage: The girls played a long badminton doubles match. They had to talk and move as a pair. At first they bumped into each other near the net. With good calling, they soon worked together and won.
payload.title: Good teamwork wins the badminton doubles
decoys: They bumped near the net at first.

payload.passage: At the beach, a man sold roasted corn from a small cart. He fanned the coals to keep them hot. The smell made everyone feel hungry. Anjali and her father shared a hot corn while watching the sea.
payload.title: The Corn Seller at the Beach
decoys: Anjali shared corn with her father.

payload.passage: Anjali went to the market to buy fresh curd and milk. The dairy seller poured the milk into her steel can. He wrapped the curd in a clean leaf-lined box. Anjali carried them home carefully so nothing would spill.
payload.title: Buying Milk and Curd
decoys: He poured milk into a can.

payload.passage: An old couple struggled to carry their bags up the railway bridge. The steps were many and steep. Two young boys took the bags and climbed up for them. The couple blessed the boys for their help.
payload.title: Boys help an old couple cross the bridge
decoys: Helping elders is a fine deed

payload.passage: Kabir and his cousins played beach cricket on the sand. They used a flat piece of wood as a bat. The soft sand made it hard to run quickly. Everyone laughed and cheered until the game finally ended.
payload.title: Playing Cricket on the Beach
decoys: They used wood as a bat.

payload.passage: Tanya read the same favourite book again and again. Each time she noticed something new in the pictures. Her mother asked why she liked it so much. Tanya said good books feel like dear old friends.
payload.title: Tanya rereads her favourite book

payload.passage: Riya went with her father to the weekly farmers market. Farmers sold fruit and vegetables straight from their fields. Everything looked fresh and smelled of the earth. Riya's father said this food was the freshest you could buy.
payload.title: Shopping at the Farmers Market

payload.passage: Ravi's baby sister was crying loudly in her cot. Their mother was busy cooking in the kitchen. Ravi sat by the cot and sang a soft little song. Slowly the baby stopped crying and fell fast asleep.
payload.title: Ravi soothes his crying baby sister
decoys: The baby was crying loudly in her cot
Ravi sang a soft little song
Babies cry when they feel upset

payload.passage: Tara was given a fluffy white rabbit to look after. She fed it carrots and soft green leaves each day. She cleaned its hutch and gave it room to hop. Tara loved how her gentle rabbit grew tame over time.
payload.title: Tara Looks After Her Rabbit

payload.passage: Aarav loves to make paper aeroplanes that fly far. He folds the wings sharp and straight. He tests each plane to see which flies best. Aarav holds little flying races with his friends in the park.
payload.title: Aarav Makes Flying Paper Planes

payload.passage: Kabir enjoys making music with empty glass bottles. He fills each bottle with a different amount of water. When he taps them, they make different notes. Kabir can play a simple tune on his bottle row.
payload.title: Kabir Makes a Bottle Tune

payload.passage: Manya grew a leafy fern in a shady corner. She kept the soil damp but never too wet. She liked how the fronds curled out slowly. Over time, the fern filled the pot with green lace.
payload.title: Manya Grows a Shady Fern

payload.passage: Saira was sad because she had no books to read at home. Her teacher took her to the school library. There she got a card to borrow two books a week. Saira beamed as she carried her first book home.
payload.title: Saira gets her own library card
decoys: Her teacher took her to the library.
She could borrow two books a week.

payload.passage: The two friends were on rival teams for the football match. They played hard but fairly the whole game. Even when one team lost, the friends hugged at the end. Their friendship stayed strong no matter who won.
payload.title: Friendship stays strong after the football match
decoys: The friends hugged at the end.

payload.passage: The library held a storytelling hour on Saturday morning. Children sat in a circle on the soft mat. The storyteller used funny voices for each character. Everyone laughed and begged for just one more tale.
payload.title: A storytelling hour at the library
decoys: Children sat on the soft mat.

payload.passage: Our group made a model of a river and its banks. We poured blue beads to show the flowing water. We added trees, boats, and people fishing along the side. Our teacher said the river model looked very real.
payload.title: A Model of a Flowing River

payload.passage: Sneha visited the camel at the zoo on a hot day. The big camel had a tall hump on its back. A board said camels can go many days without water. Sneha learned that camels are made for living in the dry desert.
payload.title: The Camel at the Zoo
decoys: The camel had a tall hump.
Sneha visited on a hot day.

payload.passage: Sara loves to make her own bookmarks. She cuts strips of card and draws fun pictures on them. She tapes a small ribbon to the top of each one. Sara gives her best bookmarks to friends who love reading.
payload.title: Sara Makes Her Own Bookmarks
decoys: She tapes a ribbon on top.

payload.passage: Reyansh's team was losing the kabaddi match by many points. The coach asked them to stay calm and keep trying. They made two brave raids in the last minutes. Their never-give-up spirit turned the match into a win.
payload.title: A never-give-up spirit wins the kabaddi match
