decoys: The coach asked them to stay calm.

payload.passage: Tara stayed with her grandfather, who told the best stories. Every night he sat on the swing and called her over. He told tales of brave kings and clever animals. Tara fell asleep happy after each wonderful story.
payload.title: Grandfather Tells Bedtime Stories

payload.passage: The fair had a fun house full of curved mirrors. In one mirror Anaya looked very tall and thin. In another she looked short and round. She laughed at her funny shapes in the mirror room.
payload.title: The Funny Mirror Room
decoys: One mirror made her look tall.

payload.passage: An old lady's spectacles broke right before her eye check. She could not see the doctor's chart at all. A helpful nurse lent her a spare pair of glasses. The lady completed her check with a smile.
payload.title: A nurse lends spare glasses to a lady

payload.passage: Tara and her family had a picnic right on the beach. They ate sandwiches, fruit, and cold juice on a mat. Seagulls flew close, hoping for a few crumbs. The picnic by the sea was the best part of the trip.
payload.title: A Picnic on the Beach

payload.passage: Our class made a big model of a railway station. We laid down tracks and placed little trains on them. We built a platform with tiny people waiting around. The teacher said our station was the best in the class.
payload.title: A Class Model Railway Station

payload.passage: Ravi could only read slowly when the year began. He visited the library and read a little each day. Bit by bit, the words came faster and easier. By the end of the year he loved reading.
payload.title: Daily library visits make Ravi a reader
decoys: He read a little each day.

payload.passage: The classroom door handle came loose and would not turn. The children were stuck inside before the bell. A clever boy fixed the handle with a small screw. The door opened and everyone went out happily.
payload.title: A boy fixes the loose door handle

payload.passage: Geeta took part in the singing competition on stage. She practised her song many times at home first. On the day, she sang sweetly without missing a note. The judges smiled and gave Geeta the winner's badge.
payload.title: Geeta Sings Her Way to Victory

payload.passage: The market had a stall full of bright woollen caps. Winter was coming, so many people stopped to buy. Aditya tried on a red cap with a fluffy ball on top. He chose it because it kept his ears nice and warm.
payload.title: Buying a Warm Cap for Winter
decoys: The cap had a fluffy ball.

payload.passage: The boys played a game of seven stones with a soft ball. They had to stack the stones and knock them down. Vivek aimed well and hit the pile cleanly. His team rebuilt the stones and won the round.
payload.title: Vivek's team wins seven stones
decoys: Aim and speed win this game

payload.passage: Sara and her friends drew big pictures in the sand. They used sticks and shells to make a smiling sun. Then they wrote their names in tall letters. The waves slowly washed their drawings clean again.
payload.title: Drawing Pictures in the Sand

payload.passage: Komal grew a small bonsai tree in a flat dish. She trimmed its leaves and bent its branches with care. She watered it just enough each day. Over the years, the tiny tree took a graceful shape.
payload.title: Komal Shapes a Bonsai Tree

payload.passage: A small boy could not reach his ball under the parked car. He bent down but his arms were too short. An older girl used a long stick to push it out. The boy grabbed his ball and thanked her.
payload.title: A girl gets the ball back

payload.passage: Tanmay took part in the cycling race in the school ground. He pedalled hard and steered around each turn. He kept his eyes on the path and did not slow down. Tanmay crossed the line first and lifted the trophy.
payload.title: Tanmay Wins the Cycling Race

payload.passage: Aarav learned to fly kites from his grandfather. They run the strong thread between their fingers just right. On windy days they fly bright kites from the terrace. Aarav loves the long evenings of flying kites together.
payload.title: Aarav Learns to Fly Kites

payload.passage: The train rolled slowly through a wide stretch of desert. The children stared at the endless golden sand. Far away, camels moved like tiny dots on the dunes. The vast, dry land amazed them for hours on end.
payload.title: The train rolls through golden desert

payload.passage: Our group made a working volcano for the project day. We mixed soda and vinegar to make it bubble over. Red foam ran down the paper mountain like real lava. The whole class gathered around to watch our volcano erupt.
payload.title: Our Group Makes a Bubbling Volcano

payload.passage: Lakshmi kept a pair of small turtles in a tank. She fed them, cleaned the water, and gave them a rock. She let them bask under a soft warm light. Over the months, her turtles grew bigger and bolder.
payload.title: Lakshmi Cares for Two Turtles

payload.passage: Aman discovered a book full of jokes in the library. He laughed so hard he had to cover his mouth. At home he told the jokes to his whole family. The library book filled their evening with giggles.
payload.title: Aman finds a joke book at the library

payload.passage: Diya saw stuffed animals from many lands at the museum. There was a lion, a bear, and a big spotted leopard. They stood so still that they looked almost alive. A board told her where each animal once lived.
payload.title: Animals Display at the Museum

payload.passage: The class made a giant book of their own stories. Each child wrote one page about a magic forest. The librarian bound the pages into a real book. They placed it proudly on the library shelf.
payload.title: The class makes a giant story book

payload.passage: A little girl's shoelace came undone on the busy stairs. She could nearly trip on the loose lace. Her elder brother bent down and tied it tight. They walked down the stairs safely.
payload.title: A brother ties the loose lace

payload.passage: The village bus was the only ride to the weekly market. Farmers climbed in with baskets of fresh vegetables. The children sat on a sack of grain near the back. The cheerful bus rolled slowly down the dusty road.
payload.title: The village bus carries people to market

payload.passage: Sara loves to make snow globes from old jars. She glues a small toy to the inside of the lid. She fills the jar with water and tiny glitter. When Sara shakes it, the glitter swirls like snow.
payload.title: Sara Makes a Snow Globe
decoys: She glues a toy to the lid.

payload.passage: The library held a reading challenge for the summer. Each child kept a list of the books they finished. Stars were given for every ten books read. By August the walls were covered in shiny stars.
payload.title: A summer reading challenge at the library
decoys: Children kept a list of books.
Stars were given for ten books.

payload.passage: The train slowed at every small station on the way. People got off and new travellers climbed aboard. Vendors called out, selling tea and warm snacks. The slow train showed the children many little towns.
payload.title: A slow train stops at many stations

payload.passage: Asmita was given a small green frog to mind. She kept it in a glass tank with a little pool. She fed it tiny insects and kept it cool. Over time, the frog grew used to its quiet home.
payload.title: Asmita Minds a Little Frog

payload.passage: The girls' basketball team practised passing for many weeks. In the final, the other side was tall and strong. The girls used clever quick passes to move around them. Their smart teamwork won them the school basketball cup.
payload.title: Clever passing wins the basketball cup

payload.passage: Priyansh missed an easy goal early in the match. He felt sad, but his teammates cheered him up. He focused again and played his very best. Later he scored two goals and helped his team win.
payload.title: Priyansh recovers and scores two goals
decoys: He missed an easy goal first.

payload.passage: The twins, Reva and Dev, made jam from ripe mangoes. They cut the fruit and cooked it slowly with sugar. They poured the thick jam into clean glass jars. Now they could enjoy mango jam long after the season ended.
payload.title: Twins make mango jam in jars
decoys: They cooked the fruit slowly with sugar.
They poured the jam into jars.

payload.passage: A poor student had no umbrella during the rainy season. He got wet every day on his way to school. His classmate brought him an old raincoat from home. The boy stayed dry and felt very thankful.
payload.title: A boy gives away his raincoat

payload.passage: An old man's groceries were too many to carry alone. The bags slipped from his tired hands. A schoolboy offered to carry them to his home. The old man rested while the boy did the lifting.
payload.title: A schoolboy carries an old man's groceries
decoys: The bags slipped from his hands
The old man rested at home

payload.passage: Riya was very good at drawing, and her friend Kavya struggled with it. Kavya wanted to draw a nice peacock for the art class. So Riya showed her how to make the feathers step by step. Kavya finished a lovely peacock and felt very happy.
payload.title: Riya teaches Kavya how to draw
decoys: Kavya wanted to draw a peacock
Riya showed the feathers step by step
Drawing is a wonderful skill to learn

payload.passage: Diya planted a bright marigold in a round pot. She watered it each morning before going to school. She checked for tiny pests on the green leaves. After a few weeks, the pot was full of golden flowers.
payload.title: Diya Grows Golden Marigolds

payload.passage: Every morning Meera helps her mother in the kitchen. She washes the small cups and lays the plates on the table. Her mother says the work finishes faster with two hands. Meera feels proud to be a good helper at home.
payload.title: Meera helps her mother every morning
decoys: The work finishes faster with two hands
Children should always be helpful and kind

payload.passage: Tushar planted a basil herb in a small pot. He watered it gently and kept it in the light. He pinched the tops so it would grow bushy. Slowly the basil filled the pot with green leaves.
payload.title: Tushar Grows a Basil Herb

payload.passage: An old lady's heavy shopping bag tore open in the market. Fruits and packets fell onto the dusty ground. Some children gathered them and found a new bag. They filled the bag and walked her home.
payload.title: Children help a lady with her torn bag
decoys: Helping in the market is kind

payload.passage: Every Friday was library day for Class Three. The librarian read them a fun story aloud. Then the children chose books to take home. Friday quickly became their favourite day of the week.
payload.title: Friday is library day for Class Three
decoys: The librarian read a story aloud.
The children chose books to take home.

payload.passage: The children made bookmarks during library craft day. They cut coloured paper and drew their favourite animals. Then they slipped the bookmarks into their library books. Now they could always find their page again.
payload.title: Children make bookmarks on craft day

payload.passage: Rohit fell down halfway through the long race. His knee hurt, but he stood up and kept going. He did not come first, but he finished the whole race. The crowd clapped loudest for his brave effort.
payload.title: Rohit finishes the race after falling
decoys: His knee hurt after the fall.

payload.passage: The children had a hopping race in the school ground. Each player had to hop on one leg to the line. Bunty hopped steadily without putting his foot down. He reached first and won the funny race.
payload.title: Bunty wins the one-leg hopping race

payload.passage: Pari forgot her lines during the school play and froze. The crowd grew quiet and she felt like crying. From the side, her friend softly reminded her of the words. Pari remembered, finished the play, and got a big clap.
payload.title: A friend helps Pari remember her lines
decoys: She got a big clap at the end

payload.passage: Two friends played a clapping rhyme game in the corridor. They had to clap in time with the song. Jaya kept the rhythm without missing a beat. She and her friend won the clapping game.
payload.title: Jaya keeps perfect rhythm in the clapping game
decoys: She did not miss a beat
Rhythm games are fun to play

payload.passage: Karthik took part in the tug-of-war on sports day. His team held the thick rope and dug in their heels. They pulled together with one big heave. Karthik's team dragged the other side over and won.
payload.title: Karthik's Team Wins the Tug-of-War

payload.passage: Naina joined the stencil-art competition at the fair. She placed a leaf on paper and dabbed colour around it. When she lifted the leaf, its clear shape stayed. The judges loved her neat prints and gave her the prize.
payload.title: Naina's Leaf Stencil Art Wins

payload.passage: Nidhi and her father baked a batch of crunchy nut cookies for the weekend. They crushed the nuts and folded them into the soft dough. They shaped small rounds and pressed each one with a fork. The crisp cookies were gone within an hour because everyone loved them.
payload.title: Nidhi and father bake nut cookies
decoys: They pressed each cookie with a fork.

payload.passage: On a cold morning, Father and Diya made warm porridge. They added milk, oats, and a little sugar to the pot. Diya watched it bubble and stirred so it would not stick. The hot porridge warmed them both before school.
payload.title: Father and Diya make warm porridge
decoys: They added milk and oats to the pot.
Diya stirred so it would not stick.

payload.passage: The train passed slowly through a wide green valley. The children pressed their faces to the cool window glass. They spotted grazing cows and a winding silver stream. The lovely view made the long journey feel short and happy.
payload.title: The train passes through a green valley

payload.passage: The bus took a shortcut through a quiet forest road. Tall trees made a cool, green roof overhead. The children spotted a deer near the path. The peaceful ride felt like a special treat.
payload.title: The bus takes a quiet forest road

payload.passage: Ananya loves to make her own paper kites for her dolls. She folds tiny squares of paper into little kites. She ties them to short bits of thread. Ananya's dolls fly the tiny kites in pretend play.
payload.title: Ananya Makes Tiny Doll Kites

payload.passage: Dhruv was chosen to run the final leg of the relay. His team had a small lead when he took the baton. He ran with all his heart down the last stretch. He crossed the line first, and his team jumped for joy.
payload.title: Dhruv runs the winning relay leg
decoys: His team had a small lead.

payload.passage: Shalini went to her grandmother's house full of old photos. They sat with a big album on a rainy afternoon. Granny told a story behind each black-and-white picture. Shalini loved hearing about her family from long ago.
payload.title: Old Family Photos at Granny's

payload.passage: The reptile keeper held a baby crocodile for the children to see. He showed its sharp little teeth and rough skin. He told them crocodiles can stay still for hours waiting for food. The children listened with wide eyes and many questions.
payload.title: Learning About Baby Crocodiles

payload.passage: A new boy sat alone at lunch with no one to talk to. He looked down at his food sadly. Two friends moved over and made room for him. Soon all three were chatting and laughing.
payload.title: Friends make room for the new boy

payload.passage: Ravi found a message in a bottle on the beach. He pulled out a small note rolled up inside. The note had a smiley face and a kind hello. Ravi wondered who had sent it across the wide sea.
payload.title: Ravi Finds a Bottle Message
decoys: The note had a smiley face.
He pulled out a small note.

payload.passage: The bus driver stopped to help a stranded family by the road. Their car had broken down in the hot sun. He let them ride along to the next town. The grateful family thanked the kind driver again and again.
payload.title: A kind bus driver helps a stranded family
decoys: He took them to the next town.

payload.passage: Gaurav went to his uncle's mango farm in the heat of June. Rows of trees stood heavy with golden fruit. His uncle taught him how to pick the ripe mangoes. Gaurav filled a whole basket and felt very proud.
payload.title: Gaurav Picks Mangoes at the Farm

payload.passage: Sara planted chilli seeds in a pot on the terrace. She kept the soil moist and the pot in the sun. Tiny white flowers bloomed, then little green chillies. Sara was proud when she picked her first ripe chilli.
payload.title: Sara Grows Chillies on the Terrace

payload.passage: The boys at the hostel learned to make simple egg toast for breakfast. They beat the eggs and dipped slices of bread into the mixture. The warden showed them how to cook each slice until golden. The warm toast gave them energy before a busy day of classes.
payload.title: Hostel boys make egg toast
decoys: They dipped bread in beaten eggs.

payload.passage: Beena joined the thumb-print art competition at school. She pressed her inky thumb to make tiny round shapes. She turned the prints into a tree full of fruit. The judges loved her clever idea and gave her the prize.
payload.title: Beena's Thumb-Print Tree Wins

payload.passage: Sahil took part in the balloon-pop race on field day. He had to run, sit on a balloon, and pop it loudly. Then he raced back to tag his next friend. Sahil's team popped all theirs first and won.
payload.title: Sahil's Team Wins the Balloon Pop
decoys: He sat to pop the balloon.

payload.passage: Reva rode the bus to the city for the very first time. The tall buildings amazed her as they passed. So many cars and lights filled the busy roads. She held her grandfather's hand and stared in wonder.
payload.title: Reva's first bus ride to the city

payload.passage: The cricket match between the two classes was very close. Both teams batted well and the score stayed even. In the last over, a careful single decided the winner. The two captains shook hands warmly after the exciting game.
payload.title: A close cricket match between two classes

payload.passage: Reyansh helped his mother make a warm pot of lentil soup for dinner. He washed the lentils and watched them cook until soft. His mother added a few spices while he stirred carefully. The simple soup with rice made a cosy meal on the cool evening.
payload.title: Reyansh helps cook lentil soup

payload.passage: Aarav rode the bus to his new school for the first time. He felt shy among all the unfamiliar faces. A friendly boy beside him started a happy chat. By the time they arrived, Aarav had made his very first friend.
payload.title: Aarav makes a friend on the bus

payload.passage: Our group built a small bridge from ice-cream sticks. We glued the sticks in layers to make it strong. Then we placed weights on it to test its strength. Our bridge held the most weight and won the challenge.
payload.title: Our Stick Bridge Wins the Challenge
decoys: We added weights to test it.

payload.passage: The library books were piled in a great mess on the floor. The librarian looked tired and overwhelmed. A group of students offered to sort them by number. Soon every book sat neatly on its shelf.
payload.title: Students help the tired librarian sort books
decoys: The books were in a mess

payload.passage: Ishaan enjoys making a calendar with his own drawings. He draws a picture for each month of the year. He adds the numbers in neat little boxes. Ishaan hangs his handmade calendar in the kitchen.
payload.title: Ishaan Makes a Drawing Calendar

payload.passage: Tara stopped at the fish tank in the zoo. Bright fish of every colour swam past the glass. A small striped fish hid inside a soft sea plant. Tara pressed her nose to the glass and watched them glide by.
payload.title: Bright Fish in the Zoo Tank
decoys: A striped fish hid in a plant.
Tara pressed her nose to the glass.

payload.passage: The cousins baked a chocolate cake for their grandfather's birthday. They mixed the batter and licked the spoons clean. They wrote his name on the cake with white icing. Grandfather laughed with joy when he saw the special cake.
payload.title: Cousins bake grandfather's birthday cake
decoys: They wrote his name in white icing.

payload.passage: The old well in the village had become dirty and unsafe. People could not draw clean water from it. The villagers cleaned it together over the weekend. Now they get fresh water from the well again.
payload.title: Villagers clean the dirty well together
decoys: People could not draw clean water
They cleaned it over the weekend
Working together helps the whole village

payload.passage: Our class made a model of a busy farm for the fair. We added toy cows, a barn, and rows of green crops. We showed how the farmer works from dawn to dusk. Visitors said our farm looked alive and real.
payload.title: A Class Model of a Busy Farm

payload.passage: Gaurav stayed with his grandfather, who fixed wooden chairs. The workshop smelled of fresh sawdust and glue. Grandfather let Gaurav hand him each tool he needed. Gaurav enjoyed helping mend the old wooden chairs.
payload.title: Mending Chairs With Grandfather

payload.passage: The school canteen aunty dropped a tray full of glasses. The glasses rolled across the wet floor. Some students quickly gathered them before anyone slipped. They wiped the floor dry and stacked the glasses.
payload.title: Students help the canteen aunty

payload.passage: Aarav went to the pet shop in the busy market. Small fish swam in tanks and birds chirped in cages. A puppy wagged its tail when Aarav came close. Aarav wished he could take a pet home that very day.
payload.title: The Pet Shop in the Market

payload.passage: Yusuf borrowed a book about building simple machines. He read how levers and wheels make work easier. Over the weekend he built a small toy cart. He was thrilled that a library book taught him to make it.
payload.title: Yusuf builds a cart from a library book
decoys: He read about levers and wheels.
He built a small toy cart.

payload.passage: Ravi liked the flower seller at the market best. She had roses, marigolds, and bunches of soft white jasmine. She tied the flowers into pretty garlands with quick fingers. Ravi bought a small garland for his grandmother.
payload.title: The Flower Seller's Pretty Garlands

payload.passage: Two friends had a skipping race in the school yard. They had to skip to the wall and back. Harini skipped fast without tripping on the rope. She reached the wall first and won.
payload.title: Harini wins the skipping race

payload.passage: Veer enjoys making paper boats and planes. He folds the paper carefully, line by line. On rainy days he floats his boats in the puddles. Veer's room is always full of his colourful paper creations.
payload.title: Veer Makes Paper Boats and Planes

payload.passage: Tarun planted a row of carrots in the garden. He watered the soft soil and pulled out weeds. He waited as the green tops grew taller. At last he pulled up bright orange carrots from the ground.
payload.title: Tarun Grows Carrots in the Garden

payload.passage: Meera visited a museum that showed how books were made. She saw old paper, ink pots, and metal letters. A guide showed how pages were once pressed by hand. Meera was glad that books are easy to make today.
payload.title: How Books Were Made Long Ago

payload.passage: Renu went to her grandmother's house full of books. Tall shelves rose from the floor to the ceiling. Granny helped Renu pick a story to read each day. Renu loved exploring the cosy room full of books.
payload.title: Granny's Room Full of Books

payload.passage: Rakesh stayed with his grandparents during the cool winter. Each night they gathered under a thick warm quilt. Granny told stories while grandfather sipped hot milk. Rakesh felt safe and snug on those cold winter nights.
payload.title: Snug Winter Nights With Grandparents

payload.passage: It started to rain heavily as the children walked home. Only Simran had remembered to bring an umbrella. She called her classmate Rekha to walk under it with her. They reached home dry and giggling all the way.
payload.title: Simran shares her umbrella in the rain

payload.passage: A new boy named Sameer joined the class and knew no one. He sat alone and looked very shy at break time. Nisha walked up and asked him to share her bench. Soon they were laughing together like old friends.
payload.title: Nisha welcomes the lonely new boy
decoys: Sameer sat alone at break time
They laughed together like old friends
Making friends is good for everyone

payload.passage: Dev stayed with his grandparents who had an old well. Each morning grandfather drew up cool water in a bucket. Dev helped pull the rope hand over hand. Dev felt strong and proud helping at the village well.
payload.title: Drawing Water at the Village Well

payload.passage: Our group built a model house with a slanting roof. We made the walls from cardboard and the roof from foil. We showed how rain would slide off the slanted top. Our teacher praised how well our little house was made.
payload.title: Our Model House With a Slanting Roof

payload.passage: Ravi was the youngest player in the football team. The bigger boys did not want to pass him the ball. But the coach told them to play as one team. When they finally passed to Ravi, he scored a goal.
payload.title: Teamwork helps young Ravi score
decoys: The coach told them to share
A team plays better as one

payload.passage: Saanvi helped a young mother lift her bags onto the train. The mother was holding a baby and could not manage alone. Saanvi placed the bags neatly on the upper rack. The thankful mother praised the kind and helpful girl.
payload.title: Saanvi helps a mother on the train
decoys: The mother was holding a baby.
Bags went on the upper rack.

payload.passage: Meera visited the plant nursery at the edge of the market. Rows of green plants sat in little pots and bags. A man helped her pick a plant with bright red flowers. Meera carried it home to brighten up her balcony.
payload.title: Buying a Plant at the Nursery
decoys: She picked one with red flowers.

payload.passage: Faisal's team was losing the football match by two goals. The players felt tired and almost gave up. But Faisal told them to keep trying till the end. They scored three goals quickly and won the match.
payload.title: Faisal's team never gives up and wins
decoys: The team was losing by two goals
Hope can change a losing game

payload.passage: The swimming gala filled the pool deck with families. Children dived in and raced across the cool water. Whistles blew and the crowd cheered each splash. By evening, many shiny medals had been given out.
payload.title: The swimming gala is held at the pool

payload.passage: Ananya brought home two little kittens to care for. She fed them milk and kept them warm in a basket. She played with them gently so they felt safe. As the weeks passed, the kittens grew strong and playful.
payload.title: Ananya Raises Two Kittens

payload.passage: Ishaan found a small theatre inside the museum. A short film told the story of an old city. He sat in the dark and watched the screen come alive. Ishaan learned how that city grew over hundreds of years.
payload.title: Watching a Film at the Museum
decoys: The film was about an old city.

payload.passage: The hockey team had lost many games this season. Their coach told them to keep their spirits up. They practised harder and trusted each other on the field. In the final game, their effort finally paid off with a win.
payload.title: The hockey team's effort earns a win
decoys: The coach kept their spirits up.
They trusted each other on the field.

payload.passage: The bus driver waited a moment for a running boy. The boy had nearly missed the morning bus. He thanked the driver, out of breath, as he climbed in. The kind wait meant the boy was not late for school.
payload.title: A kind driver waits for a late boy
decoys: The boy was out of breath.
He was not late for school.

payload.passage: Priya loved the monkeys best at the zoo. They jumped from branch to branch and hung by their tails. One cheeky monkey grabbed a banana and ran up the tree. Priya laughed so much that her cheeks began to hurt.
payload.title: Funny Monkeys Made Priya Laugh
decoys: The monkeys hung by their tails.

payload.passage: Veer found a room about the sea at the museum. Glass cases held shells, coral, and a model whale. A screen showed fish swimming deep in the dark water. Veer learned how many strange creatures live in the sea.
payload.title: The Sea Room at the Museum

payload.passage: Our class made a chart about saving electricity. We drew a fan, a light, and a fridge with happy faces. We wrote how to switch off things we do not use. The chart taught the school to save power each day.
payload.title: A Class Chart on Saving Electricity

payload.passage: Faiz cheered for the losing team during the match. He told them their hard work mattered more than the score. The tired players smiled at his kind words. In the next match they played even better.
payload.title: Faiz cheers up the losing team

payload.passage: Ananya rode a camel along the beach with her father. The tall camel swayed gently as it walked. She could see far out over the blue sea. Ananya laughed every time the camel took a big step.
payload.title: A Camel Ride on the Beach

payload.passage: The relay swimmers stood ready at the edge of the pool. Each one waited for a teammate to touch the wall. Their handovers were fast and perfectly timed. Smooth teamwork helped them win the swimming relay by a wide margin.
payload.title: A team wins the pool relay smoothly
decoys: They waited for a teammate's touch.

payload.passage: Sara enjoys making her own simple puzzles. She draws a picture and sticks it onto card. Then she cuts it into many odd pieces. Sara mixes them up and asks her friends to put it back.
payload.title: Sara Makes Her Own Puzzles
decoys: She sticks the picture on card.

payload.passage: A blind man was walking with his stick on the footpath. A pile of bricks lay right in his path. Aryan quickly warned him and guided him around the bricks. The man thanked Aryan and walked on safely.
payload.title: Aryan guides a blind man safely
decoys: A pile of bricks lay on the path
The man walked with a stick
We must help those who cannot see

payload.passage: Manya was afraid to bat against the fast bowler. The hard ball came at her very quickly. She practised facing fast throws every day. Soon she hit the fast balls with ease.
payload.title: Manya learns to face fast bowling
decoys: Courage and practice help in cricket

payload.passage: Anjali enjoys building forts out of blankets and chairs. She drapes the blankets over the chair backs. Inside, she makes a cosy little room with cushions. Anjali loves to read her books inside the soft fort.
payload.title: Anjali Builds Blanket Forts

payload.passage: Harsh took part in the obstacle challenge on field day. He crawled under nets and jumped over low bars. He ran around cones without knocking a single one. Harsh finished first and won a bright ribbon.
payload.title: Harsh Wins the Obstacle Challenge

payload.passage: The waves at the beach rolled in one after another. Ananya stood at the edge and let the cool water touch her feet. Each time a wave came, she squealed and jumped back. She played this game with the sea for a long time.
payload.title: Playing with the Waves
decoys: The water was cool on her feet.
Ananya jumped back from the waves.
The sea is full of water.

payload.passage: Suresh was running in the relay race for his team. He gripped the baton tightly and waited for his turn. When his friend reached him, he grabbed the baton and sprinted. His team finished first because of his fast run.
payload.title: Suresh helps his team win the relay

payload.passage: Rohan stood near the snake house at the zoo. Behind the thick glass, a long green snake slid slowly over a branch. A board said the snake was not harmful and ate small frogs. Rohan was a little scared but very curious too.
payload.title: Rohan Watches the Zoo Snake
decoys: The snake was long and green.

payload.passage: The children planted a small garden outside the library. They had learned how to grow plants from a library book. They watered the seeds and watched them sprout. Reading had helped them grow real flowers.
payload.title: A library book helps children grow a garden

payload.passage: Riya started a stamp collection this year. She keeps her stamps neatly in a small album. Friends and family give her stamps from their old letters. Riya loves to look at the pictures from many far places.
payload.title: Riya's New Stamp Collection
decoys: She keeps them in an album.

payload.passage: Our class made a chart about the five senses for the project. We drew an eye, an ear, a nose, a tongue, and a hand. Under each we wrote what that sense helps us do. The chart taught us how we learn about the world.
payload.title: A Class Chart on the Five Senses

payload.passage: The school held a cycling race around the big ground. Many children pedalled as fast as they could. Manisha kept a steady speed and did not tire out. She crossed the line first and won the race.
payload.title: Manisha wins the cycling race
decoys: The race went around the ground

payload.passage: A baby goat got its leg stuck in a wire fence. It bleated loudly in pain and fear. Joy carefully bent the wire and freed its leg. The little goat hopped away to its mother.
payload.title: Joy frees the trapped baby goat
decoys: It hopped away to its mother
Saving animals is a kind deed

payload.passage: Aarav joined the cricket team but was nervous about batting. The coach made him practise his shots every single evening. Slowly he learned to watch the ball and time his hits. In the big match, his careful batting helped his team reach the score.
payload.title: Aarav's practice helps him bat well
decoys: He learned to watch the ball.

payload.passage: Mohit took part in the relay race with three friends. He ran his part and passed the baton smoothly. Each boy ran his hardest around the track. Their team came first and they hugged with joy.
payload.title: Mohit's Team Wins the Relay

payload.passage: The two best friends ran side by side in the long race. Near the end, one of them stumbled and fell hard. The other stopped and helped his friend back up. They finished the race together, and the crowd cheered their kindness.
payload.title: Two friends finish the race together
decoys: One of them stumbled and fell.

payload.passage: Manoj entered the paper plane competition in the hall. He folded his plane with sharp, careful creases. When he threw it, the plane sailed far across the room. Manoj's plane flew the farthest and he won a medal.
payload.title: Manoj's Paper Plane Flies Farthest

payload.passage: The two teams were tied at the end of the cricket match. It was time for a special last ball to decide. Manav stood ready with the bat in his hands. He hit the ball for two runs and won the game.
payload.title: Manav wins the tied cricket match
decoys: He hit the ball for two runs
A close match is thrilling to watch

payload.passage: Sneha noticed many books had no proper labels. She offered to help the librarian sort and label them. Together they marked each book with its right number. Now children could find any book quickly and easily.
payload.title: Sneha helps label the library books

payload.passage: Vihaan kept forgetting to return his library books on time. The librarian gently showed him how to use a bookmark with the due date. After that, Vihaan returned every book on the right day. He felt proud to be a careful reader.
payload.title: Vihaan learns to return books on time
decoys: The librarian gave him a bookmark.

payload.passage: Sneha buried her brother's feet in the warm sand. She piled the sand high until only his toes showed. He wiggled free with a laugh, sending sand flying. They both rolled in the sand and giggled for a long time.
payload.title: Burying Feet in the Sand

payload.passage: The boys had a wheelbarrow race on the soft grass. One boy held his friend's legs while the friend walked on his hands. Many pairs tumbled and laughed in a heap. One steady pair reached the line and won.
payload.title: A steady pair wins the wheelbarrow race
decoys: One boy held his friend's legs.

payload.passage: Rohit took part in the obstacle-and-balance game on field day. He walked a low beam and crawled through a tunnel. He hopped between hoops without a single slip. Rohit finished first and lifted the bright cup.
payload.title: Rohit Wins the Balance Game

payload.passage: Ravi watched the kangaroos hop around their grassy field at the zoo. They jumped on their strong back legs and balanced with their tails. One mother kangaroo had a baby peeking out from her pouch. Ravi thought the bouncing animals were the funniest of all.
payload.title: Kangaroos Hop at the Zoo
decoys: A baby peeked from the pouch.

payload.passage: The school held a swap-and-read morning before the holidays. Children brought a book they no longer needed. They traded with friends to find a fresh holiday read. Everyone went on break with an exciting new story to enjoy.
payload.title: A swap-and-read morning before holidays

payload.passage: Rohan was new to taking the bus to school alone. His mother taught him which stop to get down at. On the first day he watched the stops carefully. He got off at the right place and felt very proud.
payload.title: Rohan learns to take the bus alone
decoys: His mother taught him the stop.

payload.passage: The bus journey home was during a heavy thunderstorm. Rain lashed the windows and lightning flashed outside. The driver drove slowly and kept everyone calm. They reached home safely, glad to be out of the storm.
payload.title: The bus drives home through a storm

payload.passage: The fair had a stall where you could win goldfish. Children threw small balls into little bowls of water. If a ball landed in a bowl, they won a fish. Aarav tried hard but his ball missed every time.
payload.title: The Goldfish Game at the Fair

payload.passage: Reshma joined the storytelling competition at school. She told a funny tale about a clever crow and a fox. She used different voices for each animal in her story. The audience laughed so hard that Reshma won the first place.
payload.title: Reshma Wins the Storytelling Contest
decoys: Her story had a clever crow.

payload.passage: A zoo guide took the children on a short walk. She told them never to tease or feed the animals. She said loud noises can scare the animals and make them sad. The children promised to be quiet and kind during their visit.
payload.title: Zoo Rules Keep Animals Safe
decoys: The guide took them on a walk.

payload.passage: The whole class boarded a special train for the trip. They had a full coach just for their school. The teachers counted everyone before the train moved. The children sang and clapped as the journey began.
payload.title: The class boards a special school train

payload.passage: Vikram visited his uncle who worked on a tea estate. They walked up the green hills covered with bushes. His uncle showed him how the leaves are picked. Vikram drank fresh tea and loved the cool hill air.
payload.title: Vikram Visits the Tea Estate

payload.passage: Ananya likes to colour in her big drawing book. She fills the shapes with bright crayons and pencils. She is careful to stay inside the lines. Ananya feels happy looking at each finished page of colour.
payload.title: Ananya's Hobby of Colouring

payload.passage: The bus took the children up a winding mountain road. The driver turned the wheel carefully at every bend. The children looked down at the deep green valleys. They held the rails tight and enjoyed the ride.
payload.title: The bus winds up the mountain road

payload.passage: It was a cold morning and a kitten sat shivering on the gate. Its fur was wet and it cried softly. Aarush brought a warm cloth and a saucer of milk. The kitten curled up warm and stopped crying.
payload.title: Aarush cares for a cold kitten
decoys: He brought a saucer of milk
Small animals need warmth and care

payload.passage: A magician put on a show at the fair. He pulled a rabbit out of an empty hat and made coins disappear. The children gasped and could not guess how he did it. Diya thought the magician was the cleverest man at the fair.
payload.title: The Magician's Show at the Fair
decoys: He pulled a rabbit from a hat.

payload.passage: On sports day, a boy from another class hurt his ankle and could not walk. Mohan offered his shoulder for support at once. He helped the boy reach the shaded tent for rest. The teachers thanked Mohan for his quick kindness.
payload.title: Mohan helps an injured boy on sports day
decoys: The boy hurt his ankle badly
He helped him reach the shaded tent
Kindness should be shown to everyone

payload.passage: Tarun could not skip the rope even once at first. The rope kept hitting his feet and he tripped. He practised every day in his backyard. After two weeks, he could skip a hundred times without stopping.
payload.title: Tarun learns to skip the rope
decoys: The rope kept hitting his feet

payload.passage: Ravi visited a museum filled with old toys. There were wooden dolls, tin cars, and spinning tops. A board said children played with these toys long ago. Ravi thought it was funny how toys had changed over time.
payload.title: Old Toys at the Museum

payload.passage: Ananya tried the ring toss game at the fair. She had to throw rings onto rows of bottles. On her last try, a ring landed neatly around a bottle. The man at the stall handed her a small teddy as a prize.
payload.title: Ananya Wins at the Ring Toss

payload.passage: Vikram saw the hippo for the first time at the zoo. The big animal stayed in the water with only its eyes showing. When it opened its huge mouth, everyone gasped. Vikram learned that hippos love to spend the day in water.
payload.title: The Hippo Loves the Water
decoys: The hippo opened its huge mouth.
The zoo is a fun place.

payload.passage: Anaya watched the sunset from the window of the moving train. The sky turned orange, pink, and then soft purple. The fields outside grew dark and quiet. She felt the gentle journey was the loveliest ride of all.
payload.title: Anaya watches the sunset from the train
decoys: The sky turned orange and pink.

payload.passage: Mehak felt sick on the winding hill bus ride. Her father told her to look at the far hills outside. Slowly the uneasy feeling went away as she gazed out. By the end she was pointing happily at the green peaks.
payload.title: Mehak feels better on the hill bus
decoys: She gazed at the far hills.

payload.passage: Aditi stayed with her grandparents who had a vegetable plot. Each evening they picked beans, gourds, and chillies. Granny cooked the fresh vegetables for dinner. Aditi loved eating what they picked from the plot.
payload.title: Fresh Vegetables From Granny's Plot

payload.passage: Ravi enjoys making a model rocket from a bottle. He tapes paper fins around the bottom. He draws a sharp paper cone for the top. Ravi pretends his bottle rocket blasts off into space.
payload.title: Ravi Builds a Model Rocket

payload.passage: An old lady stood at the busy road and was afraid to cross. The cars and bikes went past very fast. Yash gently held her arm and raised his hand to the traffic. He walked her safely to the other side.
payload.title: Yash helps an old lady cross the road
decoys: The cars went past very fast
He raised his hand to the traffic
Helping elders is a great duty

payload.passage: Diya likes to weave little mats from coloured paper strips. She lays some strips down and threads others across. The strips lock together into a neat pattern. Diya uses her paper mats under her small flower pots.
payload.title: Diya Weaves Paper Mats

payload.passage: Ravi has taken up the hobby of growing plants. He has small pots of mint, money plant, and a tiny rose. Every morning he waters them and checks for new leaves. Ravi feels happy each time a fresh bud appears.
payload.title: Ravi's Hobby of Growing Plants
decoys: He has a pot of mint.

payload.passage: A young tree near the school had bent in the strong wind. It looked like it would fall over soon. Some students tied it to a wooden stick for support. The tree slowly grew straight and tall again.
payload.title: Students help a bent young tree stand
decoys: The tree bent in the wind
They tied it to a stick
Caring for trees is good for all

payload.passage: Madhu noticed that the class fish tank was very dirty. The water had turned cloudy and green. She told the teacher and offered to clean it. Together they changed the water and the fish swam happily.
payload.title: Madhu helps clean the class fish tank
decoys: Caring for pets is a kind duty

payload.passage: The class started a reading wall at the back of the room. Every time a child finished a book, they added a paper leaf. Slowly the bare wall grew into a green, leafy tree. The reading tree showed how much the whole class loved books.
payload.title: The class grows a reading tree

payload.passage: Meera visited the small zoo pond full of pink flamingos. The tall birds stood on one thin leg in the shallow water. They dipped their curved beaks to find food. Meera wondered how they balanced so well on just one leg.
payload.title: Flamingos at the Zoo Pond

payload.passage: Our class made a model showing the parts of a flower. We used coloured paper for the petals and leaves. We labelled the stem, the root, and the bud. Our teacher said it helped everyone learn about plants.
payload.title: A Class Model of a Flower

payload.passage: Tara enjoys making puppets dance on strings. She ties thread to a little wooden cross. The puppet moves its arms and legs when she pulls. Tara puts on small puppet shows for her family at night.
payload.title: Tara's String Puppet Shows
decoys: She ties thread to a cross.

payload.passage: Sushma stayed with her aunt who taught her to sew. They threaded bright cloth and stitched small bags. Aunt showed her how to make neat little stitches. Sushma was proud of the first bag she sewed herself.
payload.title: Sushma Learns to Sew at Aunt's

payload.passage: Two teams played a relay with water in spoons. They had to carry water without spilling it. Sonal's team moved carefully and lost the least water. They filled their bottle first and won the game.
payload.title: Sonal's team wins the water relay

payload.passage: Aman volunteered to read stories to the youngest class. He chose a book with big pictures and a happy ending. He used funny voices that made the little ones laugh. The children begged him to come and read again soon.
payload.title: Aman reads stories to little children
decoys: He chose a book with pictures.

payload.passage: Sara made a new friend on the long train journey. They sat together and shared their colouring books. They laughed and talked until the trip ended. They promised to write letters to each other.
payload.title: Sara makes a friend on the train

payload.passage: On Sunday, a group of friends went for a long cycle ride. They rode past green fields and a small river. The sun was warm and the wind felt cool on their faces. Everyone enjoyed the ride and reached home tired but happy.
payload.title: Friends enjoy a long cycle ride

payload.passage: Geeta stayed with her grandmother who loved old songs. Each evening granny hummed tunes from her youth. Geeta tried to learn the words and sing along. Geeta treasured the gentle songs her granny shared.
payload.title: Singing Old Songs With Granny

payload.passage: The water relay race was the wettest event of all. Children ran with cups of water to fill a bucket. Most of the water spilled along the way. The team that ran carefully filled their bucket first.
payload.title: A careful team wins the water relay

payload.passage: The early bus carried sleepy workers and students. Some dozed while others read the morning paper. The streets outside were still quiet and grey. Slowly the city woke as the bus moved along.
payload.title: The early bus carries sleepy travellers
decoys: The streets were quiet and grey.

payload.passage: Grandfather's spectacles fell behind the heavy almirah. He could not see well without them. Little Ria crawled into the small gap and reached them. Grandfather wore his glasses and read his book again.
payload.title: Ria finds grandfather's lost spectacles
decoys: The glasses fell behind the almirah

payload.passage: The neighbours' children met to make a big pot of vegetable stew together. Each child brought one vegetable from their own kitchen. They washed and cut everything before adding it to the bubbling pot. The shared stew tasted better because so many friends had helped to make it.
payload.title: Neighbours' children make a shared stew
decoys: They added them to a bubbling pot.

payload.passage: Anjali loves to make her own jigsaw from a photo. She glues a printed photo onto thick card. She cuts it into wavy little pieces. Anjali enjoys putting her photo puzzle back together.
payload.title: Anjali Makes a Photo Jigsaw
decoys: She glues a photo on card.

payload.passage: A boy's kite string got cut and the kite flew away. He looked sad as it floated over the houses. His friend gave him his own spare kite at once. Together they ran and flew it in the wind.
payload.title: A boy shares his spare kite

payload.passage: Sneha loved the music stall at the corner of the market. It sold small drums, flutes, and shiny bells. The seller played a tune to show how they sounded. Sneha begged her mother for the little flute, and she got it.
payload.title: Sneha's Flute from the Music Stall

payload.passage: Tara learned to make lemon juice on a hot afternoon. She squeezed the lemons and added cold water and sugar. Her little brother stirred the glass until the sugar melted. The cool drink made the warm day feel much better.
payload.title: Tara makes cool lemon juice

payload.passage: Two little children were stuck inside a locked car in the heat. They cried and banged on the window. A passing watchman called for help right away. The children were freed and given cool water.
payload.title: A watchman saves two trapped children

payload.passage: Veer loved the room full of old paintings. Each picture showed people, places, or animals from long ago. The colours had faded but the pictures were still beautiful. Veer wondered who had painted them so many years before.
payload.title: Old Paintings at the Museum

payload.passage: Renu was given a small kitten with a sore eye. She bathed the eye gently with warm water daily. She fed the kitten and kept it warm and calm. In time, the kitten's eye healed and it grew lively.
payload.title: Renu Heals Her Kitten's Sore Eye

payload.passage: Vivaan trained for months to take part in the school race. He ran around the ground before lessons every day. His legs grew stronger and his speed improved steadily. On the big day, his hard work earned him a shiny medal.
payload.title: Vivaan's hard work earns a medal

payload.passage: Mira and her friends ran a cooking stall at the school fete. They sold small bowls of vegetable noodles they had made. Customers lined up because the noodles smelled so good. The stall earned money for new sports equipment.
payload.title: Friends run a cooking stall at the fete
decoys: They sold bowls of vegetable noodles.
Customers lined up at the stall.

payload.passage: Manya planted a row of soft lettuce in the garden. She watered it each morning and shaded it from harsh sun. She watched the green leaves grow broad and crisp. Soon Manya picked fresh lettuce for the family salad.
payload.title: Manya Grows Crisp Lettuce
decoys: She shaded it from the sun.

payload.passage: Divya stayed with her grandmother who kept a parrot. The green parrot could say hello in a funny voice. Granny taught Divya how to feed it slices of fruit. Divya loved chatting with granny's clever little parrot.
payload.title: Granny's Clever Talking Parrot

payload.passage: Vivaan and his father made a fluffy egg curry on Sunday. They boiled the eggs and made a smooth onion gravy. Vivaan stirred the pot while his father added the spices. The warm curry tasted great with hot, soft bread.
payload.title: Vivaan and father make egg curry

payload.passage: Vidya visited her cousin who had a sandpit in the yard. They built castles, dug tunnels, and shaped little roads. They added toy cars to drive along the tracks. Vidya thought the sandpit play was the best fun.
payload.title: Sandpit Play at Cousin's Yard

payload.passage: The sack race made the whole crowd laugh out loud. Children hopped forward inside big cloth sacks. Some fell over and rolled in the soft grass. A boy who hopped steadily reached the line and won.
payload.title: A boy hops to win the sack race

payload.passage: The race for the youngest children was full of giggles. Many ran the wrong way or stopped to wave at parents. The teachers laughed and gently guided them along. In the end, every little runner got a small prize.
payload.title: Little children enjoy their fun race

payload.passage: Divya joined the poetry-writing competition at school. She wrote a short poem about a falling autumn leaf. Her words painted a clear picture in the mind. The judges chose Divya's gentle poem as the best.
payload.title: Divya's Autumn Poem Wins

payload.passage: Sara was new to the bus route and got off at the wrong stop. She looked lost and started to panic. An older girl spotted her and helped her find the way home. Sara thanked her and reached safely.
payload.title: An older girl helps lost Sara reach home
decoys: Sara got off at the wrong stop

payload.passage: Aditya bought a map at the zoo gate. He used it to find his way to each animal house. The map showed where the food stall and the toilets were too. With the map, Aditya never got lost at the big zoo.
payload.title: Using a Map at the Zoo
decoys: The map showed the food stall.
Aditya bought the map at the gate.

payload.passage: The school celebrated Book Week with many fun activities. Children dressed as story characters and shared their favourite tales. The library held a quiz about famous books. By the end of the week, almost everyone had borrowed a new book to read.
payload.title: The school celebrates Book Week

payload.passage: Diya found a big, smooth pebble shaped like a heart. She turned it over and over in her hands. She decided to keep it as a special beach treasure. Diya put the heart pebble safely in her little bag.
payload.title: Diya's Heart-Shaped Pebble
decoys: She put it in her bag.

payload.passage: The girls held a baking afternoon to learn from Sana's mother. She showed them how to measure flour and sugar correctly. They each made a small batch of soft jam tarts. By teatime the kitchen was full of warm tarts and happy chatter.
payload.title: The girls learn baking from Sana's mother

payload.passage: Karan enjoys baking small breads with his grandmother. They knead the dough and let it rise. They shape little rolls and bake them golden. Karan loves the smell of fresh bread filling the kitchen.
payload.title: Karan Bakes Bread with Grandmother

payload.passage: Pooja went to her cousin's home for the wedding. The house was full of music, lights, and happy guests. She wore a new dress and danced with all her cousins. Pooja had never been to such a joyful family event.
payload.title: Pooja Dances at the Family Wedding

payload.passage: The cycle race wound through the quiet park paths. Children pedalled fast around the trees and over small bridges. One boy kept a steady speed instead of rushing. His careful pace helped him win the race.
payload.title: A steady rider wins the park cycle race
decoys: One boy kept a steady speed.

payload.passage: During the picnic, a boy dropped his food on the grass. He had nothing left to eat and looked upset. Three friends each shared a bit of their own food. Soon the boy had a full plate and a big smile.
payload.title: Friends share food with a sad boy
decoys: He had a full plate again

payload.passage: Roshni looked after a noisy parrot that screeched a lot. She gave it toys and talked to it gently. She kept it busy so it would not feel bored. Over time, the parrot grew calmer and chirped softly.
payload.title: Roshni Calms Her Noisy Parrot

payload.passage: Aarav saw a crab on the wet sand near the water. It had a hard shell and ran sideways very fast. When Aarav came close, the crab hid inside a small hole. He waited quietly, hoping it would come out again.
payload.title: A Crab on the Beach Sand
decoys: It hid in a small hole.

payload.passage: The children helped paint a colourful mural in the library. They drew open books with little birds flying out. The bright wall made the room feel warm and happy. Now everyone wanted to sit and read near it.
payload.title: Children paint a mural in the library

payload.passage: Pankaj visited his grandfather who flew big kites. From the rooftop they sent kites high into the sky. Grandfather taught Pankaj how to tug the string. Pankaj loved the long kite-flying evenings with granddad.
payload.title: Flying Kites With Grandfather

payload.passage: Priya and her brother made sandwiches for the school picnic. They spread butter on the bread and added cucumber slices. Then they wrapped each sandwich in clean paper. Their tasty sandwiches were the first to be eaten at the picnic.
payload.title: Priya and her brother make picnic sandwiches
decoys: They added cucumber slices to the bread.
They wrapped each sandwich in paper.

payload.passage: Sameer planted a small guava sapling in the yard. He watered it and kept the weeds away. He waited many seasons as it slowly grew. After years, the little sapling gave sweet guavas.
payload.title: Sameer Grows a Guava Tree

payload.passage: Shalu loved gymnastics and practised her cartwheels daily. At first she wobbled and fell on the soft mat. She kept trying until her cartwheels were smooth. At the show, everyone clapped for her perfect turns.
payload.title: Shalu masters her cartwheels
decoys: She wobbled and fell at first

payload.passage: A little girl could not open her heavy school gate alone. She pushed with all her tiny strength. A kind senior boy opened it wide for her. She walked in and thanked him sweetly.
payload.title: A senior boy opens the gate
decoys: Older students can help the young

payload.passage: Zara helped her father grill vegetables for the family barbecue. She brushed oil on slices of corn, capsicum, and onion. Her father turned them over the warm coals until they softened. The smoky vegetables made the garden dinner taste wonderful.
payload.title: Zara helps grill vegetables for the barbecue
decoys: She brushed oil on the corn.

payload.passage: It started to rain during the football match, and the field grew slippery. Many players slipped and fell in the mud. But the children laughed and kept playing happily. They said the muddy match was the most fun ever.
payload.title: Children enjoy the muddy football match
decoys: Many players fell in the mud
Rain can make games more fun

payload.passage: The class collected used books for a poor village library. Each child brought stories they had finished reading. They cleaned, sorted, and packed the books into boxes. They felt happy knowing other children would enjoy the stories too.
payload.title: The class gives books to a village library

payload.passage: Naveen was the slowest runner in his group last year. He decided to run every morning before school. Slowly his legs grew strong and his speed improved. This year he surprised everyone by winning his race.
payload.title: Naveen improves and wins his race
decoys: He ran every morning before school.

payload.passage: Meera looked after a small green parrot at home. She gave it fresh fruit and clean water each day. She talked to it softly so it would not feel lonely. Over time, the parrot learned to say Meera's name.
payload.title: Meera Cares for Her Parrot

payload.passage: Meera enjoys making collages from old magazines. She cuts out colourful pictures and bits of paper. She arranges them and glues them into a scene. Meera made a bright collage of a busy city for her wall.
payload.title: Meera Makes Paper Collages

payload.passage: Vikram enjoys building tracks for his toy cars. He joins the pieces into long loops and slopes. Then he lets the cars zoom around the bends. Vikram makes a new track shape almost every day.
payload.title: Vikram Builds Toy Car Tracks

payload.passage: The fruit stall at the market was bright and busy. There were yellow bananas, red apples, and sweet green grapes. Ananya picked the ripest mangoes for the family. The smell of fresh fruit filled the whole stall.
payload.title: Choosing Fruit at the Market

payload.passage: At night the fair lit up with hundreds of lights. Bulbs of red, blue, and yellow hung over every stall. The rides glowed and music played from all sides. Priya thought the lit-up fair looked like a piece of the night sky.
payload.title: The Fair Lit Up at Night
decoys: The bulbs were red and blue.

payload.passage: Two boys played a coin flicking game on the table. They had to flick a coin into a small cup. Imtiaz flicked with a steady hand and good aim. He got the most coins in and won.
payload.title: Imtiaz wins the coin flicking game
decoys: A steady hand wins the game

payload.passage: Ravindra took part in the shot-put throw on field day. He held the heavy ball close to his neck. With a strong push, he flung it far across the field. Ravindra's throw went the farthest and won the prize.
payload.title: Ravindra Wins the Shot-Put Throw

payload.passage: Dhruv was a fast bowler in the inter-school match. He bowled straight and quick at every batter. He took three wickets in just two overs. His brilliant bowling helped his school win the trophy.
payload.title: Dhruv's bowling wins the school trophy

payload.passage: Heavy rain flooded a poor family's small house. Their books and clothes got wet and ruined. The neighbours collected dry clothes and food to give them. The family felt grateful for the warm help.
payload.title: Neighbours help a flooded family
decoys: Neighbours support each other in trouble

payload.passage: Tara loves to build little boats from walnut shells. She melts a drop of wax inside each half shell. She stands a tiny paper sail in the wax. Tara floats her walnut boats in a bowl of water.
payload.title: Tara Makes Walnut Shell Boats
decoys: She stands a paper sail in wax.

payload.passage: The family set off on a long train journey to visit the mountains. They watched green fields slowly change into rolling hills. The children spotted waterfalls and tiny villages on the slopes. By evening the cool mountain air welcomed them at the station.
payload.title: The family travels by train to the mountains
decoys: They saw waterfalls on the slopes.

payload.passage: The little ones had a picture book day in the library. The teacher held up big books with bright pictures. The children pointed and named the animals they saw. They learned new words while having lots of fun.
payload.title: A picture book day for little ones

payload.passage: Diya likes to make soft toys from old cloth. She cuts the cloth and stuffs it with bits of wool. She sews button eyes and a smiling mouth. Diya has made a little bear and a floppy rabbit.
payload.title: Diya Makes Soft Toys

payload.passage: Our class made a model of a desert for the project. We laid yellow sand and added a tall cactus. We placed a camel and a few small tents. Visitors learned how plants and people live in deserts.
payload.title: A Class Model of a Desert

payload.passage: Priya found a face-painting stall at the fair. The artist painted bright flowers on each child's cheek. Priya chose a yellow butterfly and a tiny star. She looked in the mirror and loved her painted face.
payload.title: Getting Her Face Painted

payload.passage: Anaya wore a big hat to protect herself from the sun. Her mother put cream on her arms before they played. They drank lots of water to stay cool in the heat. Anaya knew that staying safe made the beach day even better.
payload.title: Staying Safe in the Beach Sun

payload.passage: A bird's wing got stuck in a thin plastic thread. It flapped on the ground unable to fly. Sneha carefully cut the thread away with scissors. The bird shook its wings and flew up to the sky.
payload.title: Sneha frees a trapped bird's wing
decoys: The bird flapped on the ground
It flew up to the sky
Freeing birds is a kind act

payload.passage: Aarush ran the relay's last leg for his team. His friends had given him a small lead to protect. He held his speed and watched the finish line. He crossed first and his team celebrated together.
payload.title: Aarush protects the lead in the relay
decoys: His friends gave him a lead.

payload.passage: During the match, Varun dropped an easy catch at first. His teammates looked a little upset. But Varun did not give up and stayed alert. In the next over, he took a brilliant flying catch.
payload.title: Varun makes up for his dropped catch
decoys: Never give up after a mistake

payload.passage: Aarav rode the slow boat ride around a little pond at the fair. The boats were shaped like big colourful swans. He pedalled gently to push his boat along. Aarav waved at the children waiting on the shore.
payload.title: The Swan Boat Ride at the Fair

payload.passage: Tara loves to paint pictures on the weekend. She sets out her brushes, colours, and a clean sheet of paper. Last Sunday she painted a green garden full of flowers. Painting makes Tara feel calm and very happy.
payload.title: Tara's Hobby of Painting

payload.passage: Tushar visited his cousin who built model planes. They glued the parts and painted them bright. They held them up and made them swoop and dive. Tushar loved making the little planes with his cousin.
payload.title: Building Model Planes With Cousin

payload.passage: The children played a balloon stamping game in the hall. Each child had a balloon tied to one ankle. They tried to stamp others' balloons while saving their own. Karan kept his balloon safe and won the game.
payload.title: Karan saves his balloon and wins

payload.passage: The whole class went to play in the big school field. They split into two teams for a relay game. Each child cheered loudly for their own team. In the end, both teams said it was great fun.
payload.title: The class enjoys a relay game together

payload.passage: Priya loves to make models of the planets. She rolls clay into balls of different sizes. She paints each one to look like a real planet. Priya hangs her clay planets in a row from her ceiling.
payload.title: Priya Makes Clay Planets
decoys: She hangs them from the ceiling.

payload.passage: Saira helped her mother make a colourful vegetable rice. They added peas, carrots, and corn to the cooking rice. The dish turned bright and looked very pretty. The family said the rainbow rice was both tasty and beautiful.
payload.title: Saira makes colourful vegetable rice

payload.passage: Mr. Sharma's gate was stuck and would not open. He pushed and pulled but it was too heavy. Two children passing by came and pushed it together. The gate finally opened and Mr. Sharma thanked them.
payload.title: Children help open the stuck gate
decoys: A little help goes a long way

payload.passage: Faizan took part in the chess match in the school club. He thought hard before he moved each piece. Slowly he trapped his rival's king on the board. Faizan won the game and shook hands with a smile.
payload.title: Faizan Wins the Chess Match
decoys: He shook hands at the end.

payload.passage: Diya loves to make little lanterns out of paper cups. She cuts slits down the sides of each cup. A small light inside makes the slits glow. Diya lines up her glowing cup lanterns along the shelf.
payload.title: Diya Makes Paper Cup Lanterns
decoys: She cuts slits in the cups.

payload.passage: The bus crossed a long bridge over a wide river. The children pressed their faces to the windows. Below them, small boats floated on the shining water. Everyone said it was the best part of the trip.
payload.title: The bus crosses a long river bridge

payload.passage: The egg-and-spoon race was the funniest event of the day. Children walked carefully so the egg would not fall. Many eggs rolled off and broke on the ground. The girl who balanced best reached the line and won.
payload.title: A careful girl wins the egg-and-spoon race

payload.passage: During the maths lesson, Tara dropped all her crayons on the floor. They scattered under the desks of many children. Without a word, three classmates bent down to help. Together they collected the crayons before the teacher returned.
payload.title: Classmates help Tara collect her crayons
decoys: Tara dropped her crayons on the floor
The crayons scattered under the desks
Helping a friend is always nice

payload.passage: The class plant pot cracked and the soil spilled out. The little plant lay on its side. Mira found a new pot and replanted it carefully. She watered it well and it stood green again.
payload.title: Mira replants the fallen class plant

payload.passage: Our group made a model of a hospital for the project. We built wards with little beds and a doctor's room. We showed nurses helping the sick people get better. Everyone said our hospital model was very neat.
payload.title: Our Model Hospital Project

payload.passage: On rainy days the library was the children's favourite place. They sat by the big window with their books. The rain tapped softly on the glass outside. Stories and gentle rain made the afternoon perfect.
payload.title: The library is best on rainy days
decoys: They sat by the big window.

payload.passage: Akash looked after a pet rabbit that was very shy. He moved slowly and spoke in a soft voice. He fed it greens and let it come to him. Over time, the shy rabbit hopped up to greet Akash.
payload.title: Akash Wins Over His Shy Rabbit

payload.passage: Tanvi made a fruit smoothie to share with her sleepy father. She blended banana, milk, and a spoon of oats. She poured it into two tall glasses. The thick smoothie woke her father up with its sweet taste.
payload.title: Tanvi makes a fruit smoothie to share
decoys: She poured it into tall glasses.
Fruit is good for the body.

payload.passage: Ishaan tried to make pancakes for the first time. His sister read the steps from a cookbook out loud. He mixed the batter and poured small rounds on the pan. The fluffy pancakes with honey made a happy Sunday breakfast.
payload.title: Ishaan makes pancakes for the first time
decoys: His sister read the steps aloud.
He poured small rounds on the pan.

payload.passage: Divya visited her cousins who lived by a wide field. They flew kites, played tag, and rolled down the grassy slope. The open field gave them so much room to run. Divya thought playing in the big field was wonderful.
payload.title: Playing in the Wide Open Field

payload.passage: Tanvi joined the library club to share her love of books. The members met each week to talk about their reading. They suggested new titles to one another every time. Tanvi made many friends who loved stories as much as she did.
payload.title: Tanvi makes friends at the library club

payload.passage: The children played a balloon race across the field. They had to push a balloon with a stick. Sahana kept her balloon moving in a straight line. She reached the finish first and won.
payload.title: Sahana wins the balloon push race

payload.passage: The train chugged through a long, dark tunnel. The children counted the seconds until it ended. When light burst in, they all cheered together. Then they spotted snowy mountains far in the distance.
payload.title: The train passes through a long tunnel

payload.passage: Veer wanted to learn how to make a thin omelette. His mother showed him how to beat the eggs well. She let him pour the egg into the warm pan himself. Veer flipped his first omelette and felt very proud.
payload.title: Veer learns to make an omelette
decoys: His mother showed him to beat the eggs.
He poured the egg into the pan.

payload.passage: The children played a tongue twister game during break. They had to say a funny line very fast. Megha said the tricky line without a single mistake. Everyone laughed and clapped for her win.
payload.title: Megha wins the tongue twister game

payload.passage: Ananya's team lost the first half of the netball match. During the break, they made a new plan together. In the second half they passed faster and aimed better. Their fresh plan helped them win in the end.
payload.title: A new plan wins the netball match
decoys: They passed faster after the break.

payload.passage: Yusuf visited his uncle who lived near a railway line. They sat on the wall and watched the trains roar by. His uncle named each kind of train and where it went. Yusuf could have watched the busy trains all day.
payload.title: Yusuf Watches the Trains Go By

payload.passage: A big cricket match was held between two colonies. The score was very close in the last over. Deepak took a sharp catch to end the innings. His team won the match by just one run.
payload.title: Deepak's catch wins the colony match
decoys: A good catch can win a match

payload.passage: A big tree had fallen across the village road after the storm. No cars or buses could pass through. All the men, women, and children came to help move it. Working together, they cleared the road by noon.
payload.title: Villagers clear the fallen tree together
decoys: A tree fell across the road
They cleared the road by noon

payload.passage: Ravi enjoys making little kites from leaves and sticks. He finds a big strong leaf in the garden. He ties it to a thin stick with a long thread. Ravi loves running with his leaf kite in the breeze.
payload.title: Ravi Makes Kites from Leaves
decoys: He uses a big strong leaf.

payload.passage: Priya visited a museum about old machines. She saw the first telephones, radios, and big cameras. A guide showed how a hand-crank machine once worked. Priya could not believe people used such heavy things before.
payload.title: Old Machines at the Museum
decoys: A guide turned a hand crank.

payload.passage: Sneha loves to draw with chalk on the courtyard floor. She draws hopscotch squares and big bright flowers. Her friends join in to add their own pictures. The whole floor becomes a colourful chalk garden.
payload.title: Sneha Draws with Chalk Outside

payload.passage: The toy stall at the market drew a crowd of children. There were spinning tops, kites, and small wooden cars. Priya stared at a bright red kite for a long time. Her mother smiled and bought it for her as a treat.
payload.title: Priya's New Kite from the Market

payload.passage: Saanvi was the youngest swimmer in the relay team. The older girls were not sure she could keep up. But she had practised her strokes all summer long. Her fast swim surprised everyone and helped the team win the race.
payload.title: Young Saanvi surprises in the relay

payload.passage: A boy on the train could not lift his bag to the top rack. It was too heavy for his small arms. A kind uncle near him lifted it up easily. The boy thanked the uncle with a happy smile.
payload.title: An uncle helps a boy lift his bag
decoys: The boy gave a happy smile

payload.passage: Vidya kept two goldfish that liked to chase. She gave them a big tank with room to swim. She fed them well and kept the water fresh. Over the months, the goldfish grew lively and bright.
payload.title: Vidya's Two Chasing Goldfish
decoys: She gave them a big tank.

payload.passage: A small boy in the bus was scared of the loud thunder. He hid his face and started to cry. Sumit sat next to him and told him a funny story. The boy laughed and forgot all about the storm.
payload.title: Sumit comforts a scared little boy
decoys: The boy was scared of thunder
Sumit told him a funny story
A friend can chase away fear

payload.passage: Aarav enjoys collecting leaves of different shapes. He presses them flat and sticks them in a book. He writes the name of each tree beside its leaf. Aarav's leaf book is growing bigger every season.
payload.title: Aarav Collects Different Leaves

payload.passage: Ishaan helped his little sister down the bus steps. The step was high and she was afraid to jump. He held her hand and counted to three. She hopped down safely and gave him a big smile.
payload.title: Ishaan helps his sister off the bus

payload.passage: The class fan stopped working on a very hot day. The children sat sweating and could not focus. A boy fanned the youngest child with a notebook. Soon a worker came and repaired the fan.
payload.title: A boy fans a younger child
decoys: Caring for others in heat is kind

payload.passage: Nikita planted a sweet pea by the garden fence. She watered it and let the vine climb the wire. She watched the tiny buds slowly open up. After weeks, the fence was full of soft, sweet flowers.
payload.title: Nikita Grows Sweet Peas

payload.passage: Anaya entered the long jump for the very first time. She watched the older girls leap far into the sandpit. When her turn came, she ran fast and jumped with all her power. Her brave jump won her a place on the school team.
payload.title: Anaya earns a place in long jump
decoys: She watched the older girls leap.

payload.passage: Rudra fell behind in the cycle race after a slow start. He did not lose heart and kept pedalling hard. He passed two riders on the last long stretch. His steady effort brought him to a proud third place.
payload.title: Rudra fights back in the cycle race

payload.passage: The whole family cooked dinner together before the guests came. Mother boiled the rice, Father fried the vegetables, and the children set the table. Everyone did one small job, so the work was quick. By six o'clock the tasty dinner was fully ready.
payload.title: The family cooks dinner together

payload.passage: Rohan went paddling in the shallow water at the beach. He rolled up his shorts and walked in slowly. Tiny fish darted around his feet in the clear water. Rohan tried to catch one but they were far too quick.
payload.title: Paddling in the Shallow Water
decoys: The sea is full of fish.

payload.passage: During the football match, the ball went out near Veena. The referee did not see who touched it last. Veena honestly said the ball had touched her foot. The teacher praised her for telling the truth.
payload.title: Veena tells the truth during the match

payload.passage: The market had a corner with many kinds of nuts. There were almonds, cashews, and small brown walnuts. Sara watched the seller weigh them on a small scale. Her mother bought a mix to add to the evening sweets.
payload.title: The Nut Stall at the Market

payload.passage: Kabir watched the seals at the zoo show off in the water. They clapped their flippers and balanced balls on their noses. A keeper threw fish for them to catch in the air. Kabir clapped along with the playful, clever seals.
payload.title: The Clever Seals at the Zoo
decoys: They balanced balls on their noses.

payload.passage: Rohan went to the morning market while it was still cool. The sellers were just setting out their fresh goods. A baker put hot bread on his stall and the smell filled the air. Rohan bought a warm loaf for the family breakfast.
