payload.title: The Market in the Early Morning

payload.passage: The school held a long-distance race around the park. Many children ran fast and got tired early. Vinay kept a slow, steady pace the whole way. He passed the tired runners and won the race.
payload.title: Steady Vinay wins the long race

payload.passage: A small puppy followed the school children every day. One day it looked thin and very hungry. The children saved a little food from their tiffins. They fed the puppy together and it grew strong.
payload.title: Children feed a hungry school puppy
decoys: Caring for strays is a good habit

payload.passage: Anaya stayed at her grandmother's house full of plants. Granny had pots of herbs lined up on the wall. She taught Anaya the name and smell of each one. Anaya loved walking among granny's green and leafy plants.
payload.title: Granny's House Full of Plants

payload.passage: The newspaper man fell off his bicycle on the wet road. His papers scattered all over the ground. A boy and his sister rushed to gather them up. They helped him stack the papers and ride on.
payload.title: Children help the fallen newspaper man

payload.passage: The children helped Grandmother make sweets for the festival. They rolled the dough into small balls with their hands. Grandmother dipped each ball into warm sugar syrup. The kitchen was full of laughter and sweet smells all day.
payload.title: Children help make festival sweets
decoys: They rolled the dough into balls.

payload.passage: Aditya likes to grow a small herb pot on the window. He planted coriander and watered it every day. Soon green leaves filled the little pot. Aditya was happy when his mother used his herbs in cooking.
payload.title: Aditya Grows a Herb Pot

payload.passage: Shalini planted a small chrysanthemum in a pot. She watered it and kept it in the gentle sun. She waited as tight buds formed on the tips. Soon the pot was full of round, frilly flowers.
payload.title: Shalini Grows Frilly Chrysanthemums
decoys: She kept it in the sun.

payload.passage: Ananya enjoys making her own greeting beads. She rolls bits of coloured paper into tight tubes. She glues them and threads them onto string. Ananya wears the paper beads she made herself.
payload.title: Ananya Makes Paper Beads

payload.passage: The museum had a room about space and the stars. Ananya saw models of planets hanging from the ceiling. A small film showed how rockets fly into space. She decided she wanted to learn much more about the sky.
payload.title: The Space Room at the Museum
decoys: Planet models hung from the ceiling.

payload.passage: The football rolled towards the goal in the final minute. Both teams had no goals so far. Neeraj ran fast, kicked the ball, and scored. His school won the match by one goal.
payload.title: Neeraj scores the winning goal
decoys: He kicked in the final minute

payload.passage: On Sunday Riya and her mother baked a cake together. Riya cracked the eggs while her mother poured the flour. They mixed everything until it was soft and smooth. When the warm cake came out, the whole kitchen smelled lovely.
payload.title: Riya and her mother bake a cake
decoys: Riya cracked the eggs into the bowl.
Her mother poured the flour in.

payload.passage: The children played a fun shadow tag in the evening sun. One had to step on another's shadow to tag. Sahana kept her shadow away from the chaser. She stayed safe and won the game.
payload.title: Sahana wins the shadow tag game

payload.passage: The double-decker bus delighted the visiting children. They hurried up the steps to grab the top front seats. From there they could see far across the busy city. The high view made the whole trip feel like an adventure.
payload.title: Children enjoy the double-decker bus view

payload.passage: Meera went to her grandmother's house for the festival. Her grandmother taught her to make a paper lantern. Together they hung lanterns all around the doorway. Meera was proud to help decorate granny's home.
payload.title: Meera Makes Lanterns With Granny
decoys: They hung them at the door.

payload.passage: Kabir stayed at his grandparents' farm for the holidays. He woke to the crow of the rooster each morning. He helped collect eggs from the clucking hens. Kabir felt like a real farmer during his happy stay.
payload.title: Kabir Feels Like a Farmer

payload.passage: Anaya loves to learn new songs on her toy keyboard. She presses the keys to find the right notes. She practises the same tune over and over. Anaya can now play a whole nursery song by herself.
payload.title: Anaya Learns the Toy Keyboard

payload.passage: On sports day, Vinay was the slowest in the running race. But he never missed his morning practice runs. Week after week he grew faster and stronger. This year, he came second in the same race.
payload.title: Vinay improves his race timing

payload.passage: Imran took part in the maths competition on Friday. He solved sums quickly with a calm, sharp mind. He checked each answer twice before moving on. Imran scored the most points and lifted the trophy high.
payload.title: Imran Wins the Maths Competition

payload.passage: The toy train at the fair was the children's favourite ride. It chugged slowly around a track full of lights. It puffed over a little bridge and rang a cheerful bell. The short ride made the whole fair day even more special.
payload.title: Children ride the toy train at the fair

payload.passage: Mohit visited his uncle who lived near a forest. They walked along the edge and saw deer and birds. His uncle taught him to stay quiet and watch. Mohit felt lucky to see the gentle forest animals.
payload.title: Mohit Watches Forest Animals

payload.passage: Kho-kho is a fast game played in two teams. Payal sat in the line and waited for her chance to chase. When her turn came, she ran and tagged the runner quickly. Her speed helped her team win the match.
payload.title: Payal's speed helps win the kho-kho match
decoys: She sat in the line first

payload.passage: The spice corner of the market smelled wonderful. There were bags of yellow turmeric, red chilli, and brown cinnamon. The seller scooped each spice with a little spoon. Mother bought what she needed for the week's cooking.
payload.title: The Spice Corner at the Market
decoys: There were bags of red chilli.
The seller used a little spoon.

payload.passage: Sneha enjoys learning to draw birds step by step. She starts with a circle and adds a beak. Slowly the bird takes shape on her paper. Sneha is proud that her birds look better every week.
payload.title: Sneha Learns to Draw Birds

payload.passage: Yusuf kept a pet pigeon that he raised from a chick. He fed it grain and let it fly each day. He always left the cage open so it could return. Over time, the pigeon always came back home to Yusuf.
payload.title: Yusuf's Pigeon Always Returns Home

payload.passage: Imran stayed with his grandfather, who tended a small pond. Lotus flowers floated on the still green water. Grandfather showed Imran the fish darting below. Imran loved the calm hours spent by the lotus pond.
payload.title: By the Lotus Pond With Grandfather

payload.passage: Aditya likes to take photos with his father's old camera. He looks for birds, flowers, and funny clouds. He clicks a picture whenever something catches his eye. Aditya hopes to fill a whole album with his best photos.
payload.title: Aditya's Hobby of Taking Photos
decoys: He looks for birds and flowers.

payload.passage: A man at the fair could guess your weight. People stood on his scale while he made a clever guess. If he got it wrong, you won a small toy. Meera giggled when the man guessed her weight almost right.
payload.title: The Weight-Guessing Game at the Fair
decoys: A wrong guess won a toy.

payload.passage: The school garden had become dry and full of weeds. The children decided to make it green again. Some pulled the weeds while others watered the plants. By the weekend the garden was full of colourful flowers.
payload.title: Children bring the school garden back to life
decoys: The garden was full of weeds

payload.passage: Anaya helped her father make hot soup on a rainy evening. She washed the vegetables while he chopped them small. They let the soup bubble slowly on the stove. The warm soup was perfect for the cold, wet weather outside.
payload.title: Anaya helps make soup on a rainy day

payload.passage: The students cooked a simple meal for a class project. Each group made one dish, from rice to salad. They learned to keep the kitchen clean while they worked. At lunch they shared all the dishes at one long table.
payload.title: Students cook a class meal together

payload.passage: A girl in class spilled water all over her drawing. She had worked hard and now looked sad. Her friends quickly gave her fresh paper and crayons. She drew a new picture even better than before.
payload.title: Friends help a girl after a spill
decoys: She spilled water on her drawing
Friends turn a bad day good

payload.passage: Our class made a chart about different jobs people do. We drew a doctor, a farmer, a teacher, and a pilot. Under each one we wrote how that worker helps us. Our chart taught the school to thank all kinds of workers.
payload.title: A Class Chart About Helpful Jobs

payload.passage: Vikram was given a small tortoise to mind. He fed it leafy greens and a bit of fruit. He made a cosy box with a little water dish. As months went by, Vikram's tortoise slowly grew bigger.
payload.title: Vikram Minds a Little Tortoise

payload.passage: Two friends had a balloon keepy-uppy game indoors. They had to keep the balloon from touching the floor. Esha tapped it up gently again and again. Her balloon stayed up the longest and she won.
payload.title: Esha keeps the balloon up the longest
decoys: They kept it off the floor

payload.passage: A new bat and ball were given to the class for games. Some children wanted to keep them for themselves. But the captain said everyone must get a chance. They made a fair turn list and all played happily.
payload.title: The class shares new sports gear fairly

payload.passage: The family caught the last bus home after a long day. The bus was quiet and the children were sleepy. Mother told a soft story to keep them awake. They reached their stop just before everyone dozed off.
payload.title: The family catches the last bus home

payload.passage: Rakesh planted a small neem tree near the gate. He watered it and put a stick to hold it straight. He pulled out the weeds that grew around it. After a year, the neem tree gave cool, leafy shade.
payload.title: Rakesh Grows a Neem Tree
decoys: He used a stick to support it.

payload.passage: Rohan went to his cousin's house for the long weekend. The two boys built a fort from blankets and chairs. They played inside it and told stories with a torch. Rohan thought the blanket fort was the best part of his stay.
payload.title: Rohan Builds a Fort at His Cousin's

payload.passage: Tina went to her grandparents' house for the festival. Granny lit small lamps along the windowsill. Grandfather hung paper streamers across the door. Tina loved how the whole house glowed for the festival.
payload.title: The House Glows for the Festival

payload.passage: Veer loved collecting shells along the shore. He walked slowly and picked up shells of every shape. Some were curled, some flat, and some had pretty stripes. By the end Veer had a whole bucket of shiny shells.
payload.title: Veer Collects Shells at the Beach

payload.passage: On the train, Anaya read her book the whole way. The gentle rocking made the story even nicer. She finished the last page just as they arrived. The journey and the book ended together perfectly.
payload.title: Anaya finishes her book on the train

payload.passage: Riya visited a museum filled with old musical instruments. There were big drums, long horns, and tiny bells. A guide played a note on an old stringed instrument. Riya was surprised how sweet the very old music sounded.
payload.title: Old Instruments at the Museum

payload.passage: Seema visited her cousin who had a small drum set. They took turns tapping out funny beats. They made up a song with claps and drumming. Seema thought making music with her cousin was great fun.
payload.title: Seema Makes Music With Her Cousin

payload.passage: Nikita stayed with her grandmother near a big orchard. They walked under trees full of apples and pears. Granny taught her which fruit was ripe to pick. Nikita filled her basket in the lovely fruit orchard.
payload.title: Nikita Visits the Fruit Orchard

payload.passage: Aditi looked after a pet rabbit that liked to dig. She gave it a sandy corner to dig in safely. She fed it greens and kept its hutch clean. Over time, the rabbit grew calm and let her stroke it.
payload.title: Aditi's Rabbit That Loves to Dig
decoys: She gave it a sandy corner.

payload.passage: Naina kept a tank of bright little fish at home. She fed them, cleaned the glass, and changed the water. She added a green plant for them to hide in. Over time, her fish grew lively and full of colour.
payload.title: Naina Cares for Her Fish Tank

payload.passage: Sneha was given a small puppy on her birthday. She fed it, walked it, and brushed its soft fur. She taught it to sit and to come when called. Day by day, Sneha and her puppy became best friends.
payload.title: Sneha and Her New Puppy

payload.passage: Aarav found a room about the human body at the museum. There was a big model showing bones and the heart. A screen let him press buttons to learn more. Aarav was amazed at how cleverly the body is made.
payload.title: Learning About the Body
decoys: He pressed buttons on a screen.

payload.passage: Aditya has a hobby of building paper houses. He draws windows and doors before he folds. He even adds tiny paper furniture inside. Aditya is slowly making a whole paper village on his desk.
payload.title: Aditya Builds a Paper Village

payload.passage: The express train sped past the small countryside stations. It did not stop until it reached the big city. The children watched the world rush by in a blur. They arrived quickly, amazed at how fast the journey had been.
payload.title: An express train speeds to the city

payload.passage: Vikram dug a long canal in the wet sand. He led the water from the sea into his little channel. The water flowed and filled the sandy path. Vikram cheered as his canal joined a small pool he had made.
payload.title: Vikram Digs a Sand Canal
decoys: He led water into the channel.

payload.passage: Aditya loves to grow flowers from tiny seeds. He planted marigold seeds in a sunny patch of soil. He waters them and pulls out the weeds each day. Aditya was thrilled when the first orange flower opened.
payload.title: Aditya Grows Marigold Flowers

payload.passage: Our group made a model fire station for the project. We built a tall garage with little red fire trucks. We added a pole that the firemen slide down. The teacher said our fire station looked very real.
payload.title: Our Model Fire Station Project

payload.passage: Karthik stayed with his grandparents near a green canal. Each morning they walked along the cool, shady path. Grandfather pointed out the fish and the kingfishers. Karthik loved the peaceful walks beside the canal.
payload.title: Walks Beside the Green Canal

payload.passage: Tara loves to make her own board games. She draws a winding path with squares on card. She writes funny rules for each special square. Tara plays her homemade game with her whole family.
payload.title: Tara Makes Her Own Board Game

payload.passage: The school held its big sports day on Friday morning. Parents sat under tents to watch the children compete. There were running races, jumps, and a long relay. By the end, every child went home tired but happy.
payload.title: The school sports day is held
decoys: There were running races and jumps.

payload.passage: Our class made a model of the human teeth for the project. We used clay to shape big white teeth on a board. We wrote how brushing keeps teeth clean and strong. Visitors learned why we should brush twice each day.
payload.title: A Class Project on Healthy Teeth

payload.passage: Aditi stayed with her grandparents who had a goat. The goat followed granny everywhere she walked. Aditi fed it leaves and brushed its rough coat. Aditi grew very fond of the friendly little goat.
payload.title: Aditi Befriends the Goat

payload.passage: The class played a memory chain game in a circle. Each child added a word and repeated the list. Ria remembered the whole long chain of words. She was the last one left and won the game.
payload.title: Ria wins the memory chain game
decoys: She was the last one left
A sharp memory wins this game

payload.passage: The boys played a long kho-kho match in the afternoon sun. They were tired and far behind in the score. Their captain reminded them to support each other. With quick chases in the last minutes, they pulled off a thrilling win.
payload.title: A tired team pulls off a kho-kho win
decoys: They were far behind at first.

payload.passage: Diya saw her best friend crying behind the school wall. The friend had failed her spelling test. Diya sat beside her and said everyone makes mistakes sometimes. She promised to help her practise the words next time.
payload.title: Diya comforts her crying friend
decoys: The friend failed her spelling test
Diya promised to help her practise

payload.passage: Ishaan loves to make shadow puppets from card. He cuts out shapes of animals and people. He holds them up to a lamp behind a white sheet. Ishaan puts on shadow plays for his family at night.
payload.title: Ishaan Makes Shadow Puppets
decoys: He uses a lamp and sheet.

payload.passage: The market had a vendor who sold hot, roasted chestnuts. He turned them slowly over a small coal fire. The warm, smoky smell drew people to his cart. Rohan bought a small bag to warm his cold hands.
payload.title: Roasted Chestnuts at the Market
decoys: He turned them over a fire.

payload.passage: A small child dropped her ice cream on the ground and cried. She had no money to buy another one. A kind elder boy bought her a fresh cone. The little girl smiled and stopped crying.
payload.title: A boy buys a child new ice cream

payload.passage: Lavanya planted a small aloe plant in a pot. She gave it only a little water now and then. She kept it on the bright, sunny balcony. Over the months, the aloe grew thick, juicy leaves.
payload.title: Lavanya Grows an Aloe Plant
decoys: She kept it on the balcony.

payload.passage: Rahul went to stay at his grandparents' house in the village. Every morning his grandmother gave him warm milk and stories. His grandfather took him to the fields to see the crops. Rahul loved his happy days at the village home.
payload.title: Rahul's Happy Days in the Village

payload.passage: Myra wanted to bake a treat for her best friend's birthday. With her aunt's help she made small chocolate brownies. They poured the thick batter into a square tin and baked it. Myra cut the brownies into neat squares and tied them with a ribbon.
payload.title: Myra bakes brownies for a friend
decoys: They poured batter into a square tin.
She tied them with a ribbon.

payload.passage: Dev took part in the three-legged hop on field day. He tied one leg to his partner's leg. Together they had to move in step to the line. Dev and his partner hopped fastest and won the race.
payload.title: Dev's Three-Legged Hop Wins
decoys: He tied his leg to a partner.

payload.passage: The school plants were drooping in the hot summer break. No one was there to water them daily. So Harini came each morning during the holidays. She watered them and kept the garden green.
payload.title: Harini waters plants over the holidays

payload.passage: Lakshmi joined the fancy dress competition as a nurse. She wore a white cap and carried a small bag. She told the judges how nurses help sick people. Lakshmi's clear talk and neat dress won her the prize.
payload.title: Lakshmi Dresses Up as a Nurse

payload.passage: Imran planted a small fig tree in a big pot. He watered it and gave it the morning sun. He waited patiently through the changing seasons. At last the little tree gave its first soft fig.
payload.title: Imran Grows a Fig Tree in a Pot

payload.passage: The whole class cheered loudly during the tug-of-war match. Two lines of children pulled the thick rope with all their might. The flag in the middle moved slowly back and forth. After a long pull, the red team finally won.
payload.title: The class cheers at the tug-of-war
decoys: The flag moved back and forth.

payload.passage: The children made colourful book covers during library craft hour. They cut paper and drew patterns to protect their books. The librarian showed them how to fold the covers neatly. Now their borrowed books stayed clean and looked bright.
payload.title: Children make covers to protect books

payload.passage: Aarav enjoys learning magic tricks with coins. He practises making a coin vanish in his hand. He shows the trick to anyone who will watch. Aarav loves the look of wonder on their faces.
payload.title: Aarav Learns Coin Magic

payload.passage: Charu joined the leaf-art competition at the science fair. She glued dry leaves into the shape of a peacock. She used a long thin leaf for each tail feather. The judges loved her idea and gave her first prize.
payload.title: Charu's Leaf Peacock Wins

payload.passage: Our group made a model of a post office for the project. We built a counter, a red post box, and shelves of letters. We showed how a postman carries mail to homes. Visitors learned how letters travel to far places.
payload.title: Our Model Post Office Project
decoys: We built a red post box.

payload.passage: On a hot summer day, a tired postman knocked at the gate. His face was red and dripping with sweat. Vivek ran inside and brought him a glass of cold water. The postman drank it and thanked the kind boy.
payload.title: Vivek offers cold water to the postman
decoys: The postman was dripping with sweat
Vivek brought a glass of water

payload.passage: Our team built a tall tower out of straws for the building challenge. We taped the straws into triangles to make it strong. Other teams' towers fell, but ours stood up tall. The teacher measured it and said our tower was the highest.
payload.title: The Tallest Straw Tower Wins

payload.passage: The road outside the school was full of broken glass. Children could step on it and get hurt. A boy told the watchman about the danger. Together they swept the glass away safely.
payload.title: A boy helps clear broken glass

payload.passage: Aarav went to the zoo with his class. They saw lions, monkeys, and a tall giraffe. The teacher told them how each animal lives and what it eats. Aarav learned many new things about animals on this trip.
payload.title: A Class Trip to the Zoo
decoys: They saw monkeys at the zoo.

payload.passage: The library was very noisy until the children made a rule. They agreed to whisper so everyone could read. They put up a small friendly sign about quiet voices. Soon the library became a calm, peaceful place.
payload.title: Children make the library a quiet place
decoys: They put up a quiet sign.

payload.passage: The library started a quiet reading club for shy children. They met after lunch in the cosy corner. Each child read alone but felt part of the group. Slowly they began to share which stories they liked.
payload.title: A quiet reading club for shy children
decoys: They met in the cosy corner.
They shared which stories they liked.

payload.passage: Sahil went to his aunt's home in a busy town. They walked through markets full of shouts and colour. His aunt bought him sweets from a tiny corner shop. Sahil enjoyed the lively days at his aunt's town home.
payload.title: Lively Days at Aunt's Town Home

payload.passage: A skipping competition was held during the school break. Children skipped fast to see who could last longest. Bina skipped without missing for two whole minutes. She won the prize for the most skips.
payload.title: Bina wins the skipping competition
decoys: Skipping keeps us fit and happy

payload.passage: The train journey took the family across a desert. The children pressed against the glass to see the sand. Camels walked slowly far away on the dunes. The wide, golden land amazed them all day.
payload.title: The train crosses a wide desert
decoys: They saw camels on the dunes.

payload.passage: The crowded village bus carried farmers to the weekly market. Their baskets were full of fresh vegetables and fruit. The children squeezed in beside sacks and bags. The cheerful bus rattled along the bumpy country road.
payload.title: A village bus rolls to the weekly market

payload.passage: Aadhya played her first table tennis match at the club. She was nervous, but she remembered her coach's tips. She hit the ball low and fast across the net. Her smart play helped her win the close match.
payload.title: Aadhya wins her first table tennis match
decoys: She hit the ball low and fast.

payload.passage: Aarya loved visiting the library after school each day. She would find a quiet corner and open a story. Soon she forgot all about the noise outside. Books took her to faraway lands every afternoon.
payload.title: Aarya enjoys daily trips to the library

payload.passage: Priya loves to make her own scented soaps. With help, she melts a soap base and adds rose petals. She pours it into little moulds to set. Priya gives her pretty soaps as gifts to her family.
payload.title: Priya Makes Scented Soaps

payload.passage: Jatin took part in the wheelbarrow race with a friend. He held his friend's legs while she walked on her hands. They moved as fast as they could to the line. Jatin and his friend came first and laughed with joy.
payload.title: Jatin's Wheelbarrow Race Win

payload.passage: The zoo had a snack stall near the deer park. Ishaan bought a cold drink and a packet of popcorn. He sat on a bench to rest his tired legs. The break helped Ishaan feel ready to see the rest of the zoo.
payload.title: A Snack Break at the Zoo

payload.passage: Grandmother could not thread the needle for her sewing. The hole was tiny and her eyes were weak. Little Anil threaded the needle in one quick try. Grandmother patted his head and began to sew.
payload.title: Anil threads the needle for grandmother
decoys: Young eyes can help old ones

payload.passage: The girls played a long game of hopscotch on the road. They drew the squares with white chalk. Nina hopped through all the squares without a mistake. She won the game and drew a new round.
payload.title: Nina wins the hopscotch game

payload.passage: On a hot afternoon, Pia and her friends made cold fruit popsicles. They poured fresh juice into small moulds and added fruit pieces. They placed the moulds in the freezer and waited patiently. By evening the icy treats were ready to cool everyone down.
payload.title: Pia and friends make fruit popsicles
decoys: They placed them in the freezer.

payload.passage: It was the last over of the match and four runs were needed. Everyone was nervous as Sachin walked in to bat. He took a deep breath and hit the ball hard. The ball sailed over the boundary for a six.
payload.title: Sachin hits a six to win the match
decoys: Four runs were needed to win

payload.passage: Beena went to her grandmother's house during the holidays. Granny taught her to roll soft dough into round shapes. They made warm flat bread for the whole family. Beena was proud of the bread she helped to make.
payload.title: Beena Makes Bread With Granny

payload.passage: Pankaj stayed with his grandparents who had a small loom. Grandfather wove bright cloth with quick, steady hands. He let Pankaj pass the shuttle back and forth. Pankaj loved watching the cloth grow on the loom.
payload.title: Grandfather Weaves on the Loom

payload.passage: Ravi had two chocolates and his friend had none. The friend looked at the chocolates but said nothing. Ravi smiled and gave one chocolate to his friend. They both ate happily and shared a good laugh.
payload.title: Ravi shares his chocolate with a friend
decoys: The friend looked but said nothing

payload.passage: The school held a fun musical chairs game at the party. The children walked around the chairs to the music. When the music stopped, everyone rushed to sit down. Pinky was quick and won the last chair.
payload.title: Pinky wins the musical chairs game
decoys: Musical chairs is a quick game

payload.passage: Diya watched a fire dancer perform at the fair after dark. The dancer spun bright torches in big circles. The flames lit up the night with an orange glow. Diya watched closely but stayed safely behind the rope.
payload.title: The Fire Dancer at the Fair

payload.passage: Rahul loves to play cricket in the park every evening. He practises his batting against the old brick wall. Slowly his shots became stronger and straighter. Now he is one of the best batsmen in his team.
payload.title: Rahul practises hard to bat well
decoys: Rahul practises against a brick wall

payload.passage: Rohan brought home a tiny goldfish in a bowl. He fed it small flakes each morning and evening. He kept the water clean and watched it swim about. Over the months, Rohan's goldfish grew bigger and brighter.
payload.title: Rohan Cares for His Goldfish

payload.passage: The school had a fun penalty shootout to end sports day. Each child got one kick at the goal. Latha aimed at the corner and scored cleanly. Her goal won the shootout for her team.
payload.title: Latha scores in the penalty shootout
decoys: A good aim wins the shootout

payload.passage: Naresh wanted to bowl spin like the players on TV. His first tries spun the wrong way. He practised with a tennis ball every evening. Soon his spin turned sharply and fooled the batsmen.
payload.title: Naresh learns to bowl spin

payload.passage: Our group made a model of a cave for the project. We used grey paper to build a dark, rocky tunnel. We added paper bats hanging from the roof. Our teacher said our cave looked deep and spooky.
payload.title: Our Model Cave Project

payload.passage: Aarav visited a museum about rocks and gems. Shiny stones in many colours sat under bright lights. Some glowed purple, blue, and deep red. Aarav learned that these stones come from deep inside the earth.
payload.title: Shiny Rocks at the Museum

payload.passage: Lavanya went to her cousin's home for the holidays. They put on a small play for the whole family. They made costumes from old clothes and scarves. Lavanya loved acting out the funny story with her cousin.
payload.title: Lavanya Acts in a Family Play

payload.passage: The whole class went out to fly kites on the terrace. The sky was full of red, yellow, and green kites. Jaya pulled her string and made her kite go highest. Everyone looked up and clapped for her.
payload.title: Jaya flies her kite the highest
decoys: The sky was full of kites

payload.passage: Suhana and her grandmother spent the morning making sweet coconut balls. They mixed grated coconut with a little sugar and milk. Together they rolled the mixture into small, round balls. The kitchen filled with a sweet smell, and they shared the treats with neighbours.
payload.title: Suhana and grandmother make coconut balls

payload.passage: Gaurav saw a younger student crying near the gate after school. The little boy could not find his school bus. Gaurav held his hand and took him to the teacher on duty. The teacher found the right bus very quickly.
payload.title: Gaurav helps a lost little boy
decoys: The little boy could not find his bus
The teacher found the bus quickly
Older children should guide the younger

payload.passage: Riya put a small cactus on her sunny windowsill. She learned that cacti need only a little water. She gave it a few drops once every week. Slowly her tiny cactus grew taller and even sprouted a flower.
payload.title: Riya Grows a Tiny Cactus

payload.passage: Sameer visited his uncle who repaired old bicycles. The yard was full of wheels, chains, and bells. His uncle showed Sameer how to fix a flat tyre. Sameer was proud to help mend the bikes all day.
payload.title: Sameer Helps Mend Bicycles

payload.passage: Meera visited the sweet shop at the market with her uncle. Trays of sweets sat behind the clean glass case. She could not decide which one looked the nicest. In the end, her uncle bought a box of mixed sweets to share.
payload.title: Choosing Sweets at the Market Shop
decoys: Her uncle bought a mixed box.

payload.passage: Anika went on her first long bus journey to her grandmother's village. She watched towns and rivers pass by the window. A kind aunty shared snacks with the children. By evening, Anika reached the village full of happy stories.
payload.title: Anika's first long bus journey

payload.passage: Nisha visited her uncle's poultry farm in the countryside. Rows of clucking hens filled the long sheds. Her uncle showed her how the chicks were kept warm. Nisha was fascinated by all the busy little birds.
payload.title: Nisha Visits the Poultry Farm
decoys: The sheds were full of hens.

payload.passage: Tanmay was given a small pup that loved to chew. He gave it a soft toy so it would not bite shoes. He fed it on time and took it out to play. Slowly Tanmay's pup learned to behave at home.
payload.title: Tanmay Trains His Chewy Pup
decoys: He gave it a chew toy.

payload.passage: A baby bird fell from its nest in the tall mango tree. It chirped weakly on the hard ground. Harsh climbed up carefully and placed it back in the nest. The mother bird returned and fed it again.
payload.title: Harsh returns the baby bird to its nest
decoys: The baby bird fell to the ground
The mother bird returned to feed it

payload.passage: Manoj stayed with his grandfather, who kept pigeons. Each dawn the birds were let out to circle the sky. Grandfather whistled and the pigeons flew back home. Manoj loved watching the grey birds wheel overhead.
payload.title: Grandfather's Pigeons Circle the Sky

payload.passage: The bus ride to the beach felt very long for the children. They kept asking how much farther it was. The driver smiled and pointed to the blue sea ahead. The children cheered when they finally smelled the salty air.
payload.title: The long bus ride to the beach
decoys: The children kept asking the time.

payload.passage: Dev went to his grandparents' house near a river. Every evening they walked along the cool riverbank. Grandfather pointed out the birds and the boats. Dev loved the calm walks beside the gentle river.
payload.title: Evening Walks by the River

payload.passage: Ravi and his sister built a big sandcastle near the water. They used buckets to shape the towers and shells to decorate. They dug a deep moat all the way around it. They felt proud of the castle until a wave washed it away.
payload.title: Building a Sandcastle at the Beach

payload.passage: Two friends raced their spinning tops on the smooth floor. They wanted to see whose top spun longer. Yogesh threw his top with a strong wind-up. His top kept spinning the longest and won.
payload.title: Yogesh's top wins the spinning race
decoys: They raced on a smooth floor
A good throw wins the game

payload.passage: Diya enjoys keeping a scrapbook of her trips. She sticks in tickets, leaves, and small photos. She writes a few lines about each place she visits. Diya loves looking back through all her happy memories.
payload.title: Diya Keeps a Trip Scrapbook
decoys: She sticks in tickets and leaves.

payload.passage: Lata wanted to make a special drink for her tired mother. She mixed cold milk with a little chocolate powder. She stirred it well and added two ice cubes. Her mother smiled and said it was the tastiest milkshake ever.
payload.title: Lata makes a milkshake for her mother
decoys: She mixed milk with chocolate powder.

payload.passage: Anaya watched a stilt walker tower above the fair crowd. The man walked on tall wooden legs with ease. His long trousers hid the stilts almost completely. Anaya tipped her head right back to see his smiling face.
payload.title: The Stilt Walker at the Fair

payload.passage: The class played a quiz game in two big teams. Each team had to answer questions about animals. Rohan's team answered the most questions correctly. They won the quiz and got a round of claps.
payload.title: Rohan's team wins the animal quiz
decoys: They got a round of claps

payload.passage: The early train carried the family to a seaside town. The children could not sit still as they neared the coast. Soon they smelled the salty breeze through the windows. They cheered when the bright blue sea came into view.
payload.title: The family rides the train to the sea

payload.passage: Rehan learned to make crunchy toast with his big brother. They buttered the bread and sprinkled cheese on top. They toasted it until the cheese turned soft and golden. The warm, cheesy toast was a great after-school snack.
payload.title: Rehan makes cheesy toast with his brother
decoys: They sprinkled cheese on the bread.
The cheese turned soft and golden.

payload.passage: Kabir enjoys building toy cars from bottle caps and sticks. He uses four caps as round little wheels. He pushes them and watches the cars roll. Kabir races his bottle-cap cars down a smooth ramp.
payload.title: Kabir Builds Bottle-Cap Cars
decoys: He races them down a ramp.

payload.passage: Kabir flew a colourful stunt kite on the windy beach. The kite swooped and looped across the sky. He pulled the two strings to make it dance. Kabir grinned as his kite drew big circles in the air.
payload.title: Flying a Stunt Kite at the Beach

payload.passage: Naina watched the train pull into the big station. The platform was full of people with bags and boxes. A loud voice told travellers which train was leaving. Naina held her mother's hand tightly in the crowd.
payload.title: Naina arrives at the big train station

payload.title: Sonal wins the garden treasure hunt
decoys: She found the box under a tree

payload.passage: Meera loves to make her own paper crowns. She cuts zigzag points along a strip of card. She sticks on shiny paper gems and glitter. Meera wears her sparkling crown when she plays the queen.
payload.title: Meera Makes Paper Crowns

payload.title: Ravi Builds Garden Sandcastles
decoys: He shapes towers with a bucket.

payload.passage: Aanya and her brother decided to bake bread for the very first time on a slow Sunday morning. They mixed the flour with warm water and a little yeast. They waited patiently while the dough puffed up under a cloth. After baking, the golden loaf smelled wonderful and made the whole family proud.
payload.title: Aanya and brother bake their first loaf
decoys: They mixed flour with warm water.
The dough puffed up under a cloth.

payload.passage: Rohan enjoys building tracks for his marbles. He tapes cardboard tubes along the wall. The marbles roll down through the loops and turns. Rohan cheers as each marble drops into the cup at the end.
payload.title: Rohan Builds Marble Tracks
decoys: He tapes tubes to the wall.

payload.title: Dev's Fish Loves Its Bubbly Tank

payload.passage: A school chess match was held in the big hall. Two of the best players faced each other quietly. Aman thought hard before every careful move. In the end, he won the match with a smart trap.
payload.title: Aman wins the school chess match
decoys: The match was in the hall

payload.passage: The class set up a small library inside their classroom. Each child donated one book they had finished. They made a simple chart to track who borrowed what. Now the children could read a new story whenever they liked.
payload.title: The class sets up a classroom library

payload.passage: Pranav went to his grandmother's house for the holidays. Granny had an old swing hanging from the big tree. She pushed Pranav higher and higher with a laugh. Pranav loved swinging in granny's shady garden.
payload.title: Pranav Swings in Granny's Garden
decoys: The swing hung from a tree.

payload.passage: The school bus took the children on a trip to the science centre. They sang songs and played games on the way. The teacher pointed out interesting sights through the window. Everyone reached the centre full of energy and excitement.
payload.title: The school bus heads to the science centre
decoys: They sang songs on the way.

payload.passage: Naveen planted a small drumstick tree near the fence. He watered it and tied it to a strong stick. He watched the slim branches grow longer. After a long time, the tree gave long green pods.
payload.title: Naveen Grows a Drumstick Tree
decoys: He tied it to a stick.

payload.title: A meet-the-author day at the library
decoys: The writer read from her book.
She shared how she got ideas.

payload.title: A girl shares ride tokens at the fair

payload.passage: During the school trip, one boy felt sick on the bus. He looked pale and held his stomach. His classmate Rita gave him water and a wet tissue. She told the teacher right away so he could rest.
payload.title: Rita helps a sick boy on the trip
decoys: She told the teacher right away

payload.title: A cosy reading tent in the library

payload.title: Nikhil pockets the queen and wins carrom

payload.passage: Sara loves to make tiny gardens inside glass jars. She layers small stones, soil, and a little plant. She sprays a few drops of water inside. Sara keeps her jar garden on her sunny windowsill.
payload.title: Sara Makes a Jar Garden
decoys: She keeps it on the sill.

payload.title: Arjun learns to roast peanuts
decoys: They stirred the peanuts till golden.

payload.passage: Karan loves to make his own kite tails. He ties bits of cloth along a long string. The colourful tail helps his kite fly steady. Karan is proud when his kite soars high without spinning.
payload.title: Karan Makes Colourful Kite Tails

payload.title: Ria bakes garlic bread for movie night
decoys: They spread butter and garlic on top.

payload.title: Bats in the Zoo's Dark Room

payload.title: Kabir helps fix the broken park bench
decoys: The bench was broken and dusty

decoys: The plant was drooping and dry

payload.title: A game cheers up the stuck school bus

payload.passage: The two sisters made a colourful vegetable rice dish for the family dinner. They fried the rice with peas, beans, and bright carrots. They added a few mild spices and stirred everything well. The pretty, fragrant rice made the dinner table look like a feast.
payload.title: Sisters cook a colourful rice dish
decoys: They used a few mild spices.

payload.passage: Beena planted a pumpkin seed in the garden patch. She watered it and watched the big leaves spread. A yellow flower came, then a small green pumpkin. Beena was amazed how large her pumpkin slowly grew.
payload.title: Beena Grows a Big Pumpkin

payload.passage: Kavya had trained for weeks for the hundred metre race. On race day her heart pounded as she stood at the line. When the whistle blew, she ran with all her strength. Her long practice helped her cross the line first.
payload.title: Kavya's training pays off in her race
decoys: Her heart pounded at the start.
She crossed the finish line first.

payload.passage: Meera found a starfish lying on the wet sand. It had five arms and felt rough to touch. Her father told her to put it gently back in the water. Meera was happy to help the little starfish go home.
payload.title: Meera Helps a Starfish
decoys: She put it back in the water.

payload.passage: Roshni joined the cooking competition for older children. With her teacher's help she made a fresh fruit salad. She cut the fruit neatly and arranged it nicely. The judges tasted it and gave Roshni the first prize.
payload.title: Roshni's Fruit Salad Wins

payload.passage: The classroom window would not shut, and rain came in. The desks near it were getting wet. Two boys pushed the stuck window closed together. They wiped the wet desks with a cloth.
payload.title: Boys shut the stuck window in the rain
decoys: Quick action keeps the class dry

payload.passage: Akash went to his cousin's house during the rains. They watched the storm from the safe, dry porch. They counted the seconds between the flash and the thunder. Akash thought the rainy day with his cousin was thrilling.
payload.title: Watching the Storm With Cousin

payload.passage: Roopa saw her teacher carrying a heavy pile of notebooks. The pile wobbled and almost fell from her hands. Roopa ran up and took half the notebooks at once. She carried them all the way to the staff room.
payload.title: Roopa helps her teacher carry notebooks
decoys: She carried them to the staff room
Helping teachers is a kind act

payload.passage: Vikram went to the market to get his cycle tyre fixed. The repair man found the small hole quickly. He patched it and pumped in fresh air. Vikram thanked him and rode his cycle home with a smile.
payload.title: Getting the Cycle Tyre Fixed
decoys: The man found a small hole.

payload.passage: Aditya grew a money plant in a glass jar of water. He changed the water every few days to keep it fresh. He kept it where the soft sunlight could reach. Slowly the plant grew long, leafy vines.
payload.title: Aditya Grows a Money Plant in Water

payload.passage: Vikram enjoys drawing comic strips in his notebook. He draws little boxes with funny pictures inside. He writes the words his characters say in bubbles. Vikram's comics make his classmates laugh out loud.
payload.title: Vikram Draws Comic Strips

payload.passage: Two cricket teams played a hard and close match. At the end, one team won and the other lost. Both teams shook hands and said well played. They learned that playing fair is more important than winning.
payload.title: Both teams show good sportsmanship
decoys: Fair play is better than winning

payload.passage: Geet wanted to win the chess club trophy this year. She studied many tricky moves from a book. She played a practice game every single evening. At the final, she won the trophy with a clever move.
payload.title: Geet wins the chess club trophy

payload.passage: Ananya loves to make her own kite from a plastic bag. She cuts the bag and tapes on two thin sticks. She ties on a tail and a long flying string. Ananya runs across the field to lift her light kite up.
payload.title: Ananya Makes a Bag Kite

payload.passage: The school bus had a flat tyre on the way home. The children were worried they would be late. Some big boys helped the driver push the bus aside. They waited patiently while a new tyre was fixed.
payload.title: Boys help the driver with the flat tyre
decoys: The bus had a flat tyre
Helping in trouble shows good heart

payload.passage: Tisha wanted to surprise her grandmother who was feeling unwell. With her mother's help, she cooked a bowl of soft rice and lentils on the stove. She added just a little salt and stirred it slowly. Her grandmother smiled and said the warm meal made her feel much better.
payload.title: Tisha cooks a meal for her grandmother

payload.passage: The children played dodgeball in the school hall. They had to throw the soft ball and dodge it too. Karan was very quick at jumping out of the way. He was the last player left and won the game.
payload.title: Karan is the last one standing in dodgeball
decoys: They had to dodge the ball
He was the last player left

payload.passage: The young readers club chose one book to read together. Each week they read a few chapters at home. Then they met to talk about the exciting parts. Sharing made the story even more fun for everyone.
payload.title: A club reads one book together
decoys: They read a few chapters at home.

payload.passage: Karan saw a man selling bright kites near the market gate. The kites had long tails and paper of many colours. The seller showed how to hold the string just right. Karan and his father bought three kites for the windy day.
payload.title: Buying Kites for a Windy Day

payload.passage: Aarav and his father waited at the bus stop in the rain. They shared one umbrella while they waited. The warm bus finally came splashing through the water. They were glad to climb in out of the rain.
payload.title: Aarav waits for the bus in the rain

payload.passage: The giant wheel was the tallest ride at the fair. Veer sat in a swinging seat as it slowly went up. From the top he could see the whole bright fairground. The view from the giant wheel took his breath away.
payload.title: Riding the Giant Wheel
decoys: The seat swung as it rose.

payload.passage: Lakshmi stayed with her grandmother during the holidays. Granny taught her old songs while they shelled peas. They sat together for hours doing this gentle work. Lakshmi treasured the quiet time spent with her granny.
payload.title: Lakshmi Shells Peas With Granny

payload.passage: Vikram watched a man make sugar shapes at the fair. The man poured hot melted sugar onto a cold plate. It set quickly into a shape of a bird. Vikram bought the sugar bird and ate it slowly.
payload.title: The Sugar Shape Maker at the Fair

payload.passage: Akash looked after a pet dog that loved to dig holes. He gave it a sandy patch where digging was fine. He fed it well and played fetch each evening. Over time, the dog stopped digging in the flower beds.
payload.title: Akash Trains His Digging Dog
decoys: He gave it a sandy patch.

payload.passage: Karan watched a tightrope walker high above the fair. The man balanced on a thin rope with a long pole. Everyone below held their breath as he took each step. Karan clapped hardest when the brave man reached the other side.
payload.title: The Tightrope Walker at the Fair
decoys: The man held a long pole.

payload.passage: Riya watched the zebras run across their open field. Their black and white stripes made a busy pattern as they moved. A baby zebra trotted close behind its mother. Riya thought no two zebras seemed to have the very same stripes.
payload.title: Zebras and Their Stripes
decoys: A baby zebra ran behind its mother.
The zebras ran in a field.

payload.passage: On the holiday, Tanish and his sister made fresh fruit juice. They washed oranges and apples and cut them small. They pushed the fruit through the juicer and watched the juice flow. The cool, sweet drink was the perfect start to a lazy morning.
payload.title: Tanish and sister make fresh juice

payload.passage: Aditya wanted to try the high swing ride at the fair. The swings flew out in a wide circle as they spun. Aditya felt the wind rush past his face. He shouted with joy as he swung high above the ground.
payload.title: The High Swing Ride
decoys: The swings flew in a circle.

payload.passage: The class hamster's cage was getting dirty and smelly. No one wanted to clean it. But Pooja put on gloves and changed the bedding. She gave the hamster fresh food and clean water.
payload.title: Pooja cleans the class hamster's cage

payload.passage: The long train journey gave the cousins time to play games. They guessed the names of the stations they passed. They spotted cows, ponds, and small temples from the window. The hours flew by faster than they thought.
payload.title: Cousins play games on the long train ride

payload.passage: Rehan's bus had a flat tyre near the green fields. Everyone got down while the driver changed it. The children played near the grass and picked flowers. Soon the bus was ready, and they went on cheerfully.
payload.title: Rehan's bus gets a flat tyre

payload.passage: The bus to the fair was packed with excited families. Children chattered about the rides they would try. Balloons and bags filled every seat and lap. The cheerful bus buzzed like the fair itself.
payload.title: A crowded bus heads to the fair

payload.passage: Rohan loves making things out of clay and wire. He bends the wire into shapes and covers it with clay. Last week he made a little man with bendy arms. Rohan likes that he can shape his ideas into real toys.
payload.title: Rohan Makes Toys from Clay and Wire

payload.passage: The sweeper aunty had hurt her hand and could not work. The school ground was full of dry leaves. The children picked up brooms and swept the ground for her. The aunty thanked them and rested her hand.
payload.title: Children sweep the ground for the aunty
decoys: The aunty had hurt her hand

payload.passage: Sneha went to the market to buy new bangles. The shop had bangles of every colour, glass and metal. She tried red ones, then blue, then shining gold. In the end, Sneha picked the green bangles that matched her dress.
payload.title: Sneha Buys Colourful Bangles
decoys: She tried red and blue bangles.
She picked green to match her dress.

payload.passage: Priya helped her mother carry the shopping list at the market. She read out each item one by one. They found the tea, the soap, and the biscuits. Priya was happy that nothing on the list was forgotten.
payload.title: Following the Shopping List

payload.passage: Mukesh won the running race by a long way. But he saw a younger boy fall down near the finish. Instead of cheering, he went back to help the boy up. The crowd clapped for Mukesh's kind heart.
payload.title: Mukesh shows kindness after winning
decoys: Mukesh won by a long way

payload.passage: The old man's newspaper blew across the windy road. He could not run fast to catch it. A boy chased the paper and brought it back. The man folded it and thanked the boy.
payload.title: A boy catches the blown newspaper
decoys: The paper blew across the road
A small help is always nice

payload.passage: A small boy was scared to walk past a barking dog. He stood frozen on the footpath and would not move. A kind girl held his hand and walked beside him. They passed the dog safely and the boy smiled.
payload.title: A girl helps past the barking dog

payload.passage: Veer likes to make simple kites from plastic sheets. He cuts the plastic, adds sticks, and ties a string. The light kites fly well even in a soft breeze. Veer enjoys testing each new kite on the open field.
payload.title: Veer Makes Plastic Kites
decoys: He tests them on a field.

payload.passage: A football was the only ball the children had to share. They took turns to play short matches with it. Everyone got a fair chance to kick and score. They played happily till it was time to go.
payload.title: Children share one football fairly
decoys: Sharing makes games fair and fun

payload.passage: The neighbour's tap kept leaking and wasting clean water. The drops fell all day and all night. A clever boy tied a tight cloth to slow the leak. Then he told the plumber to come and fix it.
payload.title: A boy helps stop the leaking tap
decoys: He told the plumber to come

payload.passage: Dev was given a brown puppy with floppy ears. Each day he fed it and took it for a walk. He brushed its coat and washed its muddy paws. After some weeks, the puppy followed Dev everywhere.
payload.title: Dev's Brown Floppy-Eared Puppy

payload.passage: Meera ran along the beach flying a long ribbon in the wind. The bright ribbon trailed and twisted behind her. She made big loops in the air as she ran. Meera felt as free as the birds in the sky.
payload.title: Running with a Ribbon on the Beach

payload.passage: Tara enjoys making bead jewellery in her free time. She threads bright beads onto a long string. She has made necklaces and bracelets in many colours. Tara loves giving her bead jewellery to her best friends.
payload.title: Tara Makes Bead Jewellery
decoys: She threads beads on a string.

payload.passage: Two friends had a hula hoop spinning contest in the park. They had to keep the hoop spinning the longest. Manya swung her hips in a smooth rhythm. Her hoop spun longest and she won.
payload.title: Manya wins the hula hoop contest

payload.passage: The class held a book swap day in their room. Each child brought a book they had finished reading. They traded books so everyone got something new. Nobody spent any money, yet all went home with a fresh story.
payload.title: The class holds a book swap day
decoys: Each child brought a finished book.

payload.passage: Priya likes to make things from soft clay. She rolls, pinches, and shapes it into little animals. Last week she made a tiny clay turtle and a snail. Priya lines up all her clay animals on her shelf.
payload.title: Priya Makes Clay Animals
decoys: She keeps them on a shelf.

payload.passage: Priya loves to make her own wrapping paper. She stamps shapes onto plain sheets with cut sponges. She uses bright paint in red, blue, and green. Priya wraps her gifts in the cheerful paper she made.
payload.title: Priya Makes Her Own Wrapping Paper

payload.passage: Sara went to the market to buy a gift for her friend. She looked at hair clips, books, and small puzzles. After a long look around, she picked a story book with pictures. Sara hoped her friend would love the surprise.
payload.title: Buying a Gift for a Friend
decoys: She picked a picture story book.

payload.passage: Aarohi read a book about a faraway snowy land. She learned how people stay warm in deep snow. She had never seen snow in her warm city. The library let her travel to cold lands in her mind.
payload.title: A book takes Aarohi to a snowy land
decoys: She learned how people stay warm.
She lived in a warm city.

payload.passage: The zoo had a butterfly garden full of tiny flying jewels. Butterflies of orange, blue, and yellow rested on the bright flowers. Anjali stood very still and one landed gently on her arm. She held her breath until the butterfly flew away again.
payload.title: The Butterfly Garden at the Zoo

payload.passage: Aryan planted a leafy spinach bed in the yard. He watered it well and kept the soil loose. He watched the green leaves grow broad and fresh. Soon Aryan could pick spinach for the family meals.
payload.title: Aryan Grows a Spinach Bed

payload.passage: Tara enjoys pressing leaves to make pictures. She dips a leaf in paint and presses it on paper. The leaf leaves a perfect print with all its lines. Tara filled a page with leaf prints of many shapes.
payload.title: Tara Makes Leaf Prints
decoys: She dips a leaf in paint.
The print shows all the lines.

payload.passage: Two sisters made cold yoghurt cups on a hot day. They mixed thick yoghurt with chopped fruit and a little honey. They put the cups in the fridge to chill. The cool, creamy treat was perfect for the warm afternoon.
payload.title: Sisters make cold yoghurt fruit cups
decoys: They mixed yoghurt with chopped fruit.
They chilled the cups in the fridge.

payload.passage: The zoo had a shop near the gate selling soft toys. There were fluffy lions, tiny tigers, and cuddly bears. Vikram chose a small panda to remember his trip. He hugged his new toy all the way home in the car.
payload.title: Vikram's Toy from the Zoo Shop

payload.passage: The morning bus to school was always full of friends. They saved seats and shared their breakfast snacks. They sang songs as the bus bumped along the road. The ride felt like a small party every day.
payload.title: The school bus ride is full of fun

payload.passage: Ishaan looked after a pair of guinea pigs. He gave them hay, vegetables, and fresh water daily. He cleaned their pen so it stayed dry and warm. Over time, the guinea pigs squeaked happily when he came.
payload.title: Ishaan Cares for Guinea Pigs

payload.passage: On a cold day, the school guard had no hot tea. He rubbed his hands to keep warm. A teacher sent him a warm cup from the staff room. The guard smiled and felt much better.
payload.title: A teacher sends tea to the guard
decoys: He rubbed his hands for warmth

payload.passage: Vikram likes to solve jigsaw puzzles on holidays. He spreads the pieces out and finds the corners first. Slowly the picture comes together, piece by piece. Vikram feels great joy when the last piece fits in place.
payload.title: Vikram's Hobby of Solving Puzzles

payload.passage: Gaurav took part in the high jump on sports day. He ran up to the bar and sprang into the air. He cleared the bar even when it was raised higher. Gaurav jumped the highest and won the gold.
payload.title: Gaurav Wins the High Jump
decoys: He ran up to the bar.

payload.passage: Tushar took part in the lemon-and-spoon race on field day. He balanced a lemon on a spoon in his mouth. He walked carefully so it would not fall off. Tushar reached the line first without a single drop.
payload.title: Tushar Wins the Lemon-Spoon Race

payload.passage: It was the village kabaddi final and the crowd was huge. The two teams were equal at the last minute. Then Mahesh made a brave raid and tagged three players. His team won and the crowd cheered loudly.
payload.title: Mahesh's brave raid wins the kabaddi final
decoys: Bravery can win a close game

payload.passage: An old farmer's bullock cart got stuck in the soft mud. The wheels would not move forward at all. Some village boys pushed hard from behind. The cart came free and rolled on smoothly.
payload.title: Boys free the stuck bullock cart

payload.passage: Renu visited her uncle who lived by the seaside. They woke early to watch the fishermen bring their catch. Her uncle showed her the different kinds of fish. Renu was amazed at the busy, salty morning by the sea.
payload.title: Renu Watches the Fishermen

payload.passage: On a sunny day, the children played frisbee in the park. They threw the round disc to one another. Asha could catch it even while running fast. Everyone said she was the best frisbee catcher.
payload.title: Asha is the best frisbee catcher
decoys: Frisbee is a fun outdoor game

payload.passage: Tushar planted a brinjal plant in the garden patch. He watered it and pulled out the small weeds. Purple flowers came, then shiny brinjals. Tushar picked the first brinjal with great pride.
payload.title: Tushar Grows Brinjals in the Garden

payload.passage: A man fainted in the long queue at the bank. People around him did not know what to do. A young woman moved him to a chair and fanned him. She gave him water until he felt better.
payload.title: A woman helps a man who fainted
decoys: The man fainted in the queue
She fanned him with her hand

payload.passage: Our class made a model of the solar system for the project. We hung balls of every size as the planets. We painted the sun a bright yellow in the middle. The teacher said our model showed the planets very clearly.
payload.title: A Class Model of the Solar System

payload.passage: The class library was in a big mess after the holidays. Books lay in piles on every shelf and table. Lakshmi offered to stay back and arrange them all. She sorted the books by size and made the shelves neat.
payload.title: Lakshmi tidies the messy class library
decoys: She sorted the books by size
A tidy room is a happy room

payload.passage: Aditya visited his grandfather, who fixed old radios. The shed was full of wires, knobs, and tiny tools. Grandfather let Aditya hold the parts and watch closely. Aditya was amazed at how his grandfather made them work again.
payload.title: Grandfather Fixes Old Radios

payload.passage: Lavanya looked after a pet kitten that scratched the sofa. She gave it a rough post to scratch instead. She fed it and played with a string each day. Over time, the kitten left the sofa alone.
payload.title: Lavanya Trains Her Scratching Kitten
decoys: She gave it a scratch post.

payload.passage: At the zoo, Anaya found a long line of busy ants behind glass. The little ants carried leaves much bigger than themselves. A board said they were building a home under the ground. Anaya was amazed at how the tiny ants worked together.
payload.title: Busy Ants at the Zoo Display

payload.passage: Asha was scared of the dark until she read a special book. The story showed a brave child who loved the night sky. After reading, Asha looked up at the stars without fear. The book gently helped her feel brave.
payload.title: A book helps Asha stop fearing the dark
decoys: The story had a brave child.
She looked up at the stars.

payload.passage: The old gardener was too tired to water all the plants. The hot sun had made him weak. Some children took the hose and watered the rows for him. The gardener rested under a tree and thanked them.
payload.title: Children water the plants for the gardener
decoys: The sun had made him weak
The gardener rested under a tree

payload.passage: Geeta kept a pet rabbit that grew a thick coat. She brushed it daily so the fur stayed soft. She fed it greens and kept its home clean. Over time, the rabbit's coat grew shiny and neat.
payload.title: Geeta Brushes Her Rabbit's Coat

payload.passage: Priya saw the polar bear in its cool, white home. The huge bear had thick fur to keep it warm. It dived into the water and swam with strong paws. Priya learned that polar bears live where it is snowy and cold.
payload.title: The Polar Bear at the Zoo

payload.passage: Yash counted the train coaches as they rolled by. There were red ones, blue ones, and a long green one. He guessed how many people each could hold. The waiting felt fun while he watched the train.
payload.title: Yash counts the coaches of the train
decoys: He saw red and blue coaches.
He guessed how many fit inside.

payload.passage: Dev found a torn book on the library floor. Instead of leaving it, he took it to the librarian. Together they fixed the page with clear tape. Dev felt happy that he had helped save a book.
payload.title: Dev helps fix a torn library book
decoys: He found the book on the floor.
They fixed the page with tape.

payload.passage: Priya loves to make her own puppets dance to music. She moves the strings in time with the beat. She makes the puppet hop, twirl, and bow. Priya's puppet dance always brings a big cheer.
payload.title: Priya's Dancing Puppet Show
decoys: She moves the strings in time.

payload.passage: Kabir found a room about the weather at the museum. He saw old tools that measured rain and wind. A screen showed how storms form in the sky. Kabir learned how people once guessed the coming weather.
payload.title: The Weather Room at the Museum

payload.passage: Ifra was the goalkeeper in the big school match. The other team kept shooting hard at her goal. She jumped and stretched to stop ball after ball. Her brave saves kept the score and helped her team win.
payload.title: Goalkeeper Ifra's saves help her team win
decoys: She jumped to stop the balls.

payload.passage: Diya was the goalkeeper in the close hockey final. The other team kept firing shots at her net. She dived again and again to block the ball. Her brave saves kept the score level until her team scored and won.
payload.title: Diya's saves help win the hockey final
decoys: The other team fired many shots.
She dived to block the ball.

payload.passage: The girls baked heart-shaped cookies for their teacher's last day. They cut the dough with a small heart cutter. They wrote a thank-you note to go with the box. The teacher was moved by their sweet, caring gift.
payload.title: Girls bake cookies for their teacher

payload.passage: Riya enjoys building a tiny garden in a tray. She fills it with soil, small plants, and pebbles. She adds a little mirror to look like a pond. Riya's tray garden sits proudly on her study table.
payload.title: Riya Builds a Tiny Tray Garden

payload.passage: Pankaj planted a creeping pumpkin in the back garden. He watered it and let the vine spread along the ground. Big yellow flowers came, then a round pumpkin. Pankaj watched proudly as his pumpkin slowly grew fat.
payload.title: Pankaj's Pumpkin Vine Spreads Wide
decoys: The vine spread on the ground.

payload.passage: Riya and her family arrived at the fair just as it opened. The stalls were being set up and the rides switched on. They were the very first to buy entry tickets. Riya felt lucky to have the whole fair almost to herself.
payload.title: Arriving Early at the Fair

payload.passage: Aditya found a room about flying machines at the museum. Old planes hung from the high ceiling. A board told how the first plane flew long ago. Aditya dreamed of flying high above the clouds one day.
payload.title: Old Planes at the Museum
decoys: Old planes hung from the ceiling.

payload.passage: Naina went to her grandmother's house by the hills. Granny knew the names of every bird that visited. She left out grain so the birds would come close. Naina loved watching the many birds in granny's yard.
payload.title: Birds in Granny's Yard

payload.passage: Veer enjoys making spinning tops out of old buttons. He pushes a small stick through the button hole. Then he gives it a quick twist to make it spin. Veer has a race to see whose top spins the longest.
payload.title: Veer Makes Spinning Tops

payload.passage: The museum had a corner about how letters were sent before. Meera saw old post boxes, stamps, and ink pens. A board explained that letters once took many days to reach. Meera was glad messages now travel so fast.
payload.title: How Letters Were Sent Long Ago

payload.passage: Rohan dug a deep hole in the wet beach sand. Water slowly filled the bottom of the hole. He pretended it was a little pond for tiny crabs. Rohan dug until his hands were covered in cool, wet sand.
payload.title: Digging in the Wet Sand
decoys: The beach is full of sand.

payload.passage: On race day, the rain made the track wet and muddy. The runners still lined up, ready to give their best. They slipped a little but kept their balance. The race went on, and the children loved the muddy fun.
payload.title: The race goes on despite the rain
decoys: The track was wet and muddy.

payload.passage: The poor children near the bus stop had no books to read. They watched others go to school with bags. So Tanvi collected old story books from her friends. She gave them away and saw the children smile with joy.
payload.title: Tanvi gives old books to poor children

payload.passage: Rohit visited his grandfather who kept a small garden of chillies. The little bushes were full of bright red fruit. Grandfather showed him which ones were ripe to pick. Rohit filled a small bowl from the chilli garden.
payload.title: Rohit Picks Chillies With Grandfather

payload.passage: Payal joined the mask-making competition for the school play. She made a lion's face from card and yellow wool. She added round eyes and a wide open mouth. The teacher chose Payal's mask for the main actor.
payload.title: Payal's Lion Mask Wins

payload.passage: Kabir went on the spinning teacup ride at the fair. He sat inside a giant cup that turned round and round. A wheel in the middle let him spin even faster. Kabir came off the ride feeling happy but very dizzy.
payload.title: The Spinning Teacup Ride
decoys: He sat inside a giant cup.

payload.passage: Imran planted a small grapevine by the wall. He watered it and tied the vine to a wire. He waited through the seasons as it climbed. After a long while, tiny green grapes finally formed.
payload.title: Imran Grows a Grapevine
decoys: He tied it to a wire.

payload.passage: Rohan enjoys carving simple stamps from an old rubber. He cuts a star, a heart, and a little tree. He dips them in ink and stamps his books. Rohan likes to mark all his things with his own stamps.
payload.title: Rohan Carves Rubber Stamps
decoys: He cuts a star and a tree.

payload.passage: Aditi kept a pet fish that grew very fast. She moved it to a bigger tank as it grew. She fed it well and kept the water clean. Over the months, the fish became long and shiny.
payload.title: Aditi's Fish Outgrows Its Tank
decoys: She moved it to a bigger tank.

payload.passage: The market had an old man who sold balloons. He held a huge bunch of red, yellow, and blue ones. Children gathered around him with happy faces. Vikram chose a big green balloon shaped like a star.
payload.title: The Balloon Seller at the Market
decoys: He held red and blue balloons.

payload.passage: Asmita went to her aunt's home in a green valley. Tall trees and a clear stream surrounded the house. They went on walks and listened to the birds. Asmita felt the valley was the calmest place she had been.
payload.title: Asmita's Calm Valley Visit

payload.passage: A water pipe burst and flooded the lane with muddy water. People could not walk to the market. Some neighbours brought brooms and pushed the water into the drain. By evening the lane was dry and clean again.
payload.title: Neighbours clear the flooded lane together
decoys: A water pipe burst in the lane
They pushed the water into the drain

payload.passage: Our class made a model of a fruit market for the fair. We laid out clay apples, bananas, and grapes on stalls. We showed a seller weighing fruit on a scale. Visitors said our little market looked fresh and lively.
payload.title: A Class Model of a Fruit Market

payload.passage: Kabir likes to make shadow shapes on the wall. He uses just his hands and a bright torch. He can make a dog, a bird, and a rabbit. Kabir's shadow show always makes his friends clap.
payload.title: Kabir Makes Shadow Shapes
decoys: He can make a shadow bird.

payload.passage: The double-decker bus thrilled the visiting children. They raced up the narrow stairs to the top floor. From there they could see far over the busy streets. Riding high up felt like a special adventure.
payload.title: Children ride the double-decker bus
decoys: They raced up the narrow stairs.

payload.passage: Aarav helped his father carry the heavy bags from the market. They had bought rice, oil, and a sack of potatoes. Aarav held one bag in each hand and walked slowly. His father said he was a strong and helpful boy.
payload.title: Aarav Helps Carry the Bags
decoys: They bought a sack of potatoes.
Aarav held a bag in each hand.
