payload.passage: Tara shared a packet of biscuits on the long bus ride. She passed them to the children sitting around her. Soon everyone was smiling and chatting like old friends. Her small act of sharing made the journey feel shorter.
payload.title: Tara shares biscuits on the bus

payload.passage: Anaya enjoys decorating little boxes with paper and ribbon. She covers each box in bright wrapping paper. Then she ties a neat bow on the top. Anaya uses her pretty boxes to keep her tiny treasures safe.
payload.title: Anaya Decorates Little Boxes

payload.passage: Ravi explored a museum about how houses were built long ago. He saw mud bricks, wooden beams, and old tools. A model showed a tiny village of small huts. Ravi learned that people once built homes by hand.
payload.title: How Old Houses Were Built

payload.passage: The museum had a hall full of beautiful old jewellery. There were gold necklaces, silver rings, and shining stones. Each piece sat safely behind thick glass. Sneha thought the kings and queens of long ago must have worn them.
payload.title: Old Jewellery at the Museum

payload.passage: Aarav and his sister searched the beach for crabs at low tide. They lifted stones and peeked into wet holes. They spotted three tiny crabs scuttling away. Aarav was careful not to harm the little creatures.
payload.title: Searching for Crabs at the Beach

payload.passage: Vidya joined the bottle-garden competition at school. She filled a clear jar with soil and tiny plants. She watered it gently and kept it by the light. The judges loved her green jar and gave her the prize.
payload.title: Vidya's Bottle Garden Wins
decoys: She kept it by the light.

payload.passage: The little children had a lift-the-flap book day in the library. They giggled as they peeked under each paper flap. Behind the flaps hid animals, surprises, and bright colours. The fun books made the youngest readers love story time.
payload.title: A lift-the-flap book day for little ones

payload.passage: The children played blind man's buff in the garden. One child was blindfolded and had to catch the others. Sohan listened to every soft footstep around him. He caught a friend and won his turn.
payload.title: Sohan wins at blind man's buff
decoys: Sharp ears help in this game

payload.passage: Our class made a model of a green park for the fair. We laid grass paper, paths, and little benches. We added a slide, a swing, and tiny trees. Visitors said our park looked like a happy place to play.
payload.title: A Class Model of a Green Park

payload.passage: Our class made a model of a busy port for the science fair. We placed cargo ships, cranes, and stacks of boxes. We showed how goods are loaded for far countries. The teacher said our port model was the busiest of all.
payload.title: A Class Model of a Busy Port

payload.passage: Avni and her grandmother made soft idlis early in the morning. They poured the batter into the round moulds. Steam cooked the idlis until they were light and white. The fresh idlis with chutney made a happy start to the day.
payload.title: Avni and grandmother make soft idlis
decoys: They poured batter into the moulds.

payload.passage: Charu planted a tall sunflower row by the wall. She watered them and turned them toward the light. The plants grew taller than Charu herself. At last the row burst into big golden faces.
payload.title: Charu Grows a Row of Sunflowers
decoys: She turned them to the light.

payload.passage: Reena was afraid of the water and would not go near the pool. Her coach taught her to float on her back first. Day by day she grew braver and learned to swim. Now she swims across the whole pool happily.
payload.title: Reena learns to swim without fear
decoys: She was afraid of the water
Her coach taught her to float

payload.passage: Anaya loves to make her own picture books. She draws a story on folded sheets of paper. She staples the pages to keep them together. Anaya reads her little books to her younger cousins.
payload.title: Anaya Makes Picture Books

payload.passage: The cooking club made a healthy salad for the school health week. They tore lettuce and added beans, corn, and chopped cucumber. They squeezed lemon juice and tossed everything gently. Their fresh, crunchy salad taught everyone that healthy food can taste great.
payload.title: The cooking club makes a health-week salad

payload.passage: The zoo had a long row of cages full of bright birds. There were tiny finches, talking mynas, and golden canaries. One myna copied the words a visitor said. Diya laughed when the clever bird called out hello to her.
payload.title: The Talking Myna at the Zoo

payload.passage: The colony cricket match drew a big crowd on Sunday. Two teams of children played hard for the small trophy. The ball flew, runs were scored, and everyone cheered. In the end, both teams shook hands like good sports.
payload.title: A big colony cricket match is played
decoys: The ball flew across the field.
Both teams shook hands at the end.

payload.passage: Asmita looked after a pet kitten that liked high places. She set a soft shelf for it to perch on. She fed it well and kept it safe indoors. Over time, the kitten loved to nap up on its shelf.
payload.title: Asmita's Kitten Loves High Places

payload.passage: Mira loved to play badminton with her father each evening. She could not reach the high shots at first. Her father showed her how to jump and swing. Now she returns even the highest shuttle.
payload.title: Mira learns to reach high shuttles
decoys: She could not reach high shots
A parent makes a good coach

payload.passage: Pooja joined the school swimming team this year. She was slow in the water at the start. With daily practice, her arms and legs grew strong. She came first in the school swimming meet.
payload.title: Pooja becomes the top school swimmer
decoys: She was slow at the start
She came first at the meet

payload.passage: Our group made a model windmill that really turned. We cut paper blades and pinned them to a stick. When we blew on it, the blades spun round and round. We showed the class how wind can do work for us.
payload.title: Our Spinning Windmill Project

payload.passage: Ananya helped at her uncle's vegetable stall on Sunday. She arranged the tomatoes in a neat red pile. She handed bags to the customers with a smile. Ananya felt grown-up helping her uncle at the busy market.
payload.title: Ananya Helps at the Stall

payload.passage: Meera and her brother got lost in the maze at the fair. Tall green walls turned this way and that. They took many wrong turns and giggled each time. At last they found the way out and cheered together.
payload.title: Finding the Way Out of the Maze
decoys: The walls were tall and green.

payload.passage: Karthik forgot his shoes on the day of the race. A kind classmate quickly lent him a spare pair. Wearing the borrowed shoes, Karthik ran without worry. He thanked his friend for the help after the race.
payload.title: A friend's spare shoes help Karthik race
decoys: He forgot his shoes that day.

payload.passage: Pranav stayed with his grandmother, who told weather signs. She showed him how dark clouds mean rain is near. She said birds flying low also warn of a storm. Pranav was amazed at all that granny could read in the sky.
payload.title: Granny Reads the Weather Signs

payload.passage: The school held a fun limbo game at the annual party. Children bent backward under a low bar. Manya bent very low and passed without falling. She cleared the lowest bar and won.
payload.title: Manya wins the limbo game
decoys: They bent under a low bar

payload.passage: Meera enjoys making her own paper fans. She folds a sheet back and forth like an accordion. She glues one end together so it opens out. Meera waves her bright paper fan on hot afternoons.
payload.title: Meera Makes Paper Fans
decoys: She folds the paper back and forth.
She waves it on hot days.

payload.passage: There was a swimming race at the sports club on Sunday. Five children dived into the cool blue water. Sunil kicked his legs hard and moved his arms fast. He touched the wall first and won the race.
payload.title: Sunil wins the swimming race

payload.passage: Pranav planted a small lemon tree in a big pot. He watered it and gave it sunshine on the terrace. He waited patiently as the seasons changed. After a long while, the little tree gave its first lemon.
payload.title: Pranav Grows a Lemon Tree

payload.passage: Rohan found a book about the planets in the library. He read about the rings of Saturn and the red colour of Mars. He could not stop turning the colourful pages. That night he dreamed of flying among the stars.
payload.title: Rohan finds a book about the planets

payload.passage: Ravi has learned to make simple meals with his mother. He can spread jam and slice soft fruit by himself. Last week he made a fruit bowl for the whole family. Ravi loves to cook and share food with everyone.
payload.title: Ravi Learns to Make Simple Meals

payload.passage: The train crossed a wide river on a tall iron bridge. The children leaned to the window to see the water below. Small boats drifted slowly on the shining surface. Everyone agreed the bridge was the best part of the trip.
payload.title: The train crosses a tall river bridge
decoys: The bridge was made of iron.

payload.passage: Gaurav looked after a duck that lived in the yard. He gave it grain and a tub of water to splash in. He kept its little house clean and dry. Over time, the duck waddled to Gaurav for its food.
payload.title: Gaurav Cares for His Duck

payload.passage: Priya stayed with her grandfather, who kept many cows. Each morning he milked them and gave Priya a glass. He showed her how to feed the calves fresh grass. Priya loved helping her grandfather with his gentle cows.
payload.title: Priya Helps Grandfather With the Cows

payload.passage: A girl forgot her colours on drawing day at school. She sat with a blank, sad face. Her bench partner shared half of her colour box. Both girls drew bright pictures together.
payload.title: A girl shares her colour box

payload.passage: Jatin visited his grandfather who ran a small mill. Big stones ground the wheat into soft white flour. Grandfather let Jatin scoop the flour into sacks. Jatin was amazed to see how flour is made at the mill.
payload.title: Grandfather Runs a Flour Mill

payload.passage: Rohan enjoys building a tall tower of wooden blocks. He pulls out one block at a time without it falling. The tower wobbles more with every move. Rohan holds his breath until his block is safely out.
payload.title: Rohan Plays the Block Tower Game
decoys: He pulls out one block at a time.

payload.passage: Ananya enjoys making paper lanterns. She folds and cuts the paper into a fine pattern. Then she rolls it into a round shape and glues the ends. Ananya hangs her bright lanterns up for festivals.
payload.title: Ananya Makes Paper Lanterns

payload.passage: Seema went to her grandparents' home in the hills. Each morning they sat on the porch with hot tea. Grandfather named the far peaks while granny knitted. Seema felt calm and happy in the quiet hill home.
payload.title: Quiet Mornings in the Hill Home

payload.passage: The school had a wheelbarrow race on its sports day. One child walked on hands while another held the legs. Bittu and his partner moved fast and stayed steady. They reached the line first and won.
payload.title: Bittu's pair wins the wheelbarrow race

payload.passage: Sanjay is the goalkeeper for his school football team. He stands tall and watches the ball very closely. When the other team kicked hard at the goal, he jumped and saved it. His team cheered for the great save.
payload.title: Sanjay makes a great goal-saving jump

payload.passage: The book stall in the market was Ravi's favourite spot. Old and new books were piled high on the table. He looked for a comic about a brave hero. Ravi found one for a good price and read it on the way home.
payload.title: The Book Stall at the Market

payload.passage: Tarun stayed with his grandfather who kept a beehive of bees. From far off they watched the busy bees come and go. Grandfather explained how the bees help the flowers. Tarun learned how important the little bees really are.
payload.title: Tarun Learns How Bees Help

payload.passage: Riya went to the beach with her family for the day. They spread a mat on the soft, warm sand. Riya built a tall sandcastle while her brother swam. It was a happy day full of sun, sand, and sea.
payload.title: A Family Day at the Beach
decoys: They spread a mat on the sand.

payload.passage: Kabir read a thrilling book about brave sailors on the sea. He learned how they used the stars to find their way. He could almost feel the wind and the salty waves. The library book filled his whole week with adventure.
payload.title: Kabir reads about brave sailors

payload.passage: A swimming relay was held at the school pool. Each swimmer had to finish their lap fast. Harini swam her lap quicker than the rest. Her speed helped her team win the relay.
payload.title: Harini's speed wins the swimming relay
decoys: She swam quicker than the rest

payload.passage: Lakshmi planted a small lime tree by the wall. She watered it and gave it the warm sun. She waited through many seasons as it grew. At last the little tree gave its first green limes.
payload.title: Lakshmi Grows a Lime Tree

payload.passage: Divya saw the maid struggling with a tall stack of plates. She quickly took half the plates in her own hands. Then she walked carefully to the kitchen with them. The maid smiled and said thank you for the help.
payload.title: Divya helps carry the heavy plates
decoys: The maid had a tall stack of plates
The maid said thank you for help
We should be kind to everyone

payload.passage: Mehul visited his grandfather, who grew mango trees. The trees were heavy with golden fruit that summer. Grandfather plucked the ripest mangoes for Mehul. They sat in the shade and ate the sweet mangoes together.
payload.title: Mehul Eats Mangoes With Grandfather
decoys: The trees were full of fruit.

payload.passage: Mohit planted a row of beans along the back wall. He watered them and let the vines climb sticks. Pretty flowers came, then long green pods. Mohit picked a basket of beans for the kitchen at last.
payload.title: Mohit Grows a Row of Beans

payload.passage: Vihaan loved a book about dinosaurs from the library. He learned the names of the big and small ones. He drew his favourite dinosaur on a large sheet at home. The library book made him dream of life long ago.
payload.title: A dinosaur book delights Vihaan

payload.passage: A boy in the park could not blow up his football. The pump was too stiff for his small arms. An older girl pumped air into it for him. The boy ran off happily to play.
payload.title: A girl pumps air into the ball
decoys: A little help brings big joy

payload.passage: The class learned to bake bread rolls during a fun activity. The teacher showed them how to knead and shape the dough. Each child made a roll and marked it with a tiny letter. Everyone took home a warm roll baked with their own hands.
payload.title: The class bakes bread rolls together
decoys: The teacher showed them to knead dough.
Each child marked a tiny letter.

payload.passage: The school library held a story-writing contest for Book Day. Children wrote short tales about anything they liked. They read their stories aloud to a kind panel of judges. A boy's funny tale about a sleepy cat won the first prize.
payload.title: A funny story wins the writing contest
decoys: The tale was about a sleepy cat.

payload.passage: Two boys raced their cycles around the colony park. They pedalled hard along the curving path. Naresh took the turns smoothly without slowing. He crossed the line first and won.
payload.title: Naresh wins the cycle park race

payload.passage: The badminton final went on for a long, exciting time. Both players hit the shuttle hard and ran across the court. The crowd held its breath at every point. At last, a clever shot ended the close match.
payload.title: An exciting badminton final is played
decoys: Both players ran across the court.
A clever shot ended the match.

payload.passage: Manoj visited his uncle who kept colourful fish. Big glass tanks lined the wall, full of bright fish. His uncle taught Manoj how to feed them small flakes. Manoj loved watching the fish glide through the water.
payload.title: Uncle's Tanks of Bright Fish

payload.passage: The children played a fun ball balancing game in the hall. They had to balance a ball on a bat while walking. Harini walked steadily without dropping the ball. She reached the line first and won.
payload.title: Harini wins the ball balancing game
decoys: They balanced a ball on a bat

payload.passage: Riya stayed with her grandparents during the rainy season. They sat on the veranda and watched the heavy rain. Granny made hot snacks while grandfather hummed a tune. Riya thought rainy days at their house were the cosiest.
payload.title: Cosy Rainy Days at Grandparents' House

payload.passage: Kabir wanted to see the big cats most of all. The tiger paced behind the fence with its orange and black stripes. A sign said tigers sleep for many hours each day. Kabir watched quietly until the tiger lay down to rest.
payload.title: Watching the Tiger at the Zoo
decoys: Tigers sleep many hours a day.

payload.passage: A girl in the park lost her way back to her mother. She stood near the slide and began to cry. Devika held her hand and helped her look around. Together they found her mother near the gate.
payload.title: Devika helps a lost girl find her mother
decoys: The girl stood near the slide
They found her mother at the gate
Helping lost children keeps them safe

payload.passage: Naina looked after a small pet dog with muddy paws. She wiped its feet each time it came indoors. She fed it well and brushed its shaggy coat. Over the weeks, the dog grew neat, happy, and clean.
payload.title: Naina Keeps Her Dog Clean

payload.passage: The fishermen pulled their boats onto the beach in the morning. Their nets were full of silver fish from the sea. People gathered to buy the fresh catch right there. Priya watched the busy work from the soft sand.
payload.title: Fishermen Bring Their Catch
decoys: The nets were full of fish.

payload.passage: A coconut seller sat under a tree at the beach. He chopped the top off each coconut with a sharp knife. People drank the sweet water through a straw. Aditya enjoyed his coconut while resting in the cool shade.
payload.title: The Coconut Seller at the Beach

payload.passage: Yusuf was given a small fish with a long fin. He fed it daily and kept the bowl very clean. He never tapped the glass so it would not be scared. Over the months, the fish grew calm and bright.
payload.title: Yusuf Cares for His Long-Finned Fish

payload.passage: Our group made a model of a temple pond for the project. We dug a small pool and lined it with blue paper. We added lotus flowers and tiny stone steps. Our teacher said the pond model looked calm and pretty.
payload.title: Our Model Temple Pond Project

payload.passage: On the rainy weekend, the cousins made hot vegetable fritters with their aunt. They dipped slices of potato and onion into a thick batter. Their aunt fried them carefully until they turned crisp and golden. Everyone gathered to eat the warm snack while the rain fell softly outside.
payload.title: Cousins make hot snacks on a rainy day
decoys: They dipped potato slices in batter.
The snacks turned crisp and golden.

payload.passage: Pranav buried a steel spoon, a wooden spoon and a plastic spoon in damp soil in the garden. He dug them up after a month to compare. The steel spoon had gone rusty, the wooden one had darkened and softened, and the plastic was unchanged. His teacher said different materials react in different ways. Pranav learned that materials change differently when buried in damp soil.
payload.title: Materials change differently when buried in soil
decoys: The steel spoon had gone rusty
Pranav buried three kinds of spoon

payload.passage: Simran saw the village pond turn into firm land over many years, with grass growing where water once stood. Her grandfather explained that leaves, mud and dead plants slowly sink to the bottom of a still pond. Year after year they pile up and fill it from below. At last there is no water left, only soft soil. Simran learned that a still pond can slowly turn into land.
payload.title: A still pond can slowly turn into land
decoys: Grass grew where water once stood
Ponds are home to many plants
Simran's village has an old pond

payload.passage: A drop of water can become rock-hard ice or thin invisible gas. When it gets very cold, water freezes into solid ice. When it is heated, it turns into vapour that floats away in the air. Cool that vapour and it becomes liquid water once again. So the same water can be a solid, a liquid, or a gas.
payload.title: Water can be solid, liquid, or gas
decoys: Heated water turns into floating vapour
Nature is full of clever changes
We use water for drinking and washing

payload.passage: A seed packet tells a gardener how to sow. The front shows a picture of the grown plant and its name. The back gives the depth to plant, the spacing between seeds and the best season. By following these notes, the gardener gives the seeds a good start. So a seed packet guides planting with pictures and written notes.
payload.title: How a seed packet guides a gardener's planting
decoys: The back lists the planting depth
The front shows the grown plant

payload.passage: A shopkeeper runs the small store where we buy our daily needs. He stocks his shelves with rice, soap, biscuits, and many other goods. When customers come, he helps them find what they want. He weighs the goods, takes the money, and gives back the change. So a shopkeeper's job is to sell us the things we need each day.
payload.title: How a shopkeeper serves the neighbourhood
decoys: He weighs the goods and gives back change
Shops stay open late in the evening

payload.passage: Sahil could never finish his big projects because he left them till the last day. The night before submission was always full of stress and tears. His teacher taught him to do a little of the project each day. Splitting the work into small parts made it easy to manage. Sahil now finishes projects early and hands them in calmly.
payload.title: Doing a little daily solved Sahil's last-minute stress
decoys: The night before was full of tears
Hard work always pays off in the end
Sahil split the project into small parts

payload.passage: A funnel helps you pour liquid into a narrow bottle without spills. It is wide and open at the top and narrows to a small spout below. When you pour liquid into the broad mouth, it is guided down the sloping sides. The narrow spout sends a thin steady stream into the bottle. So a funnel guides a wide pour into a narrow opening.
payload.title: How a funnel guides liquid into a bottle
decoys: The spout sends a thin steady stream
Liquids can be tricky to pour
A funnel is wide at the top

payload.passage: The Clean School team noticed the bins always overflowing with rubbish. There were too few of them and they were emptied too rarely. So the team added more bins around the school and set up a daily emptying round. With enough bins and regular pickup, the litter problem soon ended. The team learned that more bins and a regular pickup solve a litter problem.
payload.title: More bins and regular pickup solve litter

payload.passage: Riya's group set up a station to collect used batteries from everyone. They learned that batteries leak harmful stuff into the soil if thrown in the normal bin. A special centre takes the collected batteries away to be handled safely. The bin slowly filled up over the weeks. The group learned that old batteries must be collected and thrown away safely.
payload.title: Old batteries must be thrown away safely
decoys: Riya's group set up a station

payload.passage: A water tap controls the flow with a part that twists shut. Inside the tap sits a washer that can press down on the opening. When you turn the handle one way, the washer lifts and lets water gush through. Turning it the other way pushes the washer down to block the gap. So a tap lets water flow or stops it by raising or lowering a washer.
payload.title: How a tap starts and stops water flow
decoys: A washer presses down on the opening
Taps are found in every kitchen
Turning the handle moves the washer

payload.passage: On a cold morning, Sara saw mist hanging low over the river. Her mother explained that during the night the air cooled down, and the warm water vapour rising from the river turned into tiny drops floating just above the surface. As the sun warmed the air, the mist slowly faded. Sara learned that morning mist forms when warm vapour meets cool air.
payload.title: Morning mist forms when warm vapour cools
decoys: The mist hung low over the river
Mornings can be cool and pleasant
Sara watched the mist from her window

payload.passage: Aniket put a thermometer in a cup of water and read it before stirring in three spoons of salt. After the salt dissolved he read the thermometer again. The water had grown a little colder than before. His teacher said dissolving salt can pull warmth from the water. Aniket learned that dissolving salt can cool the water a little.
payload.title: Dissolving salt can cool the water a little
decoys: Aniket stirred in three spoons of salt

payload.passage: Pihu set out a saucer of water with a few drops of red colour and a dry flower beside it. She dipped the flower stem into the water and waited overnight. By morning the white petals had soft pink tips where the colour had reached. Her mother said the flower drank the dye up its stem. Pihu learned that a flower can drink coloured water up into its petals.
payload.title: A flower drinks coloured water into its petals
decoys: The petal tips turned soft pink

payload.passage: Madhu was amazed that a sandy desert could bloom with flowers after one rare shower. Her teacher explained that desert seeds can wait many months, even years, for water. They lie still in the dry sand until rain finally falls. Then they sprout, flower and make new seeds very fast before the soil dries again. Madhu learned that a desert blooms quickly after a rare rain.
payload.title: A desert blooms quickly after a rare rain

payload.passage: Asha noticed that the puddles after a storm dried up much faster on a windy day than on a still one. Her teacher explained that wind sweeps away the moist air just above the water, so fresh dry air keeps reaching it and pulling more water into vapour. The more wind, the faster water leaves. Asha learned that wind makes water dry up more quickly.
payload.title: Wind makes water dry up more quickly
decoys: The puddles dried after the storm
Wind can be gentle or strong

payload.passage: At the city museum, Sara stopped at a glass case full of old coins. The label said the oldest coins were just lumps of metal stamped with a simple mark. Over hundreds of years, coins grew rounder and showed kings, animals and tiny words. Sara understood that the row of coins was really a long story of how money slowly changed over time.
payload.title: Old coins show how money changed over time
decoys: The oldest coins were just lumps of stamped metal
Museums keep many interesting old objects safe
Sara liked the shine of the polished coins

payload.passage: Ananya wanted to know if worms help the soil, so she set up two jars of damp earth. She added a few earthworms to one jar and left the other with no worms. After a week the worm jar had loose, airy soil with little tunnels running through it. The other jar stayed packed and hard. Ananya learned that earthworms loosen and air out the soil as they move.
payload.title: Earthworms loosen and air out the soil
decoys: The worm jar had little tunnels in it
Soil is home to many tiny creatures
Ananya used two jars of damp earth

payload.passage: A zookeeper takes care of the animals living in the zoo. Each morning she feeds them the right food for their kind. She cleans their homes and makes sure they have fresh water. She watches them closely and calls the vet if one looks unwell. So a zookeeper's work is to keep the zoo animals healthy and happy.
payload.title: How a zookeeper cares for zoo animals
decoys: She cleans their homes and gives fresh water
Many helpers care for living things
Zoos let people see wild animals safely

payload.passage: Ira left a damp cloth folded on a plate in a warm dark cupboard. She checked it after a week with a torch and a careful sniff. The cloth had grown a musty smell and faint grey spots of mould. Her teacher said warmth and damp let mould grow on cloth too. Ira learned that damp cloth grows mould in a warm dark place.
payload.title: Damp cloth grows mould in warm darkness
decoys: The cloth grew faint grey spots
Cloth is used for many things
Ira checked it with a torch

payload.passage: The classroom door lock was stiff and often jammed shut. Children waited outside in the corridor till someone forced it open. The teacher reported it and a worker came to oil the lock. The lock turned smoothly and the door opened with one easy push. The class now started on time without any waiting outside.
payload.title: Oiling the lock solved the jammed classroom door
decoys: Children waited outside in the corridor
Small repairs keep a school running smoothly
A worker came to oil the stiff lock

payload.passage: At home, the family could never agree on what to cook for dinner. The daily debate left everyone tired and hungry. Mother made a weekly menu and pinned it up in the kitchen. Each day's meal was decided well in advance on the chart. The dinner-time debates ended and meals were ready on time.
payload.title: A weekly menu solved the dinner debates
decoys: The daily debate left everyone hungry
A planned meal keeps a family well fed
Mother pinned a weekly menu in the kitchen

payload.passage: Ahaana stretched cling film tightly over a bowl of warm water and set a small stone in the centre of the film. She left the bowl in the sun for a few hours. Clear drops gathered under the film and ran down to drip below the stone into a cup. Her teacher said the warm water rose and dripped down clean. Ahaana learned that covered warm water can collect as clean drops.
payload.title: Covered warm water collects as clean drops
decoys: Drops gathered under the cling film
Ahaana set a stone on the film

payload.passage: A drip irrigation pipe waters plants slowly and evenly. A long pipe with tiny holes lies along a row of plants. Water flows gently through the pipe and seeps out drop by drop at each hole. Every plant gets a small steady supply right at its roots. So a drip pipe waters a whole row slowly through many tiny holes.
payload.title: How a drip pipe waters plants drop by drop
decoys: Water seeps out at each hole
The pipe lies along the row

payload.passage: A fisherman brings fresh fish from the sea to our markets. Before dawn he sets out in his boat onto the open water. He casts his nets and waits patiently for the fish to gather. He hauls in his catch and rows back to sell it on the shore. So a fisherman's work is to catch the fish that feed many people.
payload.title: How a fisherman brings fish to market
decoys: He casts his nets and waits for the fish
Many helpers work to feed us
Fish is full of goodness for the body

payload.passage: Vihaan wanted to learn how to throw a ball overarm like the bowlers. His throws went sideways and never reached his friend properly. His coach taught him to step forward and swing his arm right over. The ball began to fly straight and far towards the target. Soon Vihaan could throw all the way across the cricket ground.
payload.title: Swinging his arm over taught Vihaan to throw far
decoys: Cricket bowlers are admired all over the country
Vihaan threw across the cricket ground

payload.passage: A nail clipper trims a nail with two small sharp jaws. When you press the lever at the top, it pushes the jaws together. The two edges meet and snip cleanly through the hard nail. A spring inside opens the jaws again when you let go. So a nail clipper cuts a nail by pressing two sharp edges together.
payload.title: How a nail clipper snips a nail
decoys: A spring opens the jaws again
A lever sits at the top

The coloured warm water slowly drifted upward and gathered at the top. His teacher said warm water is lighter and floats up. Rohit learned that warm water rises above colder water.
payload.title: Warm water rises above colder water
decoys: The coloured warm water drifted upward
Rohit used a straw to pour it

payload.passage: Pranav wanted to learn how to dive neatly into the swimming pool. His early dives turned into loud, painful belly flops. His coach taught him to point his arms and tuck his head down. Slowly his dives grew smooth and made only a small splash. By the gala Pranav dived cleanly and earned a clap from the crowd.
payload.title: Tucking his head taught Pranav to dive cleanly
decoys: Pranav's early dives were painful belly flops
Swimming galas always draw a big, happy crowd
Pranav's coach taught him a useful tip

payload.passage: A field of rice changes its colour as the season goes on. When the seedlings are first planted, the whole field looks fresh green. As the plants grow tall, the green deepens and the field sways in the wind. When the grain ripens, the field slowly turns a soft golden yellow. So a rice field shifts from green to gold as it ripens.
payload.title: A rice field turns from green to gold
decoys: The field is fresh green when first planted
Crops change a great deal as they grow
Rice is the main food in many homes

payload.passage: Myra kept smudging her homework because she wrote with her hand over the ink. The wet ink streaked across the page as her hand moved. Her teacher showed her to rest her hand below the line she was writing. The ink dried before her hand reached it after that. Myra's homework stayed clean and neat from then on.
payload.title: Resting her hand below solved Myra's smudged work
decoys: Wet ink streaked across the page
Neat work always earns a teacher's praise
Her teacher showed her where to rest her hand

payload.passage: Aaradhya stood a glass of water in the freezer and checked it every hour. First the surface turned to a thin skin of ice, then the ice grew downwards and inwards. After several hours the whole glass had become a solid block. Her father said freezing starts at the top and works down. Aaradhya learned that water freezes from the surface downwards.
payload.title: Water freezes from the surface downwards
decoys: A thin skin of ice formed first
Aaradhya checked the glass every hour

payload.passage: Asha wished to fold paper into a neat crane like the one in her book. Her first cranes were lopsided and the wings refused to open. She watched the steps over and over and folded each crease slowly. With each new try her cranes grew tidier and their wings spread wide. Soon a row of paper cranes stood proudly on her study table.
payload.title: Careful folding taught Asha to make paper cranes
decoys: Asha's first cranes had wings that would not open
Paper crafts can decorate any room beautifully
Asha learned the crane from a folding book

payload.passage: A tuning fork hums one clear note when tapped. It is a metal fork with two long prongs joined at a handle. When you strike it, the prongs shake quickly back and forth. This steady shaking pushes the air and makes a pure single tone. So a tuning fork sounds a clear note by its prongs shaking the air.
payload.title: How a tuning fork hums by shaking the air
decoys: Two long prongs join at a handle

payload.passage: Aaisha set out a tray of soil and pressed seeds into rows, then covered half the tray with a clear plastic sheet. She kept both halves in the same light and watered the open half only. The covered half stayed damp and sprouted first, since the plastic trapped the moisture. Aaisha learned that a clear cover keeps soil damp and helps seeds sprout sooner.
payload.title: A clear cover keeps soil damp for seeds

payload.passage: Pia poured a thick layer of honey into a tall glass, then added water and finally a little oil. She let everything settle for a few minutes without stirring. The liquids did not mix but formed three neat layers, with honey at the bottom and oil on top. Her father said heavier liquids sink below lighter ones. Pia learned that liquids stack in layers by how heavy they are.
payload.title: Liquids stack in layers by their heaviness
decoys: Honey settled at the bottom of the glass
Liquids can be poured and mixed
Pia used honey, water and oil

payload.passage: The students collected old wooden crates and planks from the market nearby. The wood would otherwise have been thrown away as useless junk. They cleaned the pieces and joined them together carefully. From them they built sturdy benches and a low stage for the school garden. The students learned that scrap wood can be built into useful furniture.
payload.title: Scrap wood can be built into useful furniture
decoys: The crates came from the market
Wood is used to make many things

payload.passage: A street musician brings music to the people passing by. He sits at a busy corner with his instrument. He plays cheerful tunes that make people stop and smile. Some listeners drop a few coins to thank him for the music. So a street musician's work is to share music with the neighbourhood.
payload.title: How a street musician shares his music
decoys: He plays cheerful tunes for passers-by
Many people add joy to our streets
Music can lift a tired heart

payload.passage: The school stationery shop used to hand out a plastic bag with each purchase. Tara's group wanted to stop this waste. So they asked every class to bring a cloth or jute bag instead. The shop kept the cloth bags ready and soon stopped giving plastic. The group learned that bringing your own bag ends the need for plastic ones.
payload.title: Bringing your own bag ends plastic ones
decoys: The shop kept cloth bags ready

payload.passage: Charvi stood a celery stalk in red water and another in blue water for a day. When she cut them across, she saw tiny red and blue dots in rings inside each stalk. Her teacher said those dots were the tubes that carried the coloured water up. Charvi learned that a stem has tiny tubes that carry water upward.
payload.title: A stem has tiny tubes that carry water up
decoys: She saw red and blue dots inside

payload.passage: Krishiv counted how many times a cricket chirped in fifteen seconds on a warm evening. A few nights later, on a cool evening, he sat and counted the chirps in the very same way. On the warm night the chirps came much faster than on the cool one. His teacher said insects move quicker when the air is warm. Krishiv learned that crickets chirp faster when the air is warmer.
payload.title: Crickets chirp faster when the air is warmer
decoys: Krishiv counted chirps in fifteen seconds
The cool night had slower chirps

payload.passage: A vegetable market worker keeps the busy market running smoothly. Before dawn he helps unload crates of fresh vegetables from the trucks. He sets them out so sellers and buyers can see them clearly. He keeps the floor clean as the crowd buys through the morning. So a market worker's job is to help the market run well each day.
payload.title: How a market worker keeps the market running
decoys: He helps unload crates from the trucks
Markets are busiest in the early morning

payload.passage: Naira left a peeled boiled egg on the wide mouth of a bottle that was a touch too small. She dropped a lit paper inside the bottle and the flame soon went out. As the air cooled, the egg was sucked slowly into the bottle. Her teacher said cooling air pulled it in. Naira learned that cooling air can pull an egg into a bottle.
payload.title: Cooling air can pull an egg into a bottle
decoys: The flame inside soon went out

payload.passage: The students often forgot which day to bring their library books back. Late returns piled up and the librarian was unhappy. A return-day stamp was put inside every book that was borrowed. Children checked the stamp and brought their books on time. Late returns dropped sharply and the librarian was pleased.
payload.title: A return stamp solved the late library books
decoys: Late returns piled up for the librarian
A good library helps children love reading
A return-day stamp went inside each book

payload.passage: The colony placed a stone water trough in the shade by the gate. They kept it filled for the stray cows and dogs of the lane. This mattered most in the hot, dry summer. The thirsty animals came to drink, and fewer fell sick from the heat. The colony learned that a shared water trough helps street animals in summer.
payload.title: A shared water trough helps street animals
decoys: The trough stands in the shade

payload.passage: Faizan filled a glass to the very top with cold water and slid it carefully onto a saucer. As the water slowly warmed in the room, a little spilled over the edge onto the saucer. His father said warm water spreads out and takes more room than cold. Faizan learned that water grows a little bigger as it warms up.
payload.title: Water grows a little bigger as it warms
decoys: A little water spilled onto the saucer
Water can be warm or cold
Faizan filled the glass to the top

payload.passage: A escapement in a wind-up watch lets it tick steadily. A coiled spring wants to unwind all at once, but a little toothed wheel and lever hold it back. The lever lets the wheel slip forward just one tooth at a time. Each tiny slip gives the familiar tick and moves the hands a step. So an escapement lets a watch unwind one steady tick at a time.
payload.title: How an escapement lets a watch tick steadily
decoys: A coiled spring wants to unwind
Watches are worn on the wrist
The wheel slips one tooth at a time

payload.passage: A pine cone opens and closes with the weather to spread its seeds. Its woody scales are packed tightly when the air is damp. When the day turns warm and dry, the scales slowly open out. The light seeds inside then drift away on the dry breeze. So a pine cone waits for dry weather to scatter its seeds.
payload.title: How a pine cone spreads its seeds
decoys: The scales open out in warm dry weather
Plants spread their seeds in clever ways
Squirrels nibble seeds out of pine cones

payload.passage: Tina's building started keeping two bins instead of one: a green bin for wet kitchen waste and a blue bin for dry paper, glass and plastic. Sorting the rubbish this way means the dry waste can be recycled and the wet waste made into compost. Much less goes to the dump now. The building learned that sorting waste lets more of it be reused.
payload.title: Sorting waste lets more of it be reused
decoys: The green bin holds wet kitchen waste
Buildings make a lot of rubbish

payload.passage: A vacuum flask keeps a drink hot for hours. It has two walls with an empty gap between them. Heat finds it very hard to cross that empty gap, so it stays trapped inside. A tight stopper keeps the warm air from escaping at the top. So a vacuum flask holds heat in by surrounding the drink with an empty gap.
payload.title: How an empty gap keeps a flask drink hot
decoys: A tight stopper seals the top
It has two walls with a gap

payload.passage: Tarun watched dark clouds gather, then heard a great rush of wind before the rain hit. His uncle explained that as a storm cloud grows, cool air sinks fast inside it and spills out along the ground ahead of the rain, which is the sudden gust we feel. It is a warning the storm is near. Tarun learned that a sudden wind warns that a storm is coming.
payload.title: A sudden wind warns a storm is coming
decoys: Tarun felt the gust on his face

payload.passage: A pine tree stays green even through the coldest winter. Instead of broad flat leaves, it grows thin, needle-like leaves. These needles have a waxy coat that keeps water from drying out. Because it does not lose its leaves, the pine looks green all year. So a pine tree is built to stay green in any season.
payload.title: Why a pine tree stays green all year
decoys: Pine needles have a waxy outer coat
Trees come in many shapes and kinds
Pine wood is used to make furniture

payload.passage: A school van helper keeps order among the children on the trip. She helps the small ones with their heavy school bags. She makes sure no child puts a hand out of the window. She counts the children at each stop so none is left behind. So a van helper's work is to keep the children safe and settled.
payload.title: How a van helper looks after the children
decoys: She counts the children at each stop
Children must wear their seat belts

payload.passage: A shadow puppet show throws figures on a sheet. A lamp shines from behind onto a stretched white cloth. A puppet held between the lamp and cloth blocks the light. Its dark shape falls on the cloth for the watchers in front to see. So a shadow show works by a puppet blocking light onto a lit sheet.
payload.title: How a puppet blocks light for a shadow show
decoys: Stories can be told with puppets
The puppet's shape falls on the cloth

payload.passage: Sara wished to play a tune on the tabletop drums her uncle gifted her. Her beats were uneven and the rhythm kept falling apart. She tapped along with songs on the radio every afternoon. Her hands slowly learned to keep a steady, even beat. Soon Sara could drum a clear rhythm while her cousins danced around her.
payload.title: Tapping along to songs taught Sara to drum
decoys: Sara's early beats were very uneven
Music brings every family closer together
Sara's uncle gifted her some tabletop drums

payload.passage: Om wanted to learn how to draw a straight line without using a ruler. His freehand lines always curved and wobbled across the page. He practised drawing long lines quickly from one dot to another. His hand slowly grew steadier and the lines turned straighter. By the end Om could sketch neat boxes and roads without any ruler.
payload.title: Daily line drawing steadied Om's freehand
decoys: Drawing is something every artist must master
Om could sketch boxes and roads at last

payload.passage: A house painter brings fresh colour to our walls. First he covers the floor and cleans the dusty wall. He fills any cracks and lets the surface dry well. Then he brushes or rolls on smooth, bright paint, coat by coat. So a painter's work is to make our walls clean and colourful.
payload.title: How a painter brightens our walls
decoys: He fills the cracks before painting
Bright walls make a room feel cheerful

payload.passage: Manav watched a sparrow take a dust bath in the dry garden soil. The bird fluffed up and rolled, throwing dust through its feathers. After a while it shook itself clean and flew off looking neat. His grandfather said the dust helps clean pests from the feathers. Manav learned that some birds use dust baths to clean their feathers.
payload.title: Some birds use dust baths to clean feathers
decoys: The sparrow fluffed up and rolled

payload.passage: After a long dry spell, the first monsoon shower changes everything. The dusty ground sends up a fresh earthy smell that people love. Brown grass turns green almost overnight as the rain soaks in. Frogs begin to croak, and small plants spring up where there was only dust. So the first rain brings the dry land suddenly back to life.
payload.title: The first rain wakes the dry land
decoys: Frogs begin to croak after the first rain
Rain is important for all living things
Farmers wait eagerly for the monsoon

payload.passage: The school corridor was dark and a few children stumbled in it. The single dim bulb could not light the long passage. The office had two bright tube lights fixed along the corridor. The passage lit up and the stumbling stopped at once. Children now walked through safely even on cloudy days.
payload.title: Brighter lights solved the dark corridor problem
decoys: A few children stumbled in the dark
Good lighting is needed in every public place
The office fixed two bright tube lights

payload.passage: Rohan wanted to grow salt crystals, so he stirred spoon after spoon of salt into warm water until no more would dissolve. He dipped a thread into the cup and tied the other end to a pencil across the top. Over several days the water slowly dried up and left tiny shining cubes clinging to the thread. His mother said the salt had come back as solid crystals. Rohan learned that drying salty water grows neat crystals.
payload.title: Drying salty water grows shiny salt crystals
decoys: Rohan tied the thread to a pencil
Science experiments can be done at home
Salt makes food taste better in cooking

payload.passage: Pranav saw the calm pond suddenly fill with ripples when the wind picked up. His teacher explained that wind pushes against the water surface, and where it pushes hardest it lifts little ridges of water that travel along as waves. The stronger the wind, the bigger the waves grow. Pranav learned that wind blowing over water makes waves.
payload.title: Wind blowing over water makes waves

payload.passage: Saanvi found that her favourite books got their corners bent and torn. Tossing them into her bag damaged them every day. She wrapped each book in a sturdy plastic cover at home. The covers kept the pages and corners safe inside her bag. Saanvi's books stayed neat and lasted much longer after that.
payload.title: Book covers solved Saanvi's damaged books
decoys: The book corners got bent and torn
Caring for books is a good habit for all
Saanvi wrapped her books in plastic

payload.passage: A water board worker makes sure clean water reaches our taps. He checks the big pipes that carry water under the streets. He looks for leaks and repairs any pipe that is broken. He also tests the water to be sure it is safe to drink. So a water board worker's job is to give homes clean, safe water.
payload.title: How a water board worker supplies clean water
decoys: He tests the water to keep it safe
Clean water keeps a family healthy

payload.passage: At home, the family kept losing the small scissors whenever they were needed. Someone always left them in a different room each time. Mother tied the scissors to a hook in the kitchen with a string. The scissors always hung in their place after every use. The frustrating searches for scissors ended completely.
payload.title: Tying the scissors down solved the search problem
decoys: Someone left the scissors in another room
A neat home saves a family lots of time
Mother tied the scissors with a string

payload.passage: Mansi's room got too cold near the window during the winter nights. She shivered under her blanket and could not sleep well. Her father stuck a thick foam strip along the gap in the window. The cold draught stopped seeping in through the gap. Mansi slept warm and woke up fresh for school every morning.
payload.title: Sealing the gap solved Mansi's cold room
decoys: Winter brings discomfort to many homes
Her father stuck foam along the window

payload.passage: Aadhya wanted to see how birds find worms, so she sat quietly near a wet patch of garden after the rain. A myna landed and cocked its head, listening to the soft ground. Suddenly it stabbed its beak down and pulled out a wriggling worm. Aadhya noticed it did this only on the damp soil, never on the dry path. She learned that birds hunt worms in soft, wet ground after rain.
payload.title: Birds hunt worms in wet ground after rain
decoys: The myna cocked its head to listen
Birds are interesting creatures to watch
Worms wriggle when they are pulled out

payload.passage: Reyaan set a small dish of honey beside a dish of plain water in the garden. He waited and watched which one the ants preferred. A busy line of ants soon crowded the honey while the water stayed almost empty. His teacher said ants seek sweet, energy-rich food. Reyaan learned that ants are drawn to sweet honey over plain water.
payload.title: Ants are drawn to honey over plain water
decoys: A line of ants crowded the honey
Reyaan set out two small dishes

payload.passage: Sanjay wanted to learn how to make a fluffy omelette for breakfast. His first omelettes came out flat, dry, and a little burnt. He learned to whisk the eggs well and cook them on a low flame. The omelettes slowly turned soft, golden, and fluffy. Sanjay proudly served warm omelettes to his parents on Sunday morning.
payload.title: Low-flame cooking taught Sanjay to make a fluffy omelette
decoys: Sanjay's first omelettes came out flat
A good breakfast keeps the whole family healthy
Sanjay served omelettes on Sunday morning

payload.passage: The school garden plants kept dying because no one remembered to water them. The leaves drooped and the flowers withered in the sun. The teacher made a weekly chart so each group watered on its own day. With regular watering the plants stood up green and healthy. Soon the garden was full of bright, blooming flowers again.
payload.title: A watering chart saved the dying garden
decoys: The leaves drooped and flowers withered
Plants make any school look beautiful
The teacher made a weekly watering chart

payload.passage: Harsh half-filled two identical bottles with water and left the caps off. He set one in a warm sunny window and one in a cool dark shelf. After three days the sunny bottle had clearly lost more water than the shaded one. His teacher said warmth speeds up drying. Harsh learned that warm air dries out water faster than cool air.
payload.title: Warm air dries out water faster than cool
decoys: The sunny bottle lost more water

payload.passage: A street sweeper keeps the roads and footpaths clean each day. Early in the morning he walks along with his long broom. He sweeps up dust, leaves, and litter into neat little piles. He then gathers these piles and clears them away. So a street sweeper's work keeps our roads clean and tidy.
payload.title: How a street sweeper keeps roads clean
decoys: He sweeps litter into neat little piles
Many helpers keep our area clean
Litter should be put in the right bin

payload.passage: Tarun wanted to learn how to do a long jump in the sand pit. His early jumps were short and he often landed flat on his face. His coach taught him to run fast and push off hard with one foot. His jumps grew longer as his run and his push got stronger. On sports day Tarun leapt the farthest and won a bright blue ribbon.
payload.title: A strong run-up improved Tarun's long jump
decoys: Tarun's early jumps were very short
Sports day is the most exciting school event
Tarun won a bright blue ribbon

payload.passage: Kiara wanted to know if sound travels through string. She poked a hole in two paper cups and joined them with a long, tight thread. Her friend spoke softly into one cup while Kiara pressed the other to her ear. She could hear the words clearly through the stretched string. Kiara learned that sound can travel along a tight string from one cup to another.
payload.title: Sound travels along a tight string
decoys: Kiara joined two paper cups with thread
Talking is how people share their ideas
Cups can be made from paper or plastic

payload.passage: A cable worker brings television channels into our homes. He runs the cables along the poles down our street. He connects each home's wire to the main line. When a picture goes fuzzy, he comes to fix the link. So a cable worker's job is to keep our television working well.
payload.title: How a cable worker connects our homes
decoys: He connects each home's wire to the line
Television brings us news and shows

payload.passage: At the museum, Myra entered a room of old lamps, from clay dishes with cotton wicks to glass lanterns. The guide showed how each new lamp gave brighter, safer light than the one before. Before electricity, she said, people depended on these lamps to work and read after dark. Myra learned that the room showed how people slowly found better ways to light the night.
payload.title: Old lamps show better ways to light the night
decoys: An early lamp was a clay dish with a wick
Light is important in every home
Myra liked the colours of the glass lantern

payload.passage: A clean-up volunteer helps tidy the neighbourhood on weekends. With a group of friends she picks up litter from the lanes. They sweep the footpaths and clear the choked corners. They plant a few saplings to add some green to the street. So a clean-up volunteer's work is to keep the neighbourhood clean and green.
payload.title: How a volunteer keeps the neighbourhood clean
decoys: They plant a few saplings on the street
Many people help improve our area
Litter spoils the look of a street

payload.passage: A hand-crank radio plays without any wall plug. Turning the crank spins a tiny generator that makes power. That power is stored in a small cell inside the radio. The stored power then runs the radio so you can hear it play. So a wind-up radio works by turning a crank to make and store its own power.
payload.title: How a crank makes power for a radio
decoys: Power is stored in a small cell
Radios bring us news and music
Turning the crank spins a generator

payload.passage: A banana plant gives only one big bunch and then makes way for the next. It grows fast from an underground stem into a tall leafy plant. After it flowers, a single heavy bunch of bananas grows out. Once that bunch is cut, the old plant dies down. But a new shoot is already growing from the same root to take its place.
payload.title: How a banana plant gives fruit and renews
decoys: The old banana plant dies after fruiting
Plants grow and renew in many ways
Ripe bananas are sweet and soft to eat

payload.passage: A single drop of water travels in a never-ending circle. The sun heats water in seas and lakes until it rises as invisible vapour. High in the sky it cools and gathers into clouds. When the clouds grow heavy, the water falls back as rain or snow. This same water then flows to the sea and the journey begins again.
payload.title: Water travels in a never-ending circle
decoys: The sun heats water until it rises as vapour
Nature is full of repeating patterns
We need clean water every single day

payload.passage: Aman kept forgetting his homework books at home almost every day. His teacher was unhappy and his marks slowly began to drop. One evening his mother helped him make a small checklist for his bag. Every night he ticked off each book before zipping the bag shut. After that Aman never forgot a single book and his marks climbed back up.
payload.title: A nightly checklist solved Aman's forgotten books
decoys: Aman's marks slowly began to drop
Good habits can fix every problem a child has
Aman's mother helped him one evening

payload.passage: At home, Om's family kept misplacing the television remote every night. Hunting for it under cushions wasted everyone's evening. Father stuck a small holder on the side of the sofa for the remote. The remote always went back into its holder after use. The nightly hunts ended and the evenings stayed relaxed.
payload.title: A remote holder solved the misplaced-remote hunts
decoys: Hunting under cushions wasted the evening
A small habit can ease many daily annoyances
Father stuck a holder on the sofa

payload.passage: The Green Club asked families to rethink how they wrap their gifts. Shiny new wrapping paper is used just once and then thrown straight away. So they suggested using old newspaper and spare bits of cloth instead. The wrapping still looked lovely and made no waste at all. The club learned that reusing paper and cloth for wrapping cuts waste.
payload.title: Reusing paper and cloth for wrapping cuts waste
decoys: Gifts are wrapped in old newspaper
Gifts are given on happy days
The Green Club made the suggestion

payload.passage: Reyaan held a magnifying glass between the bright sun and a scrap of dark paper on the ground, well away from anything else. He moved it until the sunlight gathered into one tiny bright dot. The dot grew hot and made a thin curl of smoke rise. His teacher said the lens bunched the sun's heat into one spot. Reyaan learned that a lens can gather sunlight into a hot point.
payload.title: A lens can gather sunlight into a hot point
decoys: A thin curl of smoke rose
The sun gives heat and light

payload.passage: Ekansh laid a sheet of paper over a coin and rubbed across it with the side of a pencil. Slowly the pattern of the coin appeared on the paper as a clear picture. He tried it on a leaf and got its veins too. His teacher said rubbing copies the raised pattern underneath. Ekansh learned that pencil rubbing copies the pattern of what lies beneath.
payload.title: Pencil rubbing copies a hidden pattern
decoys: The coin's pattern appeared on the paper
Ekansh rubbed over a leaf too

payload.passage: Jai set a black sheet and a white sheet on the warm grass and laid a thin square of butter on each one. He left both in the bright afternoon sun and timed them carefully. The butter on the black sheet melted into a puddle long before the one on the white sheet. His teacher said black soaks up heat while white throws it back. Jai learned that butter melts faster on a black surface.
payload.title: Butter melts faster on a black surface
decoys: Kabir timed both squares of butter
He used a black and a white sheet

payload.passage: Laksh wanted to learn how to play a tune on water-filled glasses. His first notes were all the same, dull, and tuneless. He poured different amounts of water until each glass sang a new note. Tapping them in order, he found the notes of a real song. Laksh played a little melody on his glasses for the science fair.
payload.title: Adjusting the water taught Laksh the glass melody
decoys: Laksh's first notes were dull and the same
Science fairs are exciting for every student
Laksh played his melody at the science fair

payload.passage: Mehul lined up a row of dominoes on the floor, each standing close to the next. He gave the first one a gentle push with his finger. It fell against the second, which knocked the third, and so the fall ran all the way down the line. His teacher said each tile passes its push to the next. Mehul learned that a falling domino passes its push along a whole row.
payload.title: A falling domino passes its push along the row
decoys: Mehul pushed the first domino gently
Dominoes are fun to set up
The first tile fell against the second

payload.passage: Lavanya noticed snails come out only after it rains. To check, she watched the garden wall on a dry day and saw none. After a rainy evening many snails crept slowly along the same wall, leaving shiny trails. Her mother said snails need damp air or their soft bodies dry out. Lavanya learned that snails come out when the air is damp.
payload.title: Snails come out when the air is damp
decoys: The snails left shiny trails on the wall
Rain changes how a garden looks
Snails move very slowly along walls

payload.passage: A meter reader checks how much electricity each home has used. He visits each house carrying his notebook. He reads the numbers shown on the electricity meter on the wall. He writes them down so the right bill can be prepared. So a meter reader's job is to record the power each home uses.
payload.title: How a meter reader records power use
decoys: He reads the numbers on the meter
We should switch off unused lights

payload.passage: A coconut palm gives useful gifts at every stage of its life. Its sweet water and soft flesh make a healthy food and drink. Its tough leaves are woven into mats, brooms, and roofs. Even its hard shell and husk are used for ropes and bowls. So nearly every part of a coconut palm is put to good use.
payload.title: Every part of a coconut palm is useful
decoys: Coconut leaves are woven into mats and brooms
Plants give us many helpful things
Coconut water is a refreshing summer drink

payload.passage: Tanvi's class learned that strong washing powders and soaps can harm the fish in rivers. They decided to spread the word in their lane. They asked families to use gentle, plant-based cleaners instead. They also asked them to pour soapy water on the garden, not into the drain. The class learned that gentle cleaners help keep rivers safe for fish.
payload.title: Gentle cleaners keep rivers safe for fish
decoys: Soapy water can be poured on the garden
Rivers are home to many fish

payload.passage: At the museum, Sneha found a room of old measuring tools: weights, rods and balance scales.
